title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄕試錄序
聖皇帝文涵武蕩海徼內外戎夷
咸知向學矧嶺以南乃寰宇
中州歲丁酉廣東如期舉試
維時巡按監察御史余光恭
先厥事曁提調官左布政使
陸杰左參議余Rp監試官按
===
察使蔣淦副使鄒守愚與先
巡按監察御史陳大用以禮
聘考試官學正王本才訓導
郭愷同考試官學正黃仲陽
教諭蔣孟倫林人紀陳玉郝
光潤王蘭矢心入院恪供乃
務維時右布政使柴經左參
punctuated:
廣東鄕試錄序

聖皇帝文涵武蕩，海徼內外戎夷咸知向學，矧嶺以南，乃寰宇中州。歲丁酉，廣東如期舉試。維時巡按監察御史余光恭先厥事，曁提調官左布政使陸杰、左參議余Rp、監試官按察使蔣淦、副使鄒守愚，與先巡按監察御史陳大用，以禮聘考試官學正王本才、訓導郭愷，同考試官學正黃仲陽、教諭蔣孟倫、林人紀、陳玉、郝光潤、王蘭，矢心入院，恪供乃務。維時右布政使柴經、左參
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

The sage Emperor’s civil virtue embraces all, and his martial might extends far and wide. Even the non-Chinese peoples within and beyond the maritime frontiers know to turn toward learning; how much more so the lands south of the mountain ranges, which form a central region of the realm. In the dingyou year [1537], Guangdong held its examination at the appointed time. The Regional Inspecting Censor, Yu Guang, respectfully took the lead in preparing for this undertaking. Together with the Proctors, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Lu Jie and Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Yu Rp [?], the Examination Monitors, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Jiang Gan and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zou Shouyu, and the former Regional Inspecting Censor Chen Dayong, he ceremoniously invited Instructor Wang Bencai and Assistant Instructor Guo Kai to serve as Examiners; and Instructor Huang Zhongyang and Instructors Jiang Menglun, Lin Renji, Chen Yu, Hao Guangrun, and Wang Lan to serve as Associate Examiners. With resolute dedication, they entered the examination compound and conscientiously discharged their duties. At this time, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Chai Jing and the Left …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
政詹瀚右參政朱珮右參議
盧蕙副使顧可久葉照僉事
吳玭江匯朱道瀾周相李默
相與畫謨作範殫思獻藝維
時提督兩廣軍務兼理巡撫
兵部左侍郎兼右副都御史
潘旦提督南贛汀漳等處軍
===
務右副都御史王浚昭謀備
典總兵安遠侯柳珣協寅觀
成禮科右給事中沈伯咸湖
廣道監察御史毛復恤刑郎
中鄭朝輔咸諮度定規都指
揮潘瑛張輗李讓咸賛翼防
範合提學僉事吳鵬所選士
punctuated: 政詹瀚、右參政朱珮、右參議盧蕙、副使顧可久、葉照、僉事吳玭、江匯、朱道瀾、周相、李默，相與畫謨作範，殫思獻藝。維時，提督兩廣軍務兼理巡撫、兵部左侍郎兼右副都御史潘旦，提督南贛汀漳等處軍務、右副都御史王浚，昭謀備典；總兵安遠侯柳珣，協寅觀成；禮科右給事中沈伯咸、湖廣道監察御史毛復、恤刑郎中鄭朝輔，咸諮度定規；都指揮潘瑛、張輗、李讓，咸賛翼防範。合提學僉事吳鵬所選士
translation_en: …Left Administration Vice Commissioner Zhan Han, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhu Pei, Administration Assistant Commissioner of the Right Lu Hui, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Gu Kejiu and Ye Zhao, and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Wu Pin, Jiang Hui, Zhu Daolan, Zhou Xiang, and Li Mo jointly devised plans and established procedures, exhausting their thought and contributing their expertise. At this time, Pan Dan, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Guangdong and Guangxi, concurrently serving as Grand Coordinator, Left Vice Minister of War, and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Wang Jun, Supreme Commander of Military Affairs in Nan’an, Ganzhou, Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and other places and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, clarified the plans and made full provision for the prescribed ceremonies. Liu Xun, Commander-in-Chief and Marquis of Anyuan, cooperated respectfully and witnessed the successful completion. Shen Boxian, Supervising Secretary of the Right in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites; Mao Fu, Investigating Censor for the Huguang Circuit; and Zheng Chaofu, Bureau Director charged with reviewing penal cases, all consulted and deliberated to establish the rules. Regional Military Commissioners Pan Ying, Zhang Ni, and Li Rang all assisted with security precautions. The total number of candidates selected by Wu Peng, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner for Education, …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
一千九百有奇錄其中式者
七十五人旣竣事本才當叙
諸首曰夫原道立灋綿絡天
地以灋守道範圍古今
國家制灋秉公萬世不磨者科
目其一也我
太祖高皇帝開國統天開科延士
===
肇於洪武三年定於洪武十
七年中乃止者一十四載竭
智力以旁搜厭巧者之暗移
歷試罔效乃更繹思故制爲
科式歸於正途俾豪傑向風
哲人有守是百世王典通乎
天地者也大之公孤論道次
punctuated: 一千九百有奇，錄其中式者七十五人。旣竣事，本才當叙諸首，曰：夫原道立灋，綿絡天地；以灋守道，範圍古今。國家制灋秉公，萬世不磨者，科目其一也。我太祖高皇帝開國統天，開科延士，肇於洪武三年，定於洪武十七年，中乃止者一十四載。竭智力以旁搜，厭巧者之暗移，歷試罔效，乃更繹思，故制爲科式，歸於正途，俾豪傑向風，哲人有守。是百世王典，通乎天地者也。大之公孤論道，次
translation_en:
…numbering more than 1,900, of whom seventy-five were recorded as successful candidates. Once the proceedings were concluded, I, Bencai, was charged with composing a preface to head the record, as follows:

To establish regulations by tracing their source to the Way is to bind together Heaven and Earth; to preserve the Way through regulations is to encompass past and present. Among the impartial institutions established by the dynasty to endure undiminished for all ages, the examination system is one. Our Emperor Taizu Gao founded the dynasty under Heaven’s mandate and instituted examinations to attract worthy men. These began in the third year of Hongwu and were definitively established in the seventeenth year of Hongwu; in between, they were suspended for fourteen years. He exhausted his wisdom and strength in searching widely for talent and abhorred covert manipulation by the cunning. After successive trials proved ineffective, he reconsidered the matter in depth. Thus he established the examination regulations, returning recruitment to its proper course, so that outstanding men would respond to his influence and wise men would have standards to uphold. These are royal institutions for a hundred generations, consonant with Heaven and Earth. At the highest level, the Three Dukes and Three Solitaries deliberate on the Way; next …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之九卿分理中之邦伯司牧
外之將帥分閫文武幷效纖
洪畢陳洋洋乎聖謨帝懿彬
彬乎鳳翥麟遊猗歟盛哉或
曰雄論無稽彌文不實言寓
莊周談空鄒衍以科取人無
乃摭華棄腴予應之曰官先
===
事士先志志以論士言以發
志典曰敷奏以言非乎世非
洪龐人非淳古是故求賢良
則深情進矣求隱逸則僞遜
至矣求多途則私門啓矣是
廣虛名而蔽實德乃覬進者
之要津也况非豪傑所樂趨
punctuated:
之九卿分理，中之邦伯司牧，外之將帥分閫，文武幷效，纖洪畢陳。洋洋乎聖謨帝懿，彬彬乎鳳翥麟遊，猗歟盛哉！
或曰：「雄論無稽，彌文不實，言寓莊周，談空鄒衍，以科取人，無乃摭華棄腴？」
予應之曰：「官先事，士先志，志以論士，言以發志。典曰：『敷奏以言。』非乎？世非洪龐，人非淳古。是故求賢良，則深情進矣；求隱逸，則僞遜至矣；求多途，則私門啓矣。是廣虛名而蔽實德，乃覬進者之要津也。况非豪傑所樂趨
translation_en:
…next, the Nine Ministers divide administrative responsibilities; at the intermediate level, regional governors shepherd the people; beyond them, generals exercise command in their allotted territories. Civil and military officials alike render service, and talents great and small are all brought forth. How expansive are the sage plans and imperial virtues! How splendid, like phoenixes soaring and qilin roaming! Ah, how glorious!
Someone says: “Grand arguments lack substantiation; elaborate writing lacks substance. Their words are allegories like Zhuang Zhou’s, their discussions empty speculation like Zou Yan’s. In selecting men through examinations, are we not gathering blossoms and discarding the rich substance?”
I reply: “For office, duties come first; for a scholar, aspiration comes first. Aspiration is the basis for judging a scholar, and words express aspiration. Does not the Canon say, ‘Have them present their statements in words’? Our age is no longer one of primordial simplicity, nor are people as guileless as in antiquity. Thus, seek the worthy and good, and men with concealed motives advance; seek recluses, and men feigning modest withdrawal arrive; seek candidates through many channels, and doors to private patronage open. This spreads empty reputations while obscuring genuine virtue: it becomes the principal route for those coveting advancement. Moreover, is it not a course that outstanding men gladly pursue…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乎故謂藝文不能觀人者妄
也謂科目不能盡士者迂也
惟額於數不竝一時終無留
良矣惟執事者秉公司衡者
深識務窮正學以貢於澤宮
爾乃相與告誡於百執事曰
聖天子在上賢公卿在下三年一
===
比士類淹期庸弗愼乎得人
以應社稷攸倚庸弗精乎分
經校藝者毋眩浮獵毋奪鉤
玄則眞才得矣監臨提調者
嚴憲肅令協恭和衷則大典
成矣登明以選錄士以應乃
擇日會讌讌畢進之曰嶺以
punctuated:
乎？故謂藝文不能觀人者，妄也；謂科目不能盡士者，迂也。惟額於數，不竝一時，終無留良矣。惟執事者秉公，司衡者深識，務窮正學，以貢於澤宮。
爾乃相與告誡於百執事曰：「聖天子在上，賢公卿在下，三年一比，士類淹期，庸弗愼乎？得人以應，社稷攸倚，庸弗精乎？分經校藝者，毋眩浮獵，毋奪鉤玄，則眞才得矣。監臨提調者，嚴憲肅令，協恭和衷，則大典成矣。」
登明以選，錄士以應。乃擇日會讌，讌畢進之曰：「嶺以
translation_en:
…would they? Thus, to say that literary compositions cannot reveal a person's character is rash; to say that the examination system cannot encompass all worthy scholars is misguided. Only the numerical quota prevents them from all being selected at one time; ultimately, no worthy man will remain overlooked. Those conducting the examination need only uphold impartiality, and those weighing its merits exercise profound discernment, striving to investigate orthodox learning thoroughly so as to present worthy men to the imperial school.
Then we jointly admonished all those serving in the examination: “The sage Son of Heaven is above, and worthy dukes and ministers are below. The examination is held once every three years, and scholars must wait a long time: how could we fail to exercise care? Obtaining suitable men in response to the court's call is what the altars of soil and grain depend upon: how could we fail to exercise discrimination? Those assigned to assess compositions on the respective Classics must not be dazzled by superficial gleanings of learning or slight those who probe its depths; then true talent will be found. The Supervising Official and Proctors must enforce regulations strictly, maintain discipline in their orders, and cooperate with respect and unity of purpose; then this great ceremony will be accomplished.”
We advanced the discerning for selection and enrolled scholars in response to the court's call. We then chose a day to gather for a banquet. When the banquet was over, we addressed them, saying: “Beyond the Ling mountains …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
南雖在遐荒入漢卽爲名郡
烈士奇節學士雄文卑俯衡
廬濶吞滄溟無論漢宋且評
本朝如丘文莊之經濟陳白沙
之清脩倫迂岡之純懿皆名
諸天下亶非濶論諸士子鍾
奇而力學際時而奮庸近儷
諸公遠匹於古者志也進退
以禮窮達罔變者毅也困而
裕如亨而兼善者弘也若騁
藝徼惠而棄其所學爾士子
其自顛殞以疚乃心若别求
往哲以無負明世廓之以配
于天地厥亦自余爾多士其
punctuated: 南雖在遐荒，入漢卽爲名郡。烈士奇節，學士雄文，卑俯衡廬，濶吞滄溟。無論漢宋，且評本朝：如丘文莊之經濟，陳白沙之清脩，倫迂岡之純懿，皆名諸天下，亶非濶論。諸士子鍾奇而力學，際時而奮庸，近儷諸公，遠匹於古者，志也；進退以禮，窮達罔變者，毅也；困而裕如，亨而兼善者，弘也。若騁藝徼惠，而棄其所學，爾士子其自顛殞，以疚乃心。若别求往哲，以無負明世，廓之以配于天地，厥亦自余。爾多士其
translation_en:
…south of the mountains, though situated in the distant hinterlands, became a renowned commandery upon incorporation into the Han. The extraordinary integrity of its resolute men and the magnificent writings of its scholars tower above Mount Heng and Mount Lu and encompass the vast blue seas. Leaving aside the Han and Song, let us consider our own dynasty: the statecraft of Qiu Wenzhuang, the pure self-cultivation of Chen Baisha, and the unsullied virtue of Lun Yugang are all renowned throughout the realm. These are assuredly no empty generalizations.

For you scholars, endowed with exceptional gifts, to study diligently, seize the opportunities of your age, and exert yourselves in service—to equal these gentlemen of recent times and match the ancients of distant ages—is aspiration. To advance and withdraw according to ritual propriety, remaining unchanged in adversity or success, is steadfastness. To remain at ease amid hardship and, when successful, extend goodness to others is magnanimity. If you display your literary skill to seek favors and abandon what you have learned, you scholars will bring about your own downfall and burden your consciences with remorse. If you seek further among the wise men of the past, so as not to fail this enlightened age, and enlarge your aspirations to accord with Heaven and Earth, this too begins with me [?]. You many scholars, …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
毋以余爲竅言哉
浙江湖州府安吉州儒學學
正王本才謹序
punctuated:
毋以余爲竅言哉！

浙江湖州府安吉州儒學學正王本才謹序。
translation_en:
…do not regard what I say as mere clever talk [?]!

Preface respectfully written by Wang Bencai, Instructor at the Confucian School of Anji Subprefecture, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試
監臨官
巡按廣東監察御史余光〔晦之應天府江寧籍祁門縣人壬辰進士〕
提調官
廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使陸杰〔元望浙江平湖縣人甲戌進士〕
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參議余鋔〔文甫浙江遂安縣人辛巳進士〕
監試官
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使蔣淦〔汝潔廣西全州人辛未進士〕
廣東等處提刑按察司副使鄒守愚〔君哲福建莆田縣人丙戌進士〕
===
考試官
浙江湖州府安吉州儒學學正王本才〔思學江西安福縣人甲午貢士〕
直隸松江府華亭縣儒學訓導郭愷〔汝才江西泰和縣人壬午貢士〕
同考試官
河南開封府許州儒學學正黃仲陽〔宗乾福建閩縣人辛卯貢士〕
湖廣承天府京山縣儒學教諭蔣孟倫〔邦典廣西全州人甲午貢士〕
浙江台州府天台縣儒學教諭林人紀〔肇脩福建莆田縣人戊子貢士〕
江西贛州府會昌縣儒學教諭陳玉〔汝良福建長樂縣人辛卯貢士〕
直隸太平府繁昌縣儒學教諭郝光潤〔子玉湖廣華容縣人戊子貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試

監臨官：
巡按廣東監察御史余光〔晦之，應天府江寧籍，祁門縣人，壬辰進士〕。

提調官：
廣東等處承宣布政使司左布政使陸杰〔元望，浙江平湖縣人，甲戌進士〕。
廣東等處承宣布政使司左參議余鋔〔文甫，浙江遂安縣人，辛巳進士〕。

監試官：
廣東等處提刑按察司按察使蔣淦〔汝潔，廣西全州人，辛未進士〕。
廣東等處提刑按察司副使鄒守愚〔君哲，福建莆田縣人，丙戌進士〕。

考試官：
浙江湖州府安吉州儒學學正王本才〔思學，江西安福縣人，甲午貢士〕。
直隸松江府華亭縣儒學訓導郭愷〔汝才，江西泰和縣人，壬午貢士〕。

同考試官：
河南開封府許州儒學學正黃仲陽〔宗乾，福建閩縣人，辛卯貢士〕。
湖廣承天府京山縣儒學教諭蔣孟倫〔邦典，廣西全州人，甲午貢士〕。
浙江台州府天台縣儒學教諭林人紀〔肇脩，福建莆田縣人，戊子貢士〕。
江西贛州府會昌縣儒學教諭陳玉〔汝良，福建長樂縣人，辛卯貢士〕。
直隸太平府繁昌縣儒學教諭郝光潤〔子玉，湖廣華容縣人，戊子貢士〕。
translation_en:
Guangdong Provincial Examination, the Sixteenth Year of Jiajing (1537)

Supervising Official
Yu Guang, Investigating Censor on an inspection tour of Guangdong, had the courtesy name Huizhi. He was registered in Jiangning, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Qimen County; he became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the renchen year.

Proctors
Lu Jie, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Yuanwang. A native of Pinghu County, Zhejiang, he became a metropolitan graduate in the jiaxu year.
Yu Wan, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Wenfu. A native of Sui'an County, Zhejiang, he became a metropolitan graduate in the xinsi year.

Examination Surveillance Officials
Jiang Gan, Surveillance Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Rujie. A native of Quanzhou, Guangxi, he became a metropolitan graduate in the xinwei year.
Zou Shouyu, Vice Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Junzhe. A native of Putian County, Fujian, he became a metropolitan graduate in the bingxu year.

Examiners
Wang Bencai, Instructor at the Confucian School of Anji Subprefecture, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, had the courtesy name Sixue. A native of Anfu County, Jiangxi, he became a tribute student (gongshi) in the jiawu year.
Guo Kai, Assistant Instructor at the Confucian School of Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, had the courtesy name Rucai. A native of Taihe County, Jiangxi, he became a tribute student in the renwu year.

Associate Examiners
Huang Zhongyang, Instructor at the Confucian School of Xuzhou Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Zongqian. A native of Min County, Fujian, he became a tribute student in the xinmao year.
Jiang Menglun, Instructor at the Confucian School of Jingshan County, Chengtian Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Bangdian. A native of Quanzhou, Guangxi, he became a tribute student in the jiawu year.

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
固天縱之將聖又多能也
致中和天地位焉萬物育焉
智譬則巧也聖譬則力也由射於百步之
外也其至爾力也其中非爾力也
易
坤道其順乎承天而時行
九五渙汗其大號渙王居无咎
===
仁者見之謂之仁知者見之謂之知百姓
日用而不知故君子之道鮮矣
君子藏器於身待時而動何不利之有動
而不括是以出而有獲語成器而動者
也
書
曰若稽古帝舜曰重華協于帝
德無常師主善爲師善無常主協于克一
王來紹上帝自服于土中旦曰其作大邑
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書

固天縱之將聖，又多能也。

致中和，天地位焉，萬物育焉。

智譬則巧也，聖譬則力也。由射於百步之外也，其至，爾力也；其中，非爾力也。

易

坤道其順乎！承天而時行。

九五：渙汗其大號，渙王居，无咎。

仁者見之謂之仁，知者見之謂之知，百姓日用而不知，故君子之道鮮矣。

君子藏器於身，待時而動，何不利之有？動而不括，是以出而有獲，語成器而動者也。

書

曰若稽古帝舜，曰重華協于帝。

德無常師，主善爲師；善無常主，協于克一。

王來紹上帝，自服于土中。旦曰：「其作大邑
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Surely Heaven has endowed him to be a great sage; he also possesses many abilities.

Bring centrality and harmony to their fullest realization, and Heaven and Earth will take their proper places and the myriad things will flourish.

Wisdom may be compared to skill, and sagehood to strength. It is like shooting at a target more than a hundred paces away: reaching it is due to your strength; hitting the mark is not due to your strength.

Book of Changes (Yijing)

How compliant is the way of Kun! It follows Heaven and acts in accordance with the seasons.

Nine in the fifth place: He issues his great proclamations as sweat pours forth; he disperses the king’s accumulated stores. There is no blame.

The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom. The common people use it daily without understanding it. Thus the way of the gentleman is seldom understood.

The gentleman stores his capacities within himself and waits for the proper time to act. How could anything be unfavorable? He acts without being constrained, and therefore gains something when he goes forth. This speaks of one who acts only after bringing his capacities to completion.

Book of Documents (Shujing)

Examining antiquity, we find that Emperor Shun was called Chonghua, “Repeated Brilliance,” and matched the preceding emperor in virtue.

Virtue has no fixed teacher: take goodness as your teacher. Goodness has no fixed standard: accord with the ability to remain single-minded.

The king has come to carry on the work of the Lord on High and himself undertake his duties in the center of the land. Dan said: “Let him build a great city …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
其自時配皇天毖祀于上下其自時中
乂王厥有成命治民今休
惟德惟義時乃大訓不由古訓于何其訓
詩
九月築場圃十月納禾稼黍稷重穋禾麻
菽麥嗟我農夫我稼旣同上入執宮功
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋其始播
百穀
夜如何其夜未央庭燎之光君子至止鸞
===
聲將將
比于文王其德靡悔旣受帝祉施于孫子
以介眉壽永言保之思皇多祜烈文辟公
綏以多福俾緝熙于純嘏
春秋
大雩〔桓公五年〕秋八月壬午大閱〔桓公六年〕
晉人納捷菑于邾弗克納 宋子哀來奔
〔文公十四年〕
公至自伐齊〔襄公十九年〕
punctuated:
其自時配皇天，毖祀于上下；其自時中乂，王厥有成命，治民今休。
惟德惟義，時乃大訓；不由古訓，于何其訓？
詩
九月築場圃，十月納禾稼：黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麥。嗟我農夫，我稼旣同，上入執宮功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯；亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。
夜如何其？夜未央。庭燎之光，君子至止，鸞聲將將。
比于文王，其德靡悔。旣受帝祉，施于孫子。以介眉壽，永言保之。思皇多祜，烈文辟公，綏以多福，俾緝熙于純嘏。
春秋
大雩。〔桓公五年〕秋八月壬午，大閱。〔桓公六年〕
晉人納捷菑于邾，弗克納。宋子哀來奔。〔文公十四年〕
公至自伐齊。〔襄公十九年〕
translation_en:
…From here he shall match August Heaven and carefully conduct sacrifices to the powers above and below; from here he shall govern from the center. The king has a settled mandate; may his rule over the people now be excellent.
Only virtue and righteousness constitute the great instruction. If one does not follow the teachings of antiquity, what teachings can one follow?

Book of Odes
In the ninth month we prepare the threshing grounds and gardens; in the tenth month we bring in the crops: millet and panicled millet, late-ripening and early-ripening grain, grain and hemp, beans and wheat. Ah, we farmers! Our crops have all been gathered; we go up into the settlement to undertake work on the dwellings. By day gather thatch; by night twist ropes. Hurry up onto the roofs to repair them, for soon you must begin sowing the hundred grains.
What time of night is it? The night is not yet half spent. The courtyard torches shine; the lords arrive, their carriage bells jingling.
Model yourself on King Wen, whose virtue gave no cause for regret. Having received the blessings of the Lord on High, pass them down to your descendants. Thereby attain venerable longevity and preserve these blessings forever. Ah, splendid are the many blessings! Illustrious and cultured lords, may you be granted abundant good fortune and enabled to continue in ever greater splendor amid perfect blessings.

Spring and Autumn Annals
A great rain sacrifice was held.〔Fifth year of Duke Huan〕In autumn, in the eighth month, on the renwu day, a grand military review was held.〔Sixth year of Duke Huan〕
The men of Jin sought to install Jiezi in Zhu but could not install him. Zi’ai of Song came fleeing here.〔Fourteenth year of Duke Wen〕
The duke returned from campaigning against Qi.〔Nineteenth year of Duke Xiang〕

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
盟于召陵僖公四年夏四月巳巳晉侯齊
師宋師秦師及楚人戰于城濮楚師敗
績僖公二十八年三月公會劉子晉侯
宋公蔡侯衞侯陳子鄭伯許男曹伯莒
子邾子頓子胡子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
子齊國夏于召陵侵楚定公四年
禮記
凡官民材必先論之論辨然後使之任事
然後爵之位定然後祿之爵人於朝與
===
士共之
立太傅少傅以養之欲其知父子君臣之
道也
五色成文而不亂八風從律而不姦百度
得數而有常
天無私覆地無私載日月無私照奉斯三
者以勞天下此之謂三無私
第貳場
論
punctuated:
盟于召陵，僖公四年。夏四月巳巳，晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績，僖公二十八年。三月，公會劉子、晉侯、宋公、蔡侯、衞侯、陳子、鄭伯、許男、曹伯、莒子、邾子、頓子、胡子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子、齊國夏于召陵，侵楚，定公四年。

禮記
凡官民材，必先論之；論辨，然後使之；任事，然後爵之；位定，然後祿之。爵人於朝，與士共之。
立太傅、少傅以養之，欲其知父子、君臣之道也。
五色成文而不亂，八風從律而不姦，百度得數而有常。
天無私覆，地無私載，日月無私照。奉斯三者以勞天下，此之謂三無私。

第貳場
論
translation_en:
They concluded a covenant at Shaoling. Fourth year of Duke Xi.

In summer, in the fourth month, on the sisi [?] day, the Marquis of Jin and the armies of Qi, Song, and Qin fought the men of Chu at Chengpu. The army of Chu suffered a crushing defeat. Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.

In the third month, the duke met the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Marquis of Wei, the Viscount of Chen, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Dun, the Viscount of Hu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, the Viscount of Lesser Zhu, and Guo Xia of Qi at Shaoling, and they invaded Chu. Fourth year of Duke Ding.

Record of Rites (Liji)

Whenever appointing talented men from among the people to office, one must first assess them. Only after their abilities have been assessed and distinguished should they be employed; only after they have undertaken responsibilities should they be granted rank; and only after their positions have been settled should they receive stipends. Rank is conferred upon men at court, in consultation with the officers.

A Grand Preceptor and a Junior Preceptor are appointed to nurture him, so that he may understand the proper relations between father and son and between ruler and minister.

The five colors form patterns without confusion; the eight winds accord with the pitch standards without deviation; and the hundred measures attain their proper numerical proportions and remain constant.

Heaven shelters all without partiality; earth bears all without partiality; the sun and moon shine upon all without partiality. To follow these three in laboring for the welfare of all under Heaven is what is called the three forms of impartiality.

Second Session

Discourse

先天下而後天下之謂君
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔建元

策五道。
問：我
translation_en:
“One who goes before all under Heaven and comes after all under Heaven is called a ruler.”

One topic from the categories of edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?].
Compose a simulated Han edict calling for the recommendation of worthy, upright men who will speak frankly and remonstrate without reserve. First year of Jianyuan.
Compose a simulated Tang proclamation appointing Lu Zhi as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Jointly Manager of Affairs. Eighth year of Zhenyuan.
Compose a simulated congratulatory memorial from the assembled officials on the formal investiture of the imperial heir apparent and his assumption of his proper position in the Eastern Palace.

Five legal judgments:
Committing an offense and voluntarily confessing.
Omitting the use of the seal on paper currency.
Keys and locks for controlled gates.
Forging an imperial decree.
Exceeding the prescribed time limit for manufacture or construction.

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
朝建官植國表裏周官
聖皇統大經而運乾斷羣臣綸萬糸而體坤承
三公集議而
天子裁之盡去中書威福之權九卿分職而百
僚佐之猶存冢宰統均之要六科有封
駁之寄十三道有激揚之專大率君人
如天運而健行三公如陰陽而輔理九
卿如五行而敷化科道如風行以肅清
至於振綱貞度以通上下則御史按藩
===
其設也惟於史官未有專職以復於古
夫史官默握予奪之柄而暗運砥礪之
機以相天地垂戒道今雖有脩撰編脩
之名而咸豫養
經筵之德分直入史館孰為馬遷更番舉故
事孰效吳競乃以紀言動書事實為末
務而皆不屑為矣聞之前人用心者亦
不過集通報紀頒行而已豈諸臣咸不
恭厥事以恪乃職殆亦不專其官以責
punctuated:
朝建官植國，表裏周官。聖皇統大經而運乾斷，羣臣綸萬糸而體坤承。三公集議而天子裁之，盡去中書威福之權；九卿分職而百僚佐之，猶存冢宰統均之要。六科有封駁之寄，十三道有激揚之專。大率君人如天運而健行，三公如陰陽而輔理，九卿如五行而敷化，科道如風行以肅清。至於振綱貞度以通上下，則御史按藩，其設也。惟於史官，未有專職以復於古。
夫史官默握予奪之柄，而暗運砥礪之機，以相天地垂戒道。今雖有脩撰、編脩之名，而咸豫養經筵之德。分直入史館，孰為馬遷？更番舉故事，孰效吳競？乃以紀言動、書事實為末務，而皆不屑為矣。聞之前人用心者，亦不過集通報、紀頒行而已。豈諸臣咸不恭厥事以恪乃職？殆亦不專其官以責
translation_en:
…our dynasty established offices and founded the state, taking the Offices of Zhou as its framework within and without. The sagely emperor commands the great guiding principles and exercises Heaven’s decisiveness; his ministers order the myriad threads of affairs and embody Earth’s obedient support. The Three Dukes deliberate collectively, and the Son of Heaven decides, entirely removing the Secretariat’s power to dispense rewards and punishments. The Nine Ministers divide their duties, assisted by the hundred officials, preserving the essential coordinating function of the Grand Steward. The Six Offices of Scrutiny are entrusted with returning and rejecting imperial directives; the Thirteen Circuits have special responsibility for censuring the unworthy and commending the worthy. Broadly speaking, the ruler moves vigorously like Heaven in its revolutions; the Three Dukes assist in ordering affairs like yin and yang; the Nine Ministers extend transforming influence like the Five Phases; and the supervising secretaries and censors bring purification like the coursing wind. As for upholding the governing framework and rectifying standards to maintain communication between higher and lower ranks, this is the purpose of appointing investigating censors to inspect the provinces. Only for the historiographers have dedicated duties yet to be established that would restore ancient practice.
Historiographers silently wield the power to confer or withhold approval, discreetly operating the means of moral encouragement and correction, thereby assisting Heaven and Earth in transmitting the way of admonition [?]. Today, although the titles Senior Compiler and Junior Compiler exist, their holders all participate in cultivating imperial virtue at the Classics Colloquium. They enter the Historiography Office in separate duty shifts, but who among them is a Sima Qian? They take turns presenting historical precedents, but who emulates Wu Jing 吳競 [?]? Instead, they regard recording words and actions and writing down the facts of events as minor tasks, and all disdain to undertake them. I have heard that even conscientious men of earlier times did no more than collect official reports and record what was promulgated. Can it be that all these ministers fail to attend respectfully to their business and discharge their duties diligently? Perhaps it is also because their offices have not been given exclusive responsibilities by which to hold them accountable for …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乃成故耳
聖天子在上禮樂爲昭文物爲備諸生母惜討
論往制以敷大典
問天地爲廣龍蛇並育而不相悖
聖王爲廣華夷同體而罔以凌故侵暴而後有
甲兵之興不得已而後有征伐之舉若
彼來格因受而化之不咎其往不拒其
歸畜以禽獸古之道也何者天以星躔
分野地以山川分域人以音形分類氣
===
以清厲分俗自弗能一也而以力一之
終罔能久昔人伐獫狁走東胡城朔方
空幕南皆破胡以立武功征有苗伐鬼
方開南夷誅徵側皆平蠻以成偉績其
間或難或易倏服倏叛勒燕然者雄赫
赫之武立銅表者假燁燁之光薄伐不
窮者得禦戎之體班師聽格者享來王
之休何憚而不竟其說也今者吉囊猖
獗人忌其强安南不庭人輕其弱竊恐
punctuated:
乃成故耳。聖天子在上，禮樂爲昭，文物爲備。諸生母惜討論往制，以敷大典。

問：天地爲廣，龍蛇並育而不相悖；聖王爲廣，華夷同體而罔以凌。故侵暴而後有甲兵之興，不得已而後有征伐之舉。若彼來格，因受而化之，不咎其往，不拒其歸，畜以禽獸，古之道也。何者？天以星躔分野，地以山川分域，人以音形分類，氣以清厲分俗，自弗能一也。而以力一之，終罔能久。昔人伐獫狁，走東胡，城朔方，空幕南，皆破胡以立武功；征有苗，伐鬼方，開南夷，誅徵側，皆平蠻以成偉績。其間或難或易，倏服倏叛。勒燕然者雄赫赫之武，立銅表者假燁燁之光；薄伐不窮者得禦戎之體，班師聽格者享來王之休。何憚而不竟其說也？今者吉囊猖獗，人忌其强；安南不庭，人輕其弱。竊恐
translation_en:
…simply because they are not held accountable for accomplishing their tasks. With the sage Son of Heaven above, rites and music shine forth, and the institutions and adornments of civilization are fully established. You candidates should spare no effort in discussing former institutions, so as to elaborate the great canons.

Policy question: Heaven and earth are capacious: dragons and snakes alike are nurtured without conflicting with one another. The sage king is capacious: the Hua and the Yi form one body, without one oppressing the other. Thus arms are raised only after aggression and violence occur, and punitive expeditions are undertaken only when unavoidable. If those peoples come to submit, receive and transform them accordingly; do not blame them for their past or reject their return. To tend them as one does birds and beasts was the way of antiquity. Why is this? Heaven divides its celestial regions by the courses of the stars; earth divides its territories by mountains and rivers; human beings fall into different groups according to speech and appearance; and vital influences distinguish customs through their purity or harshness. These things cannot naturally be made uniform. If force is used to unify them, the result can never endure.

Men of old attacked the Xianyun, put the Donghu to flight, fortified Shuofang, and emptied the lands south of the desert: all these were defeats of the Hu that established martial merit. They campaigned against the Youmiao, attacked Guifang, opened up the lands of the southern Yi, and put Zheng Ce to death: all these were pacifications of the Man that achieved great deeds. Among these undertakings, some were difficult and others easy; submission and rebellion succeeded each other in a moment. He who engraved his achievements on Mount Yanran displayed awe-inspiring martial might; he who erected a bronze marker drew upon resplendent glory. Those who mounted limited attacks without pursuing the enemy to exhaustion grasped the proper method of resisting the Rong; those who withdrew their armies and awaited submission enjoyed the blessing of others coming to acknowledge their kingship. Why hesitate to explain these matters fully?

Now Ji Nang runs rampant, and people fear his strength; Annam fails to pay homage at court, and people scorn its weakness. I venture to fear that…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
主客分形而難易之勢已判議者昧兵
徒覩其形而未究其實往日之事可考
也諸生腕穎奮志投筆封侯此其時矣
願上平胡平蠻之策以建丕烈
問周宗維藩厥後晉猶主霸而魯猶會盟
漢宗維强厥後光武中興而昭烈後振
宗室丕隆國命攸倚也我
皇明宗室如雲如林蕃邁周漢夫宗者國之榦
也民者國之土也不厚其宗是弱其榦
===
何以樹屏不恤其民是竭其土何以植
榦今山西河南之
宗室極盛而山西河南之民亦困矣及兹弗
圖榦土兩傾後將何及今之計者無已
則立宗學乎科目歲貢猶可聽之以開
仕途是通其生也無已則分派遷乎地
無藩封猶可安之以立公籍是廣其生
也王朝多官不以臨民尚可以任置田
供賦不以妨民或可以耕昔者更生立
punctuated:
主客分形，而難易之勢已判。議者昧兵，徒覩其形，而未究其實，往日之事可考也。諸生腕穎，奮志投筆，封侯此其時矣。願上平胡平蠻之策，以建丕烈。
問：周宗維藩，厥後晉猶主霸，而魯猶會盟；漢宗維强，厥後光武中興，而昭烈後振。宗室丕隆，國命攸倚也。我皇明宗室如雲如林，蕃邁周漢。夫宗者，國之榦也；民者，國之土也。不厚其宗，是弱其榦，何以樹屏？不恤其民，是竭其土，何以植榦？今山西、河南之宗室極盛，而山西、河南之民亦困矣。及兹弗圖，榦土兩傾，後將何及？今之計者，無已則立宗學乎？科目歲貢，猶可聽之，以開仕途，是通其生也。無已則分派遷乎？地無藩封，猶可安之，以立公籍，是廣其生也。王朝多官，不以臨民，尚可以任；置田供賦，不以妨民，或可以耕。昔者更生立
translation_en:
…Once the respective positions of defender and invader are distinguished, the relative difficulty of the campaigns is already clear. Those who discuss the matter do not understand warfare: they merely observe its outward configuration without investigating its realities. Past events can be examined for guidance. You students, gifted with the brush [?], should rouse your resolve and cast aside your writing brushes for military service: now is the time to win enfeoffment as marquises. Please submit plans for pacifying the Hu and the Man, so that great achievements may be accomplished.
Question: The Zhou royal lineage served as a protective screen; even in later times, Jin still exercised hegemony and Lu still participated in covenant assemblies. The Han imperial lineage provided strength; subsequently Guangwu restored the dynasty, and Zhaolie revived it once more. The flourishing of the imperial clan is that upon which the destiny of the state depends. The imperial clan of our august Ming is as numerous as clouds and as dense as a forest, surpassing those of Zhou and Han in its proliferation. The imperial clan is the trunk of the state, and the people are its soil. To fail to strengthen the clan is to weaken the trunk: how then can a protective screen be established? To fail to care for the people is to exhaust the soil: how then can the trunk take root? Today the imperial clan is exceedingly numerous in Shanxi and Henan, while the people of Shanxi and Henan are also impoverished. Unless plans are made now, trunk and soil will both collapse. What remedy will be possible afterward? In devising measures for the present, might we at least establish schools for the imperial clan? Clan members could be permitted to participate in the examinations and the annual tribute-student system, opening a path into official service and thus providing access to a livelihood. Might we at least divide them into branches and relocate them [?]? They could be settled in places without princely fiefs and entered in public registers, thus broadening their means of subsistence. The princely courts have many offices: those that do not involve governing the people could still be filled by clan members. They might also acquire fields and pay taxes, cultivating them where this would not disadvantage the people. In former times, Gengsheng stood…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
朝直氣而姦懾劉欽耕野脫難而光復
漢皆非乎請豫圖之
問伐謀者將之微也全國者師之權也破
敵者軍之法也是故不戰者帝其微以
機發乎一戰者王其權以變應乎三戰
者霸其法以形設乎今戎虜暴橫深入
肆掠寧縱弗戰作戰維何厚儲恤士固
塞據險守以虎落布以渠荅者戰之具
也廣設戰車陷堅遮北鱗次爲陣鈎聯
===
爲營者戰之技也夫步不勝騎騎不勝
車軍之明驗我車旣攻以興周兵車大
會以霸齊故古者夷狄不得志於中國
帝王握長技以制勝者此也李忠定公
銳志破金其車三勝可得聞乎張統制
經心剋敵其車制簡便可復講乎古人
用武剛者破匈奴運偏箱者滅突厥冒
狻猊者雄海内乘鐵籠者復全齊惟房
琯不善用乃以取敗後世議者遂以廢
punctuated:
朝，直氣而姦懾；劉欽耕野，脫難而光復漢，皆非乎？請豫圖之。
問：伐謀者，將之微也；全國者，師之權也；破敵者，軍之法也。是故不戰者帝，其微以機發乎？一戰者王，其權以變應乎？三戰者霸，其法以形設乎？今戎虜暴橫，深入肆掠，寧縱弗戰？作戰維何？厚儲恤士，固塞據險，守以虎落，布以渠荅者，戰之具也；廣設戰車，陷堅遮北，鱗次爲陣，鈎聯爲營者，戰之技也。夫步不勝騎，騎不勝車，軍之明驗。我車旣攻，以興周；兵車大會，以霸齊。故古者夷狄不得志於中國，帝王握長技以制勝者，此也。李忠定公銳志破金，其車三勝，可得聞乎？張統制經心剋敵，其車制簡便，可復講乎？古人用武剛者破匈奴，運偏箱者滅突厥，冒狻猊者雄海内，乘鐵籠者復全齊。惟房琯不善用，乃以取敗，後世議者遂以廢
translation_en:
…at court, his upright spirit intimidated the wicked; Liu Qin [?] tilled the fields, escaped calamity, and restored the Han. Were these not both so? Please devise plans for this in advance.
Question: Attacking the enemy’s plans is the subtle art of a general; preserving a state intact is the exercise of strategic discretion by an army; defeating the enemy is the method of military operations. Thus, does one who attains imperial rule without fighting set this subtle art in motion by seizing the opportune moment? Does one who attains kingly rule through a single battle exercise this discretion in response to changing circumstances? Does one who attains hegemony through three battles establish these methods according to the configuration of forces? Now the barbarian enemies act with brutal arrogance, penetrating deep into our territory and plundering at will. Can we let them proceed unchecked without fighting? How should we wage war? Amassing ample provisions, caring for the soldiers, strengthening fortifications, occupying strategic terrain, defending positions with palisades, and deploying quda defensive devices—these are the material means of warfare. Deploying war chariots widely, breaking through strong positions and intercepting fleeing troops, arranging formations like overlapping scales, and linking the chariots together to form camps—these are the techniques of warfare. That infantry cannot prevail over cavalry, and cavalry cannot prevail over chariots, is clearly demonstrated by military experience. ‘Our chariots were sturdy’: by these means Zhou rose to power. Great assemblies of war chariots established Qi’s hegemony. Thus, in antiquity, the barbarians could not achieve their ambitions in the Central Kingdom. This was how emperors and kings secured victory through their command of superior techniques. Duke Li Zhongding was firmly resolved to defeat the Jin: may we hear about the three advantages of his chariots? Commander Zhang devoted his attention to overcoming the enemy: could the simple and practical construction of his chariots be discussed again? Among the ancients, those who used wugang war wagons defeated the Xiongnu; those who deployed pianxiang wagons destroyed the Tujue; those who covered their vehicles with lion forms [?] dominated all within the seas; and those who rode in iron cages recovered the whole territory of Qi. Only Fang Guan failed to employ them well and consequently suffered defeat. Later commentators thereupon used this as grounds to abolish…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
車黄帝神於兵其造指南車以破蚩尤
者何也
問地分清濁肇於風氣未淳心無古今存
於敎化有道善敎化則氣自變矣變氣
質則俗自還矣
明運丕隆海島沾渥雕題沐浴豈惟嶺南英材
出而日昌獷悍革而異昔或云廣之俗
質直尚信韶之俗淳樸尚愨肇慶之俗
勤漁績南雄之俗雜夷夏雷之俗多習
===
===
學高之俗多簡嗇潮忠實而篤文行廉
儉朴而稀訟牒瓊之衣冠可齒中州黎
蛋混居野而畏法是朴風尚存或以在
嶺外也邇來崇淫祀而吉禮亂慵耕稼
而戶口隱族寡恩而豪暴張兵不戢而
盜賊縱伊欲行保甲之法舉鄉學之規
輕折抽之利申漢條之例嚴酗酒之禁
重賭博之律以救時維風政之重也諸
生生於其地長於其鄉固自有轉移之
punctuated:
車。黄帝神於兵，其造指南車以破蚩尤者何也？
問：地分清濁，肇於風氣未淳；心無古今，存於敎化有道。善敎化則氣自變矣，變氣質則俗自還矣。明運丕隆，海島沾渥，雕題沐浴，豈惟嶺南英材出而日昌，獷悍革而異昔？或云：廣之俗質直尚信，韶之俗淳樸尚愨，肇慶之俗勤漁績，南雄之俗雜夷夏，雷之俗多習學，高之俗多簡嗇，潮忠實而篤文行，廉儉朴而稀訟牒，瓊之衣冠可齒中州，黎蛋混居野而畏法。是朴風尚存，或以在嶺外也。邇來崇淫祀而吉禮亂，慵耕稼而戶口隱，族寡恩而豪暴張，兵不戢而盜賊縱。伊欲行保甲之法，舉鄉學之規，輕折抽之利，申漢條之例，嚴酗酒之禁，重賭博之律，以救時維風，政之重也。諸生生於其地，長於其鄉，固自有轉移之
translation_en:
…chariots. The Yellow Emperor possessed divine skill in warfare: why, then, did he construct the south-pointing chariot to defeat Chiyou?
Question: That lands differ in purity and turbidity originates in local influences that have not yet become refined; that the human heart is the same in antiquity and today depends on moral instruction being properly conducted. If moral instruction is effective, local influences will change of themselves; if people's temperaments are transformed, their customs will naturally return to their proper state. The fortunes of the Ming have risen magnificently: even the islands receive its abundant bounty, and peoples with tattooed foreheads bathe in its beneficence. Is this merely a matter of outstanding talent emerging and flourishing daily in Lingnan, and of its fierce and unruly ways being reformed so that they differ from the past?
Some say that the customs of Guang are straightforward and prize trustworthiness; those of Shao are simple and prize sincerity; those of Zhaoqing encourage diligence in fishing and spinning; those of Nanxiong mingle non-Han and Chinese ways; those of Lei widely encourage study; and those of Gao generally favor simplicity and frugality. The people of Chao are loyal and honest, devoted to literary learning and moral conduct; those of Lian are frugal and plain, with few lawsuits. The gentry of Qiong can rank alongside those of the Central Plain, while the Li and Dan live intermingled in the countryside and stand in awe of the law. These simple customs still survive, perhaps because the region lies beyond the mountain ranges.
Recently, however, the veneration of unauthorized cults has disrupted proper sacrificial rites; indolence in cultivation has been accompanied by concealment of households from registration; kindness within lineages has diminished while powerful bullies have grown more aggressive; and soldiers have gone unchecked while bandits run free. To implement the baojia system of mutual household responsibility, establish regulations for local schools, reduce the exactions from commutation and levies [?], reaffirm precedents from Han statutes [?], enforce strict prohibitions on drunkenness, and impose heavier penalties for gambling—these are important matters of government for remedying the troubles of the age and preserving good customs. You candidates were born in this region and grew up in its communities; surely you yourselves have means of bringing about reform…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
固天縱之將聖又多能也
馬拯
同考試官教諭陳批脫化題目以錯綜成文實不越
於矩度用以式士作之範
同考試官教諭林批子貢能言聖人之蘊此作能發
子貢之言
考試官訓導郭批子亦善言聖者
===
考試官學正王批變合雄渾
天裕聖人以大德而麗之以藝者也夫天生聖
人以統道也縱之聖以為統而多藝能盡其大
哉太宰不知聖故以多能與夫子子貢告之曰
退藏於密而不見其有者聖人之分智周萬物
而時見其能者聖人之餘夫天篤聖人上焉賴
以成天地之能下焉賴以定民物之志重其任
而薄其德則弗勝也豐其責而嗇其才則弗舉
也故定其命以為固而莫為之回縱其質以為
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「固天縱之將聖，又多能也。」

馬拯

同考試官教諭陳批：「脫化題目，以錯綜成文，實不越於矩度，用以式士作之範。」

同考試官教諭林批：「子貢能言聖人之蘊，此作能發子貢之言。」

考試官訓導郭批：「子亦善言聖者。」

考試官學正王批：「變合雄渾。」

天裕聖人以大德，而麗之以藝者也。夫天生聖人以統道也，縱之聖以為統，而多藝能盡其大哉？太宰不知聖，故以多能與夫子。子貢告之曰：「退藏於密而不見其有者，聖人之分；智周萬物而時見其能者，聖人之餘。夫天篤聖人，上焉賴以成天地之能，下焉賴以定民物之志。重其任而薄其德，則弗勝也；豐其責而嗇其才，則弗舉也。故定其命以為固，而莫為之回；縱其質以為
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Surely Heaven has endowed him to be a great sage, and he also has many abilities.”

Ma Zheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “He transforms the topic freely, weaving its elements into an essay, yet never oversteps the prescribed bounds. This may serve as a model for candidates’ compositions.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Zigong could express the sage’s inner riches; this composition can unfold the meaning of Zigong’s words.”

Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: “You too are skilled at speaking of the sage.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: “Its variations and integration are powerful and rounded.”

Heaven enriches the sage with great virtue and adorns him with accomplishments. Heaven brings forth the sage to unite the Way. It endows him with sagehood to accomplish that unity: could his many accomplishments exhaust his greatness? The Grand Steward did not understand sagehood and therefore credited the Master with many abilities. Zigong told him:

“To withdraw into secrecy without displaying what one possesses is the sage’s proper portion; to comprehend all things with his wisdom and on occasion display his abilities is the sage’s surplus. Heaven richly endows the sage: above, it relies on him to fulfill the capacities of Heaven and Earth; below, it relies on him to settle the purposes of the people and all things. Were his charge weighty but his virtue slight, he could not bear it; were his responsibilities abundant but his talents scant, he could not discharge them. Thus Heaven establishes his allotted endowment firmly, so that nothing can turn it aside; it gives free scope to his innate nature to make it …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
量而莫爲之限將其機以爲盈而莫爲之止大
心以體天下之物而思通於參兩之相形盡性
以窮天下之賾而神妙於萬類之爲一邇以正
而遠不禦靜以蓄而動有容範不立之則以順
成庶彙之變也物罔踰其神以會通古今之宜
也斯其所以爲夫子若曰多能乃滄海之引以
川瀆天體之繫以星辰太虛固無所不備而散
者非其本質太和固罔有不涵而藝者猶其技
餘射御書數兼之以備物而弗專文章禮樂假
===
===
之以應酬而匪本何者推之於大則或窒運之
於彼則弗通吾終不敢允太宰之品而庸以狹
吾夫子夫因天之縱夫子則守之而不蕩成己
之能夫子則不貪之以爲功此又非太宰所能
知也雖然據其大而畧其小則弗該無以觀聖
人之用卽其末而遺其本則弗精無以測聖人
之神其必合天縱多能而竝觀之則聖藝之辨
昭然矣在當時弗知夫子者豈特一太宰封人
以爲木鐸則精矣而不化黨人以爲博學則泛
punctuated: 量而莫爲之限，將其機以爲盈而莫爲之止。大心以體天下之物，而思通於參兩之相形；盡性以窮天下之賾，而神妙於萬類之爲一。邇以正而遠不禦，靜以蓄而動有容。範不立之則，以順成庶彙之變也；物罔踰其神，以會通古今之宜也。斯其所以爲夫子。若曰多能，乃滄海之引以川瀆，天體之繫以星辰。太虛固無所不備，而散者非其本質；太和固罔有不涵，而藝者猶其技餘。射御書數，兼之以備物而弗專；文章禮樂，假之以應酬而匪本。何者？推之於大則或窒，運之於彼則弗通。吾終不敢允太宰之品，而庸以狹吾夫子。夫因天之縱，夫子則守之而不蕩；成己之能，夫子則不貪之以爲功。此又非太宰所能知也。雖然，據其大而畧其小則弗該，無以觀聖人之用；卽其末而遺其本則弗精，無以測聖人之神。其必合天縱多能而竝觀之，則聖藝之辨昭然矣。在當時弗知夫子者，豈特一太宰？封人以爲木鐸，則精矣而不化；黨人以爲博學，則泛
translation_en:
…a measure to which no limit is set, and brings his vital workings to fullness without imposing any restraint. He enlarges his mind to embody the things of the world, his thought penetrating the mutual manifestation of the Three and the Two; he fully realizes his nature to fathom the world’s hidden complexities, his spiritual efficacy wondrously uniting the myriad kinds of things. Correct in what is near, he encounters no obstruction in what is distant; storing up his capacities in stillness, he has ample scope when acting. He takes as his pattern rules that have not been formally established, thereby bringing the transformations of all things to fulfillment in accordance with their course. Nothing exceeds the reach of his spiritual efficacy, through which he comprehends and reconciles what is fitting in past and present. This is what makes the Master what he is.

To speak merely of his many abilities is like describing the vast sea through the rivers and streams that flow into it, or the heavens through the stars attached to them. The Great Void assuredly contains everything, yet its dispersed manifestations are not its fundamental substance. The Great Harmony assuredly embraces everything, yet the arts remain only the surplus of his abilities. Archery, charioteering, calligraphy, and calculation: he possesses them all to deal fully with things, without specializing in them. Literary composition, ritual, and music: he employs them in responding to circumstances, but they are not his foundation. Why? Extended to greater matters, such skills may encounter an impasse; applied elsewhere, they may fail to work. I would never dare endorse the Grand Steward’s assessment and thereby diminish our Master.

As for the freedom Heaven bestowed upon him, the Master preserves it without allowing it to become unrestrained. As for the abilities he has perfected in himself, the Master does not covet credit for them as achievements. This, too, is beyond what the Grand Steward can understand. Nevertheless, to grasp what is great in him while neglecting what is small is insufficiently comprehensive: it provides no means of observing the sage’s practical activity. To focus on his subsidiary accomplishments while overlooking his foundation is insufficiently discerning: it provides no means of fathoming the sage’s spiritual efficacy. Only by considering together his Heaven-bestowed endowment and his many abilities does the distinction between sagehood and the arts become clear.

Among those in his own time who failed to understand the Master, was the Grand Steward the only one? The border official regarded him as a wooden-tongued bell: this was perceptive, yet failed to grasp his transformative power. The man of Daxiang regarded him as broadly learned: this was sweeping…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
矣而不根接輿以爲鳳鳥則又譏其德衰雖子
貢以爲日月尚或可則其象惟夫子自曰空空
如也吾弗測其空空而請名之以太空
致中和天地位焉萬物育焉
陳棐
同考試官教諭蔣批中和不可分動靜位育不可分
中和此作得之是用錄出
考試官訓導郭批近日爲文者往往言神化此篇
不言神化惡足語心學極功
===
考試官學正王批是可以言心學矣
廓一心而神萬化聖功之極也夫天地萬物一
於心者也善學者其測始之所致而終之極乎
今夫志以存之者運不息之機也氣以通之者
合散殊之分也而造化行於其中學則貫於兩
在者矣故學也者其藏諸心者聖也其利諸用
者神也動靜無端吾不間於致曲顯微合一吾
不息於存誠寂以立中涵陰陽剛柔之體原性
以爲命也感以達和順勝負屈伸之始率性以
punctuated:
矣而不根；接輿以爲鳳鳥，則又譏其德衰。雖子貢以爲日月，尚或可則其象。惟夫子自曰：「空空如也。」吾弗測其空空，而請名之以太空。
致中和，天地位焉，萬物育焉。
陳棐
同考試官教諭蔣批：「中和不可分動靜，位育不可分中和。此作得之，是用錄出。」
考試官訓導郭批：「近日爲文者往往言神化，此篇不言神化，惡足語心學極功？」
考試官學正王批：「是可以言心學矣。」
廓一心而神萬化，聖功之極也。夫天地萬物，一於心者也。善學者，其測始之所致而終之極乎？今夫志以存之者，運不息之機也；氣以通之者，合散殊之分也。而造化行於其中，學則貫於兩在者矣。故學也者，其藏諸心者聖也，其利諸用者神也。動靜無端，吾不間於致曲；顯微合一，吾不息於存誠。寂以立中，涵陰陽剛柔之體，原性以爲命也；感以達和，順勝負屈伸之始，率性以
translation_en:
…yet lacked grounding. Jieyu regarded him as the phoenix, but thereby also reproached him for the decline of his virtue. Even Zigong’s comparison of him to the sun and moon still perhaps offered an image that could be taken as a model. Only the Master himself said, “I am utterly empty.” I cannot fathom his emptiness, and ask leave to call it the Great Void.
“Bring equilibrium and harmony to their utmost, and Heaven and Earth will take their proper places, and the myriad things will flourish.”
Chen Fei
Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “Equilibrium and harmony cannot be divided between activity and stillness; the proper placing of Heaven and Earth and the flourishing of things cannot be divided between equilibrium and harmony. This composition grasps this, and has therefore been selected for inclusion.”
Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor, comments: “Those writing essays nowadays frequently speak of spiritual transformation. This piece does not speak of spiritual transformation: how can it adequately discuss the ultimate achievement of the learning of the mind?”
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “This does qualify to discuss the learning of the mind.”
To expand the single mind and endow the myriad transformations with spiritual efficacy is the ultimate achievement of sagehood. Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things are united in the mind. Should not those adept at learning fathom what is brought about at the beginning and what reaches its utmost at the end? Now, maintaining it through resolve sets in motion the mechanism that never ceases; making it pervasive through vital energy unites what is dispersed and differentiated. Creative transformation proceeds within this, while learning threads through both modes of presence [?]. Thus, in learning, what is stored in the mind is sagehood; what works effectively in practical application is spiritual efficacy. Activity and stillness have no beginning or end: I never interrupt my work of fully developing each particular manifestation of goodness. The manifest and the subtle form one whole: I never cease preserving sincerity. Through stillness I establish equilibrium, embracing the substance of yin and yang, firmness and yielding; this is to trace human nature to its source as Heaven’s mandate. Through responsiveness I bring harmony to realization, following the beginnings of prevailing and yielding, contraction and expansion; this is to follow human nature so as to…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爲道也夫致極者致於其豫無助長將迎之私
位育者應於其時有絪縕昭穆之妙體存故可
以厚本也用利故可以明漸也厚本故可以合
同也明漸故可以鼓舞也是故吾之一心固典
天地之神而立萬物之命矣以健順爲紀則卑
高以陳也以屈伸爲信則寒暑不易也以大德
爲化則生生不窮也以小德爲序則形形不擾
也是天地爲昭心爲神判然者不容於不渾然
一矣萬物爲變心爲通渙然者不容於不混然
===
融矣故擴一心於天地萬物象不徇於其有合
天地萬物於一心理不淪於其虛斡旋之而無
方曲成之而無體抑豈知心之爲浩浩而學之
爲蕩蕩也乎昔者堯舜在上乾清坤寧鳳儀獸
舞明此以南向渾渾噩噩之化也皐夔在下三
光時而萬物蕃明此以北向穆穆翼翼之心也
後之人通玆學者其惟仲舒得之以爲中而更
生或流於繆戾要之周文興而鳳鳴志一之動
氣也湯仁茂而天旱氣一之動志也是故志氣
punctuated: 爲道也。夫致極者，致於其豫，無助長將迎之私；位育者，應於其時，有絪縕昭穆之妙。體存，故可以厚本也；用利，故可以明漸也；厚本，故可以合同也；明漸，故可以鼓舞也。是故吾之一心，固典天地之神而立萬物之命矣。以健順爲紀，則卑高以陳也；以屈伸爲信，則寒暑不易也；以大德爲化，則生生不窮也；以小德爲序，則形形不擾也。是天地爲昭，心爲神，判然者不容於不渾然一矣；萬物爲變，心爲通，渙然者不容於不混然融矣。故擴一心於天地萬物，象不徇於其有；合天地萬物於一心，理不淪於其虛。斡旋之而無方，曲成之而無體，抑豈知心之爲浩浩而學之爲蕩蕩也乎？昔者堯舜在上，乾清坤寧，鳳儀獸舞，明此以南向，渾渾噩噩之化也；皐夔在下，三光時而萬物蕃，明此以北向，穆穆翼翼之心也。後之人通玆學者，其惟仲舒得之以爲中，而更生或流於繆戾。要之，周文興而鳳鳴，志一之動氣也；湯仁茂而天旱，氣一之動志也。是故志氣
translation_en:
…constitutes the Way. Bringing things to their utmost means doing so through prior preparation, without the selfish impulses to force growth or to anticipate and pursue things. Giving all things their proper places and nurturing them means responding at the appropriate time, with the subtle workings of intermingling vital forces and ordered generational relations. Because the underlying substance is preserved, the root can be strengthened; because its functioning is effective, gradual development can be made clear. Strengthening the root makes union possible; making gradual development clear makes inspiration and encouragement possible. Thus my single mind indeed presides over the numinous workings of Heaven and Earth and establishes the allotted nature of the myriad things. Taking vigor and compliance as its guiding principles, it sets forth the low and the high; taking contraction and extension as its dependable pattern, it keeps cold and heat from deviating from their course. Through great virtue it brings transformation, so that generation follows generation without end; through lesser virtues it establishes order, so that distinct forms do not interfere with one another. Thus Heaven and Earth are the manifest aspect, and the mind the numinous: what appears separate cannot but form one undivided whole. The myriad things are transformation, and the mind is their interconnection: what appears dispersed cannot but merge into unity. Therefore, when the single mind is extended to Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things, images are not bound by their tangible existence; when Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things are gathered into the single mind, principle does not sink into its emptiness. It directs their workings without a fixed method and brings each to fulfillment without a fixed form. How, then, could one fathom the vastness of the mind and the boundlessness of learning?

In antiquity, when Yao and Shun occupied the position above, Heaven was clear and Earth tranquil; phoenixes appeared in stately bearing and beasts danced. Understanding this, they faced south as rulers: theirs was the transforming influence of primal simplicity. When Gao and Kui occupied the positions below, the three celestial lights followed their seasons and the myriad things flourished. Understanding this, they faced north as ministers: theirs were reverent and attentive minds. Among later men who comprehended this learning, perhaps only Zhongshu grasped it and thereby attained equilibrium, while Gengsheng sometimes strayed into error and contradiction. In essence, when King Wen of Zhou rose and phoenixes sang, this was the concentrated will moving vital energy; when Tang’s benevolence flourished yet Heaven sent drought, this was concentrated vital energy moving the will. Thus will and vital energy…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
互勝而爲數君子反數而致中
智譬則巧也聖譬則力也由射於百步之
外也其至爾力也其中非爾力也
林光祖
同考試官教諭郝批氣勢宏偉詞有斷截末說清任
和爲鵠處極是
考試官訓導郭批詞雅意新形容智巧聖力之旨
有巧思
考試官學正王批意思圓融
===
觀聖智於巧力而列聖之造著矣夫聖智殊歸
而同極巧力竝發而一精觀於射則聖人之偏
全曷其隱哉且孟子深知孔子者也擬之以樂
而不足復喻之以射而愈彰乃曰古人以射而
觀德吾今以射而論人則知吾孔子巧力全而
德不孤矣何以知其然也夫聖人之智爲樂之
金聲則著也爲射之巧則智亦神矣聖人之聖
爲樂之玉振則昭也爲射之力則聖亦弘矣夫
百步者射之則也是卽聖人之地也鵠也者射
punctuated:
互勝而爲數，君子反數而致中。

智譬則巧也，聖譬則力也。由射於百步之外也，其至爾力也，其中非爾力也。

林光祖

同考試官教諭郝批：氣勢宏偉，詞有斷截，末說清任和爲鵠處極是。

考試官訓導郭批：詞雅意新，形容智巧聖力之旨，有巧思。

考試官學正王批：意思圓融。

觀聖智於巧力，而列聖之造著矣。夫聖智殊歸而同極，巧力竝發而一精。觀於射，則聖人之偏全曷其隱哉？且孟子深知孔子者也，擬之以樂而不足，復喻之以射而愈彰。乃曰：古人以射而觀德，吾今以射而論人，則知吾孔子巧力全而德不孤矣。何以知其然也？夫聖人之智，爲樂之金聲則著也，爲射之巧則智亦神矣。聖人之聖，爲樂之玉振則昭也，爲射之力則聖亦弘矣。夫百步者，射之則也，是卽聖人之地也。鵠也者，射
translation_en:
…They alternately prevail over one another, producing the constraints of fate; the gentleman turns back those constraints and attains equilibrium.

“Wisdom may be likened to skill, and sageliness to strength. It is like shooting from beyond a hundred paces: reaching the target is due to your strength; hitting the mark is not due to your strength.”

Lin Guangzu

Comment by Associate Examiner Hao, Instructor: “The momentum is grand and imposing, and the phrasing decisive. The concluding discussion that takes purity, responsibility, and harmony as the bull’s-eye is exactly right.”

Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: “Elegant diction and fresh ideas. The presentation of the meaning of wisdom as skill and sageliness as strength shows ingenuity.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The ideas are rounded and coherent.”

When sageliness and wisdom are examined through skill and strength, the attainments of the several sages become apparent. Sageliness and wisdom follow distinct paths but reach the same ultimate point; skill and strength operate together and share a single refinement. Viewed through archery, how could the partial or complete attainments of sages remain hidden? Moreover, Mengzi understood Confucius profoundly. Finding a comparison with music insufficient, he further illustrated him through archery, making the matter still clearer. Thus he said: The ancients observed virtue through archery; I now assess men through archery. We can thereby know that our Confucius possessed both skill and strength in full, and that his virtue was not confined to a single quality. How do we know this is so?

The sage’s wisdom is manifest as the sounding of bronze bells in music; as skill in archery, that wisdom is also wondrous. The sage’s sageliness is evident as the concluding resonance of jade chimes in music; as strength in archery, that sageliness is also expansive. A hundred paces is the prescribed distance for archery: it is precisely the ground occupied by the sage. The bull’s-eye is archery’s…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之的也是即聖人之準也百步以為期胡可中
之以為止中的以為則胡可視之以為難故至
之而貫革者力可强其能無待於其巧中之而
決拾者巧實神其妙何預於其强吾觀伯夷尹
惠也咸射於百步之外不以遠而弗至者也是
故射之有力者矣吾觀孔子也亦射於百步之
外不以遠而弗中者也是故天下之善射者也
故曰時乎清也以清為鵠時乎任也以任為鵠
時乎和也以和為鵠射也者射乎其鵠也鵠也
===
者心之時而隨寓以張者也中也者因其張而
中於其時者也故曰可以觀孔子聖智之備矣
古人以射名者飛衞紀昌是已二人相遇而交
射於中路二矢相觸而絶塵於不揚矢窮而捍
之以棘端棘末而中之以其矢是二人者天下
之絶技也然而有相謀之心若吾夫子則射隼
于墉往省于度天下無與為敵而進於技矣
易
坤道其順乎承天而時行
punctuated:
之的也，是即聖人之準也。百步以為期，胡可中之以為止？中的以為則，胡可視之以為難？故至之而貫革者，力可强，其能無待於其巧；中之而決拾者，巧實神，其妙何預於其强？吾觀伯夷、尹、惠也，咸射於百步之外，不以遠而弗至者也，是故射之有力者矣。吾觀孔子也，亦射於百步之外，不以遠而弗中者也，是故天下之善射者也。故曰：時乎清也，以清為鵠；時乎任也，以任為鵠；時乎和也，以和為鵠。射也者，射乎其鵠也。鵠也者，心之時而隨寓以張者也；中也者，因其張而中於其時者也。故曰：可以觀孔子聖智之備矣。古人以射名者，飛衞、紀昌是已。二人相遇而交射於中路，二矢相觸，而絶塵於不揚；矢窮而捍之以棘端，棘末而中之以其矢。是二人者，天下之絶技也，然而有相謀之心。若吾夫子，則射隼于墉，往省于度，天下無與為敵，而進於技矣。
易
坤道其順乎！承天而時行。
translation_en:
…is the target at which one shoots: this is precisely the sage’s standard. With a hundred paces set as the distance, how could one stop halfway? With hitting the mark as the rule, how could one regard it as too difficult? Thus, when an arrow reaches the target and pierces the hide, strength may be formidable, and this capacity does not depend upon skill. When one hits the mark using thumb ring and armguard, skill is truly wondrous: what does its subtlety owe to strength?
When I consider Boyi, Yi Yin, and Liuxia Hui, all shoot beyond a hundred paces, and distance does not prevent their arrows from reaching the target. They are therefore archers possessed of strength. When I consider Confucius, he too shoots beyond a hundred paces, and distance does not prevent him from hitting the mark. He is therefore the finest archer in the world. Thus, when the time calls for purity, he takes purity as his target; when the time calls for assuming responsibility, he takes responsibility as his target; when the time calls for harmony, he takes harmony as his target. Archery means shooting at the proper target. The target is what the heart sets up according to the demands of the time and whatever circumstances it encounters. Hitting it means responding to the target thus set up and hitting what is appropriate to that moment. Thus, we may discern the completeness of Confucius’s sageliness and wisdom.
Among the ancients renowned for archery were Fei Wei and Ji Chang. The two met on the road and shot at one another. Their arrows collided and fell without raising any dust [?]. When his arrows were exhausted, one warded off a shot with the tip of a thorn; the other struck the thorn’s tip with his arrow [?]. These two possessed unrivaled skills, yet each harbored designs against the other. Our Master, by contrast, shoots the falcon upon the wall and goes forth mindful of the proper measure [?]. No one in the world can rival him, and he has advanced beyond mere skill.
Book of Changes
“How compliant is the Way of Kun! It follows Heaven and acts according to the time.”

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
劉漢
同考試官敎諭蔣批理明意盡格度不浮錄之以式
多士乃易義之軌範者
考試官訓導郭批得潔淨精微之旨
考試官學正王批明暢清雅
文言論地之爲道惟代天以成化焉夫無成而
代有終地道固有然者孰謂坤非以順爲職乎
夫子旣發承天之義以贊坤元此復申之以爲
論大化則乾坤合德語功用則厚載爲勞何也
===
夫其動剛德方祖萬物而富有無疆道若擬於
乾矣然而隤然者其性也陰陽摩盪委至順以
成能凡以相乾之運而已含物化光母六子而
效灋有常似與天同其用矣然而居卑者其分
也化育流行謝玄功於勿有凡以順天之施而
已彼其運橐籥於出震之始元其時乎坤卽承
之以動由翕而之闢也蓋氣之交相爲感而坤
其後至矣鼓絪縕于下濟之初時其至乎地則
隨應而通本藏以爲顯也蓋道之相須爲用而
punctuated:
劉漢

同考試官敎諭蔣批：理明意盡，格度不浮，錄之以式多士，乃易義之軌範者。
考試官訓導郭批：得潔淨精微之旨。
考試官學正王批：明暢清雅。

文言論地之爲道，惟代天以成化焉。夫無成而代有終，地道固有然者，孰謂坤非以順爲職乎？夫子旣發承天之義以贊坤元，此復申之，以爲論大化則乾坤合德，語功用則厚載爲勞。何也？

夫其動剛，德方，祖萬物而富有無疆，道若擬於乾矣。然而隤然者其性也，陰陽摩盪，委至順以成能，凡以相乾之運而已。含物化光，母六子而效灋有常，似與天同其用矣。然而居卑者其分也，化育流行，謝玄功於勿有，凡以順天之施而已。彼其運橐籥於出震之始，元其時乎？坤卽承之以動，由翕而之闢也。蓋氣之交相爲感，而坤其後至矣。鼓絪縕于下濟之初，時其至乎？地則隨應而通，本藏以爲顯也。蓋道之相須爲用，而
translation_en:
Liu Han

Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the meaning fully expressed; the composition’s form and measure are free of superficiality. It is recorded to serve as a model for the many candidates: a standard for essays on the meaning of the Book of Changes.”
Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor, comments: “It captures the purport of purity, refinement, and subtlety.”
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “Clear, fluent, pure, and elegant.”

In discussing the Way of Earth, the Commentary on the Words of the Text states that Earth merely acts on Heaven’s behalf to complete transformation. To initiate no achievement of its own, yet bring things to completion on another’s behalf, is inherent in the Way of Earth. Who could say that Kun does not take compliance as its duty? The Master has already expounded the meaning of receiving Heaven’s action in praising the primal power of Kun. Here he develops it further: in discussing the great transformation, Qian and Kun unite their powers; in speaking of their practical operation, the labor belongs to Earth’s thick substance, which bears all things. Why is this so?

In its movement it is firm, and in its virtue square; it gives rise to the myriad things and possesses boundless abundance. Its Way seems comparable to Qian’s. Yet yielding ease is its nature. As yin and yang rub against and stir one another, it entrusts itself to utmost compliance to accomplish its work, doing no more than assisting Qian’s movement. It embraces all things, and its transforming power shines forth; it mothers the six children—the six other trigrams—and follows its model with constancy. It seems to share Heaven’s operation. Yet occupying the lower position is its allotted station. As transformation and nurture flow forth, it disclaims possession of its mysterious achievement, doing no more than complying with Heaven’s bestowal.

When Heaven works the bellows at the inception of emergence in Zhen, is this the season of primal origination [?]? Kun immediately receives its action and moves, passing from closure to opening. For their vital energies mutually stimulate one another, and Kun arrives afterward. When Heaven stirs the intermingling energies as it first descends to aid what is below, has the time arrived? Earth then responds accordingly and opens a passage, taking what is stored within as the basis for manifestation. For their Ways depend upon one another to function, and…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
地其代終矣以一施者以兩受日新之業成于
坤而非始于坤也應時而動則有之爾以氣感
者以形禪大生之功繼乎乾而實肇乎乾也與
時偕行斯其職爾是故觀于順承天施之義而
地道舉矣觀于其道而陰陽之化尊卑之理蓋
燦然可睹也嗚呼斯其所以爲闡易之蘊歟雖
然地載神氣其即天之氣也惟其氣至而應若
承順然耳故上天下澤以明履尊天親地以明
報此乾坤之大分也非順承不可以爲坤非時
===
行不足以言順豫順以動故日月不過而四時
不忒天地且然而況於人乎故曰君命順則臣
有順命
君子藏器於身待時而動何不利之有動
而不括是以出而有獲語成器而動者
也
成子學
同考試官教諭蔣批君子崇解道而慎器與時此作
得之且瑩徹可錄
punctuated:
地其代終矣。以一施者，以兩受，日新之業成于坤，而非始于坤也；應時而動，則有之爾。以氣感者，以形禪，大生之功繼乎乾，而實肇乎乾也；與時偕行，斯其職爾。是故觀于順承天施之義，而地道舉矣；觀于其道，而陰陽之化、尊卑之理，蓋燦然可睹也。嗚呼！斯其所以爲闡易之蘊歟！雖然，地載神氣，其即天之氣也。惟其氣至而應，若承順然耳。故上天下澤以明履，尊天親地以明報，此乾坤之大分也。非順承不可以爲坤，非時行不足以言順。豫，順以動，故日月不過而四時不忒。天地且然，而況於人乎？故曰：「君命順，則臣有順命。」
君子藏器於身，待時而動，何不利之有？動而不括，是以出而有獲，語成器而動者也。
成子學
同考試官教諭蔣批：「君子崇解道而慎器與時，此作得之，且瑩徹可錄。」
translation_en:
…Earth brings things to completion on Heaven’s behalf. What the One bestows, the Two receives: the work of daily renewal is completed in Kun, Earth, but does not begin in Kun. It merely moves in response to the proper time. What acts through vital energy is carried forward through form: the achievement of bringing forth life on a grand scale is continued from Qian, Heaven, and indeed originates in Qian. To move together with the times is Earth’s appointed duty. Thus, by considering the meaning of obediently receiving Heaven’s bounty, one comprehends the Way of Earth in its entirety. By considering that Way, one can clearly behold the transformations of yin and yang and the principles governing the exalted and the lowly. Ah! Is this not how the profound meaning of the Book of Changes is elucidated? Nevertheless, the numinous vital energy borne by Earth is precisely Heaven’s vital energy. Earth responds only when that energy arrives, appearing thereby to receive it obediently. Thus, Heaven above and the marsh below illuminate Treading; revering Heaven and cherishing Earth illuminate requital. This is the great distinction between Qian and Kun. Without obedient reception, there can be no Kun; without acting at the proper time, one cannot speak adequately of obedience. In Enthusiasm, movement accords with obedience; hence the sun and moon do not deviate, and the four seasons do not err. If even Heaven and Earth act thus, how much more must human beings! Therefore it is said: “When the ruler’s commands accord with what is right, his ministers will obey them.”
“The gentleman stores his capacities within himself and waits for the proper time to act. What could fail to be advantageous? He acts without being constrained; therefore, when he goes forth, he gains something. This speaks of one who perfects his capacities before acting.”
Cheng Zixue.
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: “The gentleman esteems the Way of Release and attends carefully to his capacities and the proper time. This composition grasps that meaning; it is also lucid and merits inclusion.”

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
考試官訓導郭批〔子亦藏器待時者〕
考試官學正王批〔意完辭整〕
大傳推言解悖之利而結其意也夫除大患以
收完功固非淺妄者所能與也君子得其器與
其時矣於解悖也奚其疑大傳推言以釋解上
六爻義而結之謂夫事匪豫立固昧致用之權
動違厥時豈足以制天下之變君子人也蘊康
濟之鴻猷以除戎而圖難者畜之素矣猶必察
夫天人之會因其勢而舉之不先時以階亂挾
===
戡定之遠畧以戢威而防患者德亦周矣猶必
審夫機宜之際投其便而乘之不失時以啓侮
吾知時與器謀在我已出萬全之策智勇失其
據鬼神奪其私奚往而不利器與時會於人實
有制勝之地天祐其順人助其信奚弗利之虞
夫惟舉事括礙功斯僨矣苟動而利莫我括也
由是以克大憝則允終有濟而難可夷不猶發
彼有的而獲隼于墉乎動罔攸括孰能禦之由
是以翦元兇則尚往有功而患可殄不猶捨矢
punctuated:
考試官訓導郭批〔子亦藏器待時者。〕
考試官學正王批〔意完辭整。〕
大傳推言解悖之利而結其意也。夫除大患以收完功，固非淺妄者所能與也。君子得其器與其時矣，於解悖也奚其疑？大傳推言以釋解上六爻義而結之，謂夫事匪豫立，固昧致用之權；動違厥時，豈足以制天下之變？君子人也，蘊康濟之鴻猷，以除戎而圖難者，畜之素矣；猶必察夫天人之會，因其勢而舉之，不先時以階亂。挾戡定之遠畧，以戢威而防患者，德亦周矣；猶必審夫機宜之際，投其便而乘之，不失時以啓侮。吾知時與器謀，在我已出萬全之策，智勇失其據，鬼神奪其私，奚往而不利？器與時會，於人實有制勝之地，天祐其順，人助其信，奚弗利之虞？夫惟舉事括礙，功斯僨矣。苟動而利，莫我括也。由是以克大憝，則允終有濟，而難可夷，不猶發彼有的，而獲隼于墉乎？動罔攸括，孰能禦之？由是以翦元兇，則尚往有功，而患可殄，不猶捨矢
translation_en:
Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔You too are one who stores his abilities within himself and awaits the proper time.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning is complete, and the wording well ordered.〕
The Great Commentary develops the benefits of resolving rebellious disorder and thereby brings its meaning to a conclusion. To eliminate a great calamity and achieve complete success is certainly beyond the capacity of the shallow and reckless. When the gentleman possesses both the requisite abilities and the proper opportunity, what doubt can there be about his resolving rebellious disorder? The Great Commentary develops its account to explain the meaning of the topmost yin line of Deliverance and draws it to a conclusion. Its point is that, unless an undertaking is established beforehand, one remains ignorant of the discretionary judgment needed to put one's abilities to use; if action departs from its proper time, how can one control the changes occurring throughout the realm?
The gentleman has long nurtured within himself grand plans for bringing peace and relief, preparing to eliminate armed strife and address difficulties. Yet he must still observe the convergence of Heaven's workings and human affairs, undertaking action in accordance with their momentum, without acting prematurely and thereby giving rise to disorder. He possesses far-reaching strategies for pacification; his virtue is comprehensive in restraining the use of force and guarding against calamity. Yet he must still scrutinize the moment when circumstances favor action, seizing and making use of its advantages, without missing the proper time and thereby inviting contempt.
I know that when the time and one's abilities work together, one has already devised an entirely sound strategy: the cunning and the bold lose their foothold, and ghosts and spirits are deprived of their private designs. Wherever one proceeds, how could there be no advantage? When abilities meet their proper time, one truly has the means to secure victory. Heaven aids one's compliance with what is right, and others support one's trustworthiness. What fear need there be of an unfavorable outcome?
It is when an undertaking encounters obstruction that achievement comes to ruin. If one's action is favorable, nothing can obstruct one. If by this means one overcomes a great evildoer, one will indeed ultimately succeed, and the difficulty can be quelled. Is this not like shooting at a clearly marked target and taking the falcon upon the wall? When action meets no obstruction, who can resist it? If by this means one cuts down the chief malefactor, going forward will yield achievement, and the calamity can be eradicated. Is this not like letting fly an arrow …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
如破而禽爲我獲乎彼爻易所謂公用射隼于
高墉之上獲之無不利者亦曰上六以至高之
位居解道之極是蓋器成於已夙負寧人之望
動觀其變適當解悖之時是故成功如此其偉
也不然內焉無以豫諸已外焉而弗揆於時其
不用以罔召敗者幾希聖人奚取哉抑解而至
於上六天下之險難已解所未盡者此耳聖人
猶以藏器待時言之何也夫隼本鷙害之物而
高墉則非所宜據者蠭蠆之毒不止是也然則

嘉解道之有成而深致慎重之戒歟
