考試官學正王批開闔相照以為文
punctuated:
如破，而禽爲我獲乎？彼爻，《易》所謂「公用射隼于高墉之上，獲之，無不利」者，亦曰上六以至高之位，居解道之極，是蓋器成於已，夙負寧人之望；動觀其變，適當解悖之時，是故成功如此其偉也。不然，內焉無以豫諸已，外焉而弗揆於時，其不用以罔召敗者幾希，聖人奚取哉？抑解而至於上六，天下之險難已解，所未盡者此耳。聖人猶以藏器待時言之，何也？夫隼本鷙害之物，而高墉則非所宜據者，蠭蠆之毒不止是也。然則圖之亦難矣。復隍之喻，智者所憂。斯傳也，無亦嘉解道之有成，而深致慎重之戒歟？

書
曰若稽古帝舜，曰重華協于帝。
林光祖

同考試官教諭郝批：發出重華協帝之精思，子亦史臣之善干紀舜者。得士如此，可以慶矣。
考試官訓導郭批：詞暢意完。
考試官學正王批：開闔相照以為文。
translation_en:
…as though cleaving through, with the bird captured by us? As for that line, where the Book of Changes says, “The duke shoots a falcon atop a high wall, captures it, and nothing is unfavorable,” it means that the topmost six occupies the highest position, at the culmination of the way of Deliverance. His equipment is already prepared, and he has long borne the hopes of bringing peace to the people; he observes changes before acting and encounters precisely the moment for resolving disorder. Thus his achievement is so great. Otherwise, with no inward preparation and no outward assessment of the time, scarcely could he avoid bringing defeat upon himself [?]. What would the sage find worthy in that?

Yet when Deliverance reaches the topmost six, the dangers and difficulties of the world have already been resolved; this alone remains unfinished. Why does the sage still speak of keeping one’s equipment in readiness and awaiting the proper time? The falcon is inherently a predatory, harmful creature, and the high wall is no place for it to occupy. Its venom exceeds even that of wasps and scorpions. Devising measures against it is therefore difficult. The image of the city wall collapsing back into the moat is something the wise fear. Does this commentary not both commend the successful completion of the way of Deliverance and impart a profound warning to exercise caution?

Book of Documents
“Examining antiquity, we find Emperor Shun, called Chonghua, who accorded with the Emperor.”
Lin Guangzu

Comment by Associate Examiner Hao, Instructor: “He brings out the subtle meaning of Chonghua’s accord with the Emperor. You too are like a court historian skilled at recording Shun [?]. To obtain a scholar such as this is cause for celebration.”

Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: “The language flows freely, and the meaning is fully expressed.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The opening and closing movements illuminate one another in the composition.”

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
虞帝於唐繼離明以照臨天下也夫天不可名
堯難其繼不有重華之舜烏能紹其大哉史氏
曰吾聞之天地不絕人於莫同聖人不絕德以
孤立蓋嘗仰遡之於太古洪濛之先時則文未
開也其渾淪者無以為著又嘗俯求之於世道
升降之日時則璞已斲也其斷繹者莫之相承
夫惟唐虞際貞元之會而堯舜亶文明之君則
天至是煥乎其大闢人至是昭乎其成文矣夫
灋始於伏羲而成於堯則堯為盡制運開於太
===
初而隆於堯則堯為中數夫堯至矣極矣繼夫
堯者實難乎其為舜也抑豈知舜之同堯君臣
之所懸而合天下之所快而覩乎上下殊其分
變化比其同先後異其時參兩歸于一欽明而
光被者堯之華也文明而丕升者舜之華也竝
二代而普照民物之仰而依者皥皥然矣合兩
君而同明華夷之被而麗者炳炳然矣夫有其
華而不重光猶在於有間重其華而不恊美或
涉於罔同今則華矣而謂之重重矣而恊於一
punctuated: 虞帝於唐，繼離明以照臨天下也。夫天不可名，堯難其繼，不有重華之舜，烏能紹其大哉？史氏曰：「吾聞之，天地不絕人於莫同，聖人不絕德以孤立。蓋嘗仰遡之於太古洪濛之先，時則文未開也，其渾淪者無以為著；又嘗俯求之於世道升降之日，時則璞已斲也，其斷繹者莫之相承。夫惟唐虞際貞元之會，而堯舜亶文明之君，則天至是煥乎其大闢，人至是昭乎其成文矣。夫灋始於伏羲而成於堯，則堯為盡制；運開於太初而隆於堯，則堯為中數。夫堯至矣，極矣！繼夫堯者，實難乎其為舜也。抑豈知舜之同堯，君臣之所懸而合，天下之所快而覩乎？上下殊其分，變化比其同；先後異其時，參兩歸于一。欽明而光被者，堯之華也；文明而丕升者，舜之華也。竝二代而普照，民物之仰而依者皥皥然矣；合兩君而同明，華夷之被而麗者炳炳然矣。夫有其華而不重，光猶在於有間；重其華而不恊，美或涉於罔同。今則華矣而謂之重，重矣而恊於一，
translation_en:
The Emperor of Yu succeeded Tang, continuing his radiant brilliance to illuminate all under Heaven. Heaven cannot be adequately described; Yao was difficult to succeed. Without Shun, whose splendor renewed his predecessor’s, who could have carried on his greatness? The historian says: “I have heard that Heaven and Earth do not leave a man without a counterpart [?], nor do sages leave their virtue standing alone. I have looked back to the time before the primordial chaos of remote antiquity: cultural pattern had not yet unfolded, and what lay undifferentiated had no means of manifesting itself. I have also sought through the ages when the world’s order rose and fell: the unworked jade had already been carved, yet its broken threads [?] found no one to carry them on. Only Tang and Yu stood at the meeting of an ending and a new beginning, and Yao and Shun were truly rulers of cultivated brilliance. Thus Heaven’s radiance reached its full unfolding, and human culture attained its luminous completion. Institutions began with Fuxi and were perfected under Yao: Yao therefore brought their establishment to completion. The cycle of cosmic destiny began at the primordial beginning and flourished under Yao: Yao therefore marked its central culmination.

“Yao had reached the utmost, the very pinnacle! To succeed Yao was indeed difficult for Shun. Yet who could have known that Shun would match Yao—that ruler and minister, despite the distance between their stations, would accord, to the delighted gaze of all under Heaven? Their stations as superior and subordinate differed, but their transforming influence was alike; their times as predecessor and successor differed, but the three and the two converged in unity. Reverent and discerning, with a light that spread everywhere: such was Yao’s splendor. Cultivated and enlightened, rising to great heights: such was Shun’s splendor. The two reigns together shone everywhere, with a vast brightness to which the people and all things looked up and on which they depended. The two rulers united in a common radiance, shining brilliantly upon Chinese and non-Chinese alike, who received their light and adhered to them. If there were splendor without its renewal, the light would still suffer an interruption; if splendor were renewed without concord, their excellence might fail to agree. Now there was splendor, and it was called renewed; renewed, it accorded in unity …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
莫爲之期也而自有其會莫爲之模也而自契
其神綜其緯以爲同者天地之所以成其數也
宣其光以亮寅者二聖之所以和其衷也是蓋
相乘之機聖人不能暌之離默契之道智者無
以測其兆於是而知堯不可繼則兀而無朋非
聖也舜不能繼則企而不及非聖也觀於重華
則二聖之大見矣論者乃曰堯之世蕩蕩而無
四凶之誅舜之世赫赫而有三苗之竄噫堯君
道而爲統故可以厚其終舜臣道而爲繼故不
===
得不虞於其始噫於兹而弗異抑奚其能同
惟德惟義時乃大訓不由古訓于何其訓
柯文紹
同考試官教諭郝批經旨明而辭格不羈以式多士騁其雄弗踰其軌
考試官訓導郭批得周室敦化之意
考試官學正王批辭健而意圓
因其有而覺之因乎古而信之訓之道也夫覺
其有則易悟信以古則易從以是立教烏有外
punctuated:
莫爲之期也，而自有其會；莫爲之模也，而自契其神。綜其緯以爲同者，天地之所以成其數也；宣其光以亮寅者，二聖之所以和其衷也。是蓋相乘之機，聖人不能暌之離；默契之道，智者無以測其兆。於是而知，堯不可繼，則兀而無朋，非聖也；舜不能繼，則企而不及，非聖也。觀於重華，則二聖之大見矣。論者乃曰：「堯之世蕩蕩，而無四凶之誅；舜之世赫赫，而有三苗之竄。」噫！堯君道而爲統，故可以厚其終；舜臣道而爲繼，故不得不虞於其始。噫！於兹而弗異，抑奚其能同？
惟德惟義，時乃大訓。不由古訓，于何其訓？
柯文紹
同考試官教諭郝批：「經旨明而辭格不羈，以式多士，騁其雄弗踰其軌。」
考試官訓導郭批：「得周室敦化之意。」
考試官學正王批：「辭健而意圓。」
因其有而覺之，因乎古而信之，訓之道也。夫覺其有則易悟，信以古則易從。以是立教，烏有外
translation_en:
…No one appointed their meeting, yet they naturally converged; no one supplied a pattern, yet they spontaneously accorded in spirit. Bringing their interwoven strands into unity is how Heaven and Earth complete their allotted order; spreading their radiance in reverent mutual assistance is how the two sages harmonized their innermost purposes. Such is the working of their succession: even sages could not sunder it. Such is the way of their unspoken accord: even the wise could not discern its first signs. From this we know that, if Yao could not be succeeded, he would stand isolated and without a peer, and would not be a sage; if Shun could not succeed him, he would strain upward yet fall short, and would not be a sage. In contemplating their successive splendor, we see the greatness of both sages. Yet critics say: “Yao’s age was vast and expansive, without the punishment of the Four Malefactors; Shun’s age was sternly resplendent, and saw the banishment of the Sanmiao.” Ah! Yao followed the way of the ruler and established the ruling order, and could therefore bring his tenure to a generous conclusion. Shun followed the way of the minister and carried that order forward, and therefore had to exercise foresight at its beginning. Ah! Had they not differed in this respect, how could they have achieved their unity?
“Only virtue and righteousness: these are the great teachings. If you do not follow ancient teachings, what will you take as your teaching?”
Ke Wenshao
Comment by Associate Examiner Hao, Instructor: “The meaning of the Classic is clear, and the style is unconfined. It offers a model to the many candidates, giving full rein to its vigor without straying from the proper course.”
Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: “It captures the intent of the house of Zhou in deepening moral transformation.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The language is vigorous and the meaning fully rounded.”
To awaken people through what they already possess, and to win their trust by drawing upon antiquity: this is the way of instruction. For when what they already possess is awakened, understanding comes easily; when trust is established through antiquity, compliance comes easily. If teaching is established on this basis, how could anything lie outside …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
于乃訓者哉今夫當其可之謂時資其富之謂
基今日東郊時可以敎而基可以資有基無壞
有時無失無乃是務乎是故强之以非有則扞
格而不入暴之以無徵則苦難而不從詳立規
者蹈於佔畢之習語奧遠者犯乎陵節之施皆
非敎之善也故德者敎之範也開厥心之鑑而
使之明義者敎之則也詔寐者之名而使之寤
以蕩陵德者範以制以侈滅義者嚴其閑是以
人治人達之天下而咸中本覺爲覺通於智愚
===
===
而畢照我弗立灋以更張彼胡執迷而不復其
斯以爲天下之大訓矣乎夫德義爲訓訓之大
也不古爲訓訓之耻也故古者今之則也本其
型以爲之模而弗過先者後之規也昭其準以
爲之的而使趨檃括設而無反弛之形繩墨張
而無舛枉之弊是駕在前而繫以駒習之慣而
不亂裘爲學而通於冶事以類而漸升我弗意
見以乖方彼胡溺故而弗順其斯以爲天下之
至訓矣乎夫政有恒而訓有要徵諸古而本諸
punctuated:
于乃訓者哉？今夫當其可之謂時，資其富之謂基。今日東郊，時可以敎，而基可以資。有基無壞，有時無失，無乃是務乎？是故强之以非有，則扞格而不入；暴之以無徵，則苦難而不從。詳立規者，蹈於佔畢之習；語奧遠者，犯乎陵節之施，皆非敎之善也。故德者，敎之範也，開厥心之鑑而使之明；義者，敎之則也，詔寐者之名而使之寤。以蕩陵德者，範以制；以侈滅義者，嚴其閑。是以人治人，達之天下而咸中；本覺爲覺，通於智愚而畢照。我弗立灋以更張，彼胡執迷而不復？其斯以爲天下之大訓矣乎！

夫德義爲訓，訓之大也；不古爲訓，訓之耻也。故古者，今之則也，本其型以爲之模而弗過；先者，後之規也，昭其準以爲之的而使趨。檃括設而無反弛之形，繩墨張而無舛枉之弊。是駕在前而繫以駒，習之慣而不亂；裘爲學而通於冶，事以類而漸升。我弗意見以乖方，彼胡溺故而弗順？其斯以爲天下之至訓矣乎！夫政有恒而訓有要，徵諸古而本諸
translation_en:
…outside that instruction? Now, acting when the moment is right is called timeliness; drawing upon abundant resources is called having a foundation. Today, in the eastern suburban school, the time is fit for teaching, and the foundation offers resources to draw upon. With a foundation, let it not be ruined; with a timely opportunity, let it not be lost. Surely this is what we must attend to? Thus, if people are forced toward what they do not possess, they resist and cannot take it in; if they are assailed with what has no corroboration, they find it burdensome and difficult and will not follow. Those who lay down elaborate rules fall into the habit of merely poring over texts; those who speak of abstruse and remote matters commit the fault of teaching beyond the learner’s stage. Neither is good teaching. Thus virtue is the pattern for teaching: open the mirror of their minds and make it bright. Righteousness is the rule for teaching: call the sleeper by name [?] and awaken him. Those whose unrestrained conduct encroaches upon virtue are restrained by this pattern; for those whose extravagance extinguishes righteousness, the barriers are made strict. This is governing people through what is human: extended throughout the world, it accords with what is fitting in every case. It is awakening people on the basis of their inherent awareness: reaching both the wise and the foolish, it illuminates them all. If I do not establish new rules to alter the existing order, why should they cling to delusion and fail to return? Surely this may constitute the great instruction for all under Heaven!

To make virtue and righteousness one’s instruction is the greatness of instruction; to fail to take antiquity as instruction is its disgrace. Thus antiquity is the rule for the present: take its pattern as a model and do not exceed it. Those who came before are the standard for those who come after: make their measure clear as a target and lead others toward it. When the wood-straightening frame is set up, there are no shapes that spring back or slacken; when the inked marking line is stretched, there are no defects of crookedness or distortion. This is like having a carriage in front and tethering a colt behind it: through repeated practice, it becomes accustomed to the task and does not stray. Learning to make fur garments leads to understanding metalworking: tasks advance gradually through their similarities. If I do not depart from the proper method through private notions, why should they remain mired in old habits and fail to follow? Surely this may constitute the highest instruction for all under Heaven! Now, government has its enduring norms, and instruction its essentials: verify them against antiquity and ground them in…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
身茲周室敦化之體也卒之閑蕩侈而歸於馴
化頑側而效其順以延周祚者咸絪縕於茲而
綿絡於後也夫君道立而天下定父道立而天
下安師道立而天下化故君也者統父師之紀
而相也者代父師之任與造化相循環以位天
地以紀萬物者也或者謂世趨氣漓訓不如瀇
斯人也將胥斯世爲鬼魅其咸生人之道矣乎
凡吾人得優游於今日者誰之錫也而忍於泯
訓化之功
===
詩
九月築場圃十月納禾稼黍稷重穋禾麻
菽麥嗟我農夫我稼旣同上入執宫功
晝爾于茅宵爾索綯亟其乘屋其始播
百穀
何用行
同考試官教諭陳 批 隱括成文簡勁閒雅宛然豳俗
在目
同考試官教諭林 批 說出豳俗憂勤艱難之意而規
punctuated:
身，茲周室敦化之體也。卒之閑蕩侈而歸於馴，化頑側而效其順，以延周祚者，咸絪縕於茲而綿絡於後也。夫君道立而天下定，父道立而天下安，師道立而天下化。故君也者，統父師之紀，而相也者，代父師之任，與造化相循環，以位天地，以紀萬物者也。或者謂世趨氣漓，訓不如瀇，斯人也，將胥斯世爲鬼魅，其咸生人之道矣乎？凡吾人得優游於今日者，誰之錫也？而忍於泯訓化之功！

詩

九月築場圃，十月納禾稼。黍稷重穋，禾麻菽麥。嗟我農夫，我稼旣同，上入執宫功。晝爾于茅，宵爾索綯。亟其乘屋，其始播百穀。

何用行

同考試官教諭陳批：隱括成文，簡勁閒雅，宛然豳俗在目。

同考試官教諭林批：說出豳俗憂勤艱難之意，而規
translation_en:
…in oneself: this was the foundation of the Zhou royal house’s deepening of moral transformation. Ultimately, restraining extravagance and excess and bringing people to docility, transforming the obstinate and wayward and securing their obedience—all that prolonged Zhou’s dynastic fortune was interwoven here and continued into later generations. When the way of the ruler is established, all under Heaven is settled; when the way of the father is established, all under Heaven is at peace; when the way of the teacher is established, all under Heaven is transformed. Thus the ruler unites the guiding principles of father and teacher, while the chief minister discharges their responsibilities on his behalf. Together they participate in the cycles of creation and transformation, placing Heaven and Earth in their proper positions and ordering the myriad things. Some say that the tendencies of the age have grown shallow and that instruction is inferior to expansiveness [?]. Such people would turn this entire world into ghosts and demons: could this be the way to sustain all living people [?]? Whose gift enables us to live at ease today? How could we bear to efface the achievements of instruction and transformation!

Book of Odes

“In the ninth month we prepare the threshing ground and garden;
in the tenth month we bring in the crops:
broomcorn millet and foxtail millet, late-ripening and early-ripening grain,
grain and hemp, beans and wheat.
Ah, we farmers!
Our crops have all been gathered;
we go up to undertake work on the lord’s buildings.
By day you gather thatching grass;
by night you twist ropes.
Hurry up onto the roofs to repair them,
for soon you must begin sowing the hundred grains.”

He Yongxing

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “He has fashioned a composition by drawing together the substance of the passage. Concise and vigorous, poised and elegant, it brings the customs of Bin vividly before one’s eyes.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “He brings out the anxiety, diligence, and hardship embodied in the customs of Bin, while the formal structure…”

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
格整重詞語儁燁可以爲文矣
考試官訓導郭批意純而氣昌
考試官學正王批簡明而雅
豳人自叙其終始之憂勤而力本之意篤矣夫
因終而慮始豳人之計豫也然則烏可一日而
忘農哉昔周公以成王未知稼穡艱難故陳后
稷公劉風化之由以教之意謂農者我周開國
之基而豳者後王作則之地王其曷觀之乎時
維九月物則成矣圃可爲場也則先時而築焉
===
時維十月禾則穫矣場以受禾也則自田而納
焉黍稷重穋廣其入也禾麻菽麥異其種也嗟
我農夫稼則無不聚矣然而久於外也都邑之
室能無壞乎以休勤恤以樂盈寧宮功之執兹
其時也不然則民力不堪其皆入室而奠麗之
計疎豈可遂謂之無事哉然豳人之志則遠矣
晝而取茅于野以備覆蓋無怠朝也夜而綯索
于室以預葺治無怠夕也日夜以計其功經營
以恊其力率我農夫所以若是其亟者不曰時
punctuated:
格整重，詞語儁燁，可以爲文矣。
考試官訓導郭批：意純而氣昌。
考試官學正王批：簡明而雅。
豳人自叙其終始之憂勤，而力本之意篤矣。夫因終而慮始，豳人之計豫也。然則烏可一日而忘農哉？昔周公以成王未知稼穡艱難，故陳后稷公劉風化之由以教之，意謂農者我周開國之基，而豳者後王作則之地，王其曷觀之乎？時維九月，物則成矣，圃可爲場也，則先時而築焉。時維十月，禾則穫矣，場以受禾也，則自田而納焉。黍稷重穋，廣其入也；禾麻菽麥，異其種也。嗟我農夫，稼則無不聚矣。然而久於外也，都邑之室能無壞乎？以休勤恤，以樂盈寧，宮功之執，兹其時也。不然則民力不堪，其皆入室而奠麗之計疎，豈可遂謂之無事哉？然豳人之志則遠矣。晝而取茅于野，以備覆蓋，無怠朝也；夜而綯索于室，以預葺治，無怠夕也。日夜以計其功，經營以恊其力，率我農夫，所以若是其亟者，不曰時

…the composition is orderly and dignified, its language outstanding and brilliant: this may indeed be called accomplished writing.
Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor, comments: “The ideas are pure and the vital force abundant.”
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “Concise, clear, and elegant.”
The people of Bin themselves recount their cares and labors from end to beginning, revealing their deep commitment to agriculture, the fundamental occupation. In considering the beginning as they reach the end, the people of Bin plan ahead. How, then, could they forget farming for even a single day? Long ago, because King Cheng did not yet understand the hardships of sowing and reaping, the Duke of Zhou instructed him by explaining the origins of the civilizing influence of Hou Ji and Gong Liu. His meaning was this: agriculture was the foundation upon which our Zhou established its state, and Bin was the place from which later kings should take their model. Why should the king not look to it?
In the ninth month, the crops have ripened. The vegetable garden can serve as a threshing ground, so they prepare and tamp it beforehand. In the tenth month, the grain has been harvested. The threshing ground receives it, so they bring it in from the fields. Broomcorn millet, foxtail millet, and late- and early-ripening grain make their harvest plentiful; grain, hemp, beans, and wheat provide a variety of crops. Ah, our farmers! All their crops have now been gathered. Yet they have long been working outside: could their houses in the settlements have escaped deterioration? To give respite from toil and care, and to enjoy abundance and peace [?], this is the time to undertake work on their dwellings. Otherwise, the people's strength will fail, and arrangements for everyone to return indoors and settle into their homes will be inadequate. How could one then say that nothing remains to be done?
Yet the people of Bin look far ahead. By day they gather thatch in the fields to prepare roofing, allowing themselves no idleness in the morning. At night they twist ropes indoors in readiness for repairs, allowing themselves no idleness in the evening. title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
不可失乎獻歲發春農事始矣以迎氣於天以
分利於地百穀之播又其時也不然則脉其滿
青穀乃不殖而厚生之道匱雖欲治屋固有所
不暇矣吁慮之豫而曲盡其宜趨之亟而不懈
於力豳人終始不忘於農微先公之化其誰爲
之吾王可以思矣嗟乎天下之機繫於人主之
一心是故人主知農事則知保民知保民則知
敬天不知則肆肆則無畏以易視其民而天亦
棄之故民者國之榦也農者民之命也善守國
===
者務先於察民之情而從其欲是故民悅而國
安身尊而名顯故曰人情者聖王之田也其斯
以爲七月之義乎
夜如何其夜未央庭燎之光君子至止鸞
聲將將
盧夢陽
同考試官敎諭陳批〔文有識而思益深詞不費而理〕
〔愈微〕
同考試官敎諭林批〔旨明而辭暢文瑩而思深良結〕
punctuated:
不可失乎？獻歲發春，農事始矣。以迎氣於天，以分利於地，百穀之播，又其時也。不然，則脉其滿青，穀乃不殖，而厚生之道匱，雖欲治屋，固有所不暇矣。吁！慮之豫而曲盡其宜，趨之亟而不懈於力，豳人終始不忘於農。微先公之化，其誰爲之？吾王可以思矣。嗟乎！天下之機，繫於人主之一心。是故人主知農事，則知保民；知保民，則知敬天。不知則肆，肆則無畏，以易視其民，而天亦棄之。故民者，國之榦也；農者，民之命也。善守國者，務先於察民之情而從其欲。是故民悅而國安，身尊而名顯。故曰：「人情者，聖王之田也。」其斯以爲《七月》之義乎？

夜如何其？夜未央。庭燎之光，君子至止，鸞聲將將。

盧夢陽

同考試官敎諭陳批〔文有識而思益深，詞不費而理〕〔愈微。〕

同考試官敎諭林批〔旨明而辭暢，文瑩而思深，良結〕
translation_en:
…must not be missed? As the year opens and spring begins, farming commences. To welcome Heaven’s seasonal energies and draw benefit from the earth, this again is the time to sow the many grains. Otherwise, the earth’s veins are full of green growth [?], yet the grain does not grow, and the means of sustaining life become deficient. Even if people wished to repair their houses, they would surely have no leisure for it. Ah! They planned beforehand, attending fully to every appropriate measure; they hastened to their tasks, never slackening in their exertions. The people of Bin never forgot farming, from beginning to end. Without the transforming influence of the former lords, who could have brought this about? Our king may well reflect upon this. Alas! The workings of the realm depend upon the ruler’s single heart. Thus, if the ruler understands farming, he understands how to protect the people; if he understands how to protect the people, he understands how to revere Heaven. Without this understanding, he becomes unrestrained; unrestrained, he fears nothing and regards his people lightly, and Heaven, too, abandons him. The people are the trunk of the state, and farming is the lifeblood of the people. One who preserves the state well must first attend to discerning the people’s circumstances and complying with their desires. Thus the people are content and the state secure; the ruler’s person is honored and his reputation illustrious. Hence the saying: “Human feelings are the sage king’s field.” Is this, then, the meaning of “The Seventh Month”?

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
有規警可錄
考試官訓導郭批善状周王無逸之心
考試官學正王批儆切
周王審時而急於視朝可以見其無逸之心矣
夫君人者心乎無逸則朝不踰節而事不廢紀
茲其所以崇大業者乎昔有周王者將視朝而
問夜之早晩曰嚮明而治哲王之經也坐旦而
思理化之原也毋曰予一人正位凝命天視之
以厚薄其德毋曰一日二日代天理物民視之
===
以明威其治苟幾康之弗戒則理忽之攸繫今
夜如何其意者夜猶未央乎顧庭燎者司烜設
之以視朝者也乃今大庭則已炎百枚之束而
炳乎其光矣宵衣以待猶曰未遑而我尚可以
自佚耶彼和鸞者諸侯乘之以侍朝者也乃今
君子則已播鸞聲之和而將然其至止矣辨色
以入厥有常度而我獨可以弗興耶以序旅揖
以稽復逆以廣訪聽以陳謨功如其佚樂之志
耽而兢業之道懈天下其謂我何哉吁王之心
punctuated:
有規警，可錄。
考試官訓導郭批：善状周王無逸之心。
考試官學正王批：儆切。
周王審時而急於視朝，可以見其無逸之心矣。夫君人者心乎無逸，則朝不踰節，而事不廢紀，茲其所以崇大業者乎！昔有周王者，將視朝而問夜之早晩，曰：「嚮明而治，哲王之經也；坐旦而思，理化之原也。毋曰予一人，正位凝命，天視之以厚薄其德；毋曰一日二日，代天理物，民視之以明威其治。苟幾康之弗戒，則理忽之攸繫。今夜如何其？意者夜猶未央乎？顧庭燎者，司烜設之以視朝者也。乃今大庭則已炎百枚之束，而炳乎其光矣。宵衣以待，猶曰未遑，而我尚可以自佚耶？彼和鸞者，諸侯乘之以侍朝者也。乃今君子則已播鸞聲之和，而將然其至止矣。辨色以入，厥有常度，而我獨可以弗興耶？以序旅揖，以稽復逆，以廣訪聽，以陳謨功。如其佚樂之志耽，而兢業之道懈，天下其謂我何哉？」吁！王之心

…It offers admonition and warning, and merits inclusion.
Examiner Guo, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “It well portrays the king of Zhou’s resolve to shun ease.”
Examiner Wang, an Instructor, comments: “A pointed admonition.”
The king of Zhou ascertained the hour and was eager to hold court: in this we can see his resolve to shun ease. When one who rules others sets his heart on shunning ease, court audiences do not exceed their appointed times, and affairs do not lapse into disorder. Is this not how he advances his great undertaking?
Once a king of Zhou, about to hold court, asked how far the night had progressed, saying: “To attend to government as daylight approaches is the constant practice of wise kings; to sit awaiting dawn in contemplation is the source of good government and moral transformation. Do not say, ‘I am but one man’: in occupying the proper position and securing Heaven’s mandate, Heaven watches him to judge the depth or shallowness of his virtue. Do not say, ‘It is only a day or two’: in ordering affairs on Heaven’s behalf, the people watch him to judge the clarity and majesty of his government [?]. Whether order or disorder follows hinges on vigilance against complacency in peace [?].
“What hour of the night is it now? Perhaps the night has not yet reached its midpoint? Consider the courtyard torches: the Director of Fire Services sets them out for the court audience. Yet now, in the great courtyard, bundles of a hundred stalks have already been set alight and blaze brightly. Even dressing before dawn and waiting might still be deemed insufficiently diligent; can I yet indulge in ease? Those carriage bells—the feudal lords ride with them when coming to attend court. Now the noble men have already sent forth the harmonious sound of their bells, arriving with a ringing clang. There is a fixed rule that they enter when the light permits colors to be distinguished; can I alone fail to rise?
“There are ranks to observe in exchanging bows with the assembled lords, reports and submissions to examine, inquiries and hearings to broaden, and plans and achievements to set forth. If I were to indulge a desire for ease and pleasure and slacken in vigilance and diligence, what would all under Heaven say of me?”

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
亦勤矣此其成精明之治弘文武之烈理道休
隆而聲稱長美也易曰天行健君子以自强不
息夫天以健運故萬物咸軌而靡亂君以不息
爲健故萬化常張而弗弛是故君也者天道也
故凡君之所恃以爲權者而皆繫之天若曰有
一息之怠乘其間卽與天違則百職墮而天下
棄周王何其之訪其有得於此耶以此爲訓後
世猶有宵衣之諷旬日一朝之典者
春秋
===
大雩〔桓公五年〕秋八月壬午大閱〔桓公六年〕
何右之
同考試官學正黃 批 春秋之法杜微防漸是作引禮
以斷之道名分之意凜然不獨取其文也
考試官訓導郭 批 有斷制
考試官學正王 批 整密
春秋於望國始因事而志其吉禮之僭繼因事
而志其軍禮之僭觀我魯大雩大閱之書而聖
人道名分之意昭矣且魯桓胡爲而大雩也因
punctuated:
亦勤矣！此其成精明之治，弘文武之烈，理道休隆，而聲稱長美也。《易》曰：「天行健，君子以自强不息。」夫天以健運，故萬物咸軌而靡亂；君以不息爲健，故萬化常張而弗弛。是故君也者，天道也。故凡君之所恃以爲權者，而皆繫之天。若曰有一息之怠乘其間，卽與天違，則百職墮而天下棄。周王何其之訪，其有得於此耶？以此爲訓，後世猶有宵衣之諷、旬日一朝之典者。

春秋

大雩〔桓公五年〕。秋八月壬午，大閱〔桓公六年〕。

何右之

同考試官學正黃批：「春秋之法，杜微防漸。是作引禮以斷之，道名分之意凜然，不獨取其文也。」
考試官訓導郭批：「有斷制。」
考試官學正王批：「整密。」

春秋於望國，始因事而志其吉禮之僭，繼因事而志其軍禮之僭。觀我魯大雩、大閱之書，而聖人道名分之意昭矣。且魯桓胡爲而大雩也？因
translation_en:
…was indeed diligent! Thus he achieved enlightened government and extended the glorious accomplishments of Kings Wen and Wu; the way of government flourished, and his reputation remained illustrious. The Book of Changes says: “Heaven moves with vigor; the gentleman accordingly strengthens himself without cease.” Because Heaven moves vigorously, all things follow their proper courses without disorder. Because the ruler takes unceasing effort as his vigor, the myriad processes of transformation remain active and never slacken. Thus, being a ruler embodies the Way of Heaven. Everything upon which the ruler relies for his authority is therefore bound to Heaven. Should even a moment’s indolence intervene, he would depart from Heaven: the hundred offices would fall into neglect, and all under Heaven would abandon him. In asking how far the night had advanced, had the king of Zhou perhaps grasped this principle? With this as an admonition, later ages nevertheless still had remonstrances urging rulers to dress before dawn, and established practices of holding court only once in ten days.

He Youzhi

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
旱暵之爲虐也夫春秋於歲事之常不書此胡
書而特謂之大蓋嘗攷之王制天子祭天地名
山大川五嶽四瀆於是乎用盛樂以和神人若
諸侯惟祭社稷雩境内之山川焉爾夫何桓也
不雩山川而雩上帝不用歌舞而用盛樂壇壝
昭五方之臨金石協八音之奏彼固曰鬱鬯以
迎神祝嘏以受釐燔柴以通氣我能饗帝矣曾
何思皇皇后帝不歆非祀可以僭事之乎吾見
越席疏布昭其瀆也腥醴孰醗昭其褻也是果
===
禱旱祈天降澤承祐之道哉故經於雩祭不書
此則因旱暵以書而特曰大用見非天子而僭
天子之祀其何以尊上帝也魯桓又胡爲而大
閲也懼齊鄭以講武也夫春秋於時事之常不
書此胡書而亦謂之大蓋嘗攷之周制王執路
鼓旗載太常殺下大綏於是乎教衆庶以脩戰
灋若諸侯則執賁鼓載旂與小綏焉爾夫何桓
也舍賁鼓而執路鼓載太常而下大綏物采違
五等之儀降殺同一王之制彼固曰鼓鐸鐲鐃
punctuated:
旱暵之爲虐也。夫《春秋》於歲事之常不書，此胡書而特謂之大？蓋嘗攷之《王制》，天子祭天地、名山大川、五嶽四瀆，於是乎用盛樂以和神人；若諸侯，惟祭社稷，雩境内之山川焉爾。夫何桓也，不雩山川而雩上帝，不用歌舞而用盛樂？壇壝昭五方之臨，金石協八音之奏。彼固曰：「鬱鬯以迎神，祝嘏以受釐，燔柴以通氣，我能饗帝矣。」曾何思皇皇后帝不歆非祀，可以僭事之乎？吾見越席疏布，昭其瀆也；腥醴孰醗，昭其褻也。是果禱旱祈天、降澤承祐之道哉？故經於雩祭不書，此則因旱暵以書，而特曰大，用見非天子而僭天子之祀，其何以尊上帝也？

魯桓又胡爲而大閲也？懼齊鄭以講武也。夫《春秋》於時事之常不書，此胡書而亦謂之大？蓋嘗攷之周制，王執路鼓，旗載太常，殺下大綏，於是乎教衆庶以脩戰灋；若諸侯，則執賁鼓，載旂與小綏焉爾。夫何桓也，舍賁鼓而執路鼓，載太常而下大綏？物采違五等之儀，降殺同一王之制。彼固曰：「鼓鐸鐲鐃
translation_en:
…because drought was wreaking havoc. Now the Spring and Autumn Annals does not record routine events of the agricultural year. Why does it record this one, and specifically call it “great”? I have examined the Royal Regulations: the Son of Heaven sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, to famous mountains and great rivers, and to the Five Sacred Peaks and Four Waterways. For these occasions he employs grand music to bring spirits and people into harmony. The feudal lords, however, sacrifice only to the gods of soil and grain and perform rain sacrifices to the mountains and rivers within their territories. Why, then, did Duke Huan perform a rain sacrifice to the Supreme Lord instead of to mountains and rivers, and employ grand music instead of song and dance? His altar and its enclosure displayed the presence of the deities of the five directions; bells and sounding stones harmonized the performance of the eight classes of instruments. He surely said: “With aromatic sacrificial wine I welcome the spirits; through invocations and blessings I receive good fortune; by burning wood I convey the sacrificial vapors. I can offer a feast to the Supreme Lord!” Yet did he ever consider that the august Supreme Lord accepts no sacrifice improperly offered? Could he serve the deity by usurping rites? I see that the rush mats and coarse cloth reveal his irreverence, and the raw offerings, sweet wine, cooked offerings, and fermented drink [?] reveal his desecration. Is this truly the way to pray during drought and petition Heaven, to obtain rain and receive divine aid? Thus, although the Classic does not record ordinary rain sacrifices, it records this one because of the drought and specifically calls it “great.” This shows that someone who was not the Son of Heaven usurped the Son of Heaven’s sacrifices. How could he thereby honor the Supreme Lord?

Why, again, did Duke Huan of Lu hold a great military review? He feared Qi and Zheng and therefore conducted military exercises. Now the Spring and Autumn Annals does not record routine seasonal affairs. Why does it record this one and likewise call it “great”? I have examined the institutions of Zhou: the king uses the great drum, mounts the Great Constant banner, and lowers the great pennant [?]; with these he instructs the multitude in the practice of warfare. The feudal lords, however, use the ben drum and mount the dragon banner and small pennant only. Why, then, did Duke Huan discard the ben drum and use the great drum, mount the Great Constant banner, and lower the great pennant? His insignia and colors violated the ceremonial distinctions of the five ranks of nobility; in their gradations, they matched the regulations for the sole king. He surely said: “Drums, clapper bells, marching bells, and stopping bells…”

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之以次旗表車徒之以規坐作進退之以節我
能訓民矣曾何思林林烝徒不順非禮可以僭

之文矣乎抑桓之僭非桓也然則孰僭之曰成

文公十四年
何大章
同考試官學正黃 批 改過知幾皆賢所難子能發一
punctuated:
之以次，旗表車徒之以規，坐作進退之以節，我能訓民矣。曾何思林林烝徒，不順非禮，可以僭示之乎？况夫不於農隙，刺非時也；不因田狩，刺失政也。夫豈制治保邦、綢繆牖戶之意哉？故經於閱武不書，此則因不時以書，而亦曰大，用見非王者而僭王者之政，其何以平邦國也？吁！戎祀，有國之大事；君臣，天下之大典。春秋於魯之雩閱而兩致譏焉，正名敦典，裁自聖心，其性命之文矣乎！抑桓之僭，非桓也。然則孰僭之？曰：「成王之賜、伯禽之受，皆非也。」夫周公制禮作樂，將欲傳之萬世，而壞之自伯禽始，公之心其康乎？故曰：「周公其衰矣！」厥後季氏旅泰山，歌雍徹，而于紅、比蒲、昌閒之三蒐，非時非地，肆爾無忌，其所由來亦漸矣。是故孔子懼而作春秋。

文公十四年。
何大章。

translation_en:
…ordering them in sequence, regulating chariots and foot soldiers with flags and markers, and giving measured signals for sitting and rising, advancing and withdrawing: ‘I can train the people!’ Did he never consider that the countless multitudes will not submit to what violates ritual propriety? Could he instruct them through a display of usurpation? Moreover, to hold it outside the intervals of agricultural leisure invited criticism for improper timing; to conduct it apart from a hunting expedition invited criticism for faulty governance. How could this express the intention of establishing order, safeguarding the state, and securing doors and windows against future danger? Thus the Classic does not ordinarily record military reviews. It records this one because it was untimely, and also calls it ‘great,’ thereby showing that one who was not a king had usurped royal prerogatives in government. How could he thereby bring peace to the states?
Alas! Warfare and sacrifice are great affairs of a state; the relationship between ruler and minister is a fundamental institution of all under Heaven. In its treatment of Lu’s rain sacrifice and military review, the Spring and Autumn Annals censures both. It rectifies names and upholds fundamental institutions, its judgments issuing from the sage’s mind. Is this not a text expressing human nature and Heaven’s mandate? Yet Duke Huan’s usurpation did not originate with Huan. Who, then, initiated it? The answer is: ‘King Cheng’s granting these privileges and Bo Qin’s accepting them were both wrong.’ When the Duke of Zhou established rites and created music, he intended to transmit them for ten thousand generations; yet their destruction began with Bo Qin. Could the duke’s heart have been at ease? Hence the saying: ‘How the Duke of Zhou has declined!’ Thereafter, the Ji lineage offered sacrifice to Mount Tai and sang the Yong hymn while removing the sacrificial vessels. The three hunting assemblies at Hong, Bipu, and Changjian were held at improper times and places, with unrestrained disregard for propriety. The circumstances giving rise to these abuses had developed gradually. Thus Confucius became apprehensive and composed the Spring and Autumn Annals.

Fourteenth year of Duke Wen.
He Dazhang.

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
字之褒于盾衮□其不朽矣是知史法者
考試官訓導郭批〔得聖人與善之公〕
考試官學正王批〔謹嚴〕
聖人脩經有因其徙義而予之者有因其存道
而貴之者夫春秋大改過嘉知幾者也茲其有
取於盾哀乎甞攷趙盾將兵納捷菑也置君非
義經固人之而書弗克納謂予之也予之也何
蓋君子非有過之患而勿憚改之難彼趙盾因
邾文之不祿援捷菑以求復奉少奪長是謂犯
===
順犯順弗悛果於力勝能免怙終之咎乎今也
方聞齊出獳且長之辭遂有義實不爾克之訟
引師謝慝皇皇然猶恐不及是改過有風雷之
迅而遷善同日月之明吾於易見乘墉之象焉
於書見吝過之儆焉昔秦穆自誓垂諸百篇之
末盾其有得於是乎春秋特書弗克納若曰有
過知悔悔過勿貳可謂難也已乃若稱人則諱
之傳謂外以諱爲善非歟載攷高哀來奔縁宋
亂也避難非夫經宜名之而特書其字謂貴之
punctuated:
字之褒于盾，衮□其不朽矣！是知史法者。
考試官訓導郭批〔得聖人與善之公〕
考試官學正王批〔謹嚴〕
聖人脩經，有因其徙義而予之者，有因其存道而貴之者。夫春秋大改過、嘉知幾者也，茲其有取於盾、哀乎？甞攷趙盾將兵納捷菑也，置君非義，經固人之；而書「弗克納」，謂予之也。予之也何？蓋君子非有過之患，而勿憚改之難。彼趙盾因邾文之不祿，援捷菑以求復，奉少奪長，是謂犯順。犯順弗悛，果於力勝，能免怙終之咎乎？今也，方聞「齊出獳且長」之辭，遂有「義實不爾克」之訟，引師謝慝，皇皇然猶恐不及。是改過有風雷之迅，而遷善同日月之明。吾於《易》見乘墉之象焉，於《書》見吝過之儆焉。昔秦穆自誓，垂諸百篇之末，盾其有得於是乎？春秋特書「弗克納」，若曰：「有過知悔，悔過勿貳，可謂難也已。」乃若稱人，則諱之，傳謂「外以諱爲善」，非歟？載攷高哀來奔，縁宋亂也。避難非夫，經宜名之，而特書其字，謂貴之
translation_en:
…the praise conferred on Dun by a single word: the ceremonial robe □ will surely endure forever [?]! This is someone who understands the methods of historical writing.
Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Captures the sage’s impartiality in approving goodness.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: 〔Careful and rigorous.〕
When the sage edited the Classic, there were those whom he approved because they turned toward righteousness, and those whom he honored because they preserved the Way. The Spring and Autumn Annals esteems the correction of faults and commends discernment of the first signs of events. Is this why it finds merit in Dun and Ai?
I have examined how Zhao Dun led troops to install Jiezi. Installing a ruler was contrary to righteousness, so the Classic indeed referred to him merely as a “man.” Yet its wording, “failed to install him,” signifies approval. Why approval? For the gentleman, the difficulty lies not in having faults to worry about, but in correcting them without hesitation. Zhao Dun took advantage of the death of Duke Wen of Zhu to support Jiezi’s return. Upholding the younger and dispossessing the elder was a violation of the proper order. Had he persisted in that violation without repenting, determined to prevail by force, could he have escaped blame for obstinately continuing in wrongdoing?
Instead, as soon as he heard the statement, “Nou was born of the woman from Qi and is also the elder,” he acknowledged, “In righteousness, we truly cannot prevail against you.” He withdrew his army and renounced his wrongdoing, anxiously fearing that he might be too late. Thus his correction of his fault was as swift as wind and thunder, and his turning toward goodness as bright as the sun and moon. In the Book of Changes, I see here the image of mounting a wall; in the Book of Documents, I see the warning against being reluctant to acknowledge faults. Long ago, Duke Mu of Qin made his own solemn declaration, preserved at the end of the hundred chapters. Had Dun grasped something of its meaning? The Spring and Autumn Annals specifically writes “failed to install him,” as though saying: “To recognize and regret a fault, and, having repented, never repeat it—this may indeed be called difficult.” As for referring to him merely as a “man,” this conceals his identity. Does not the Commentary say, “For those outside our state, concealment is treated as a good thing”?
I have also examined Gao Ai’s coming to seek refuge: this arose from disorder in Song. Fleeing danger is unworthy of a man, so the Classic ought to have recorded his personal name; instead, it specifically recorded his courtesy name, signifying that it honored him…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也貴之也何蓋君子非避禍之喜而預遠亂之
難彼高哀當宋昭之無道蕭封人以為卿逆亂
未萌孰不欲仕溺仕階禍禍蔓難圖得無陷阱
之虞乎今也耻非君而不事遂接淅以如魯潔
身高蹈望望然若將浼焉是先時有决蹈之智
而臨事無濡尾之凶吾於易見貞吉之幾焉於
詩見明哲之訓焉昔微子去紂列於三仁之首
哀不庶幾於此乎春秋特書其字若曰危邦不
入亂邦不居可謂明也已是故不稱名以别之
===
傳謂獨取其去而褒之者是矣吁予趙盾則人
知文過遂非之當戒貴子哀則人知蚤見預待
之為賢夫然後處仁遷義者有所灋而忘身殉
禄者有所警矣聖人垂訓之義大矣哉雖然盾
固可予也異日縱穿侵崇以發桃園之大難誰
實尸之哀固可貴也然猶有不眀去就從違之
義坐待其斃甘同匹夫匹婦之經於溝瀆而不
得與死職比者是亦子哀之罪人也已故以趙
盾論則不可以一事蓋一人以子哀論雖謂百
punctuated:
也。貴之也何？蓋君子非避禍之喜，而預遠亂之難。彼高哀當宋昭之無道，蕭封人以為卿，逆亂未萌，孰不欲仕？溺仕階禍，禍蔓難圖，得無陷阱之虞乎？今也耻非君而不事，遂接淅以如魯，潔身高蹈，望望然若將浼焉。是先時有决蹈之智，而臨事無濡尾之凶。吾於易見貞吉之幾焉，於詩見明哲之訓焉。昔微子去紂，列於三仁之首，哀不庶幾於此乎？春秋特書其字，若曰危邦不入，亂邦不居，可謂明也已。是故不稱名以别之。傳謂獨取其去而褒之者，是矣。
吁！予趙盾，則人知文過遂非之當戒；貴子哀，則人知蚤見預待之為賢。夫然後處仁遷義者有所灋，而忘身殉禄者有所警矣。聖人垂訓之義大矣哉！雖然，盾固可予也，異日縱穿侵崇，以發桃園之大難，誰實尸之？哀固可貴也，然猶有不眀去就從違之義，坐待其斃，甘同匹夫匹婦之經於溝瀆，而不得與死職比者，是亦子哀之罪人也已。故以趙盾論，則不可以一事蓋一人；以子哀論，雖謂百
translation_en:
…Why does it honor him? Because what the gentleman values is not the pleasure of escaping calamity, but the difficulty of distancing oneself from disorder beforehand. Gao Ai lived under the unprincipled rule of Duke Zhao of Song, when the keeper of the frontier at Xiao was made a minister. Before rebellion and disorder had begun to emerge, who would not have wished to hold office? Yet absorption in office invites calamity; once calamity spreads, it is difficult to counter. Would there not be reason to fear falling into a trap? Gao Ai, ashamed to serve an unworthy ruler, refused service. He gathered up his rice while it was still being rinsed and departed for Lu, keeping himself unsullied and withdrawing above worldly entanglements. He looked back anxiously, as though fearing contamination. Thus, before events unfolded, he possessed the wisdom to act decisively [?]; when the crisis came, he avoided the misfortune of wetting his tail. In the Book of Changes I see the subtle indications of good fortune through steadfast correctness; in the Book of Odes, the teaching of clear understanding and wisdom. In antiquity, Weizi left Zhou and was ranked first among the three benevolent men. Did Gao Ai not come close to this? The Spring and Autumn Annals expressly records his courtesy name, as if to say: “Do not enter an endangered state; do not remain in a disordered state.” He may indeed be called discerning. It therefore distinguishes him by not using his personal name. The Commentary is correct in saying that it singles out his departure alone for praise.
Ah! By approving Zhao Dun, it teaches people to guard against glossing over their faults and persisting in wrongdoing; by honoring Zi Ai, it teaches them the worth of early discernment and advance preparedness. Only then do those who abide in benevolence and move toward righteousness have a model to follow, while those who sacrifice themselves for their stipends have a warning. How great is the significance of the sage’s instruction for posterity! Nevertheless, although Dun certainly merits approval, who was actually responsible when, on a later occasion, he allowed Chuan to invade Chong, thereby precipitating the great calamity at the Peach Garden? Ai certainly merits honor. Yet there are still those who fail to understand the principles governing withdrawal and acceptance of office, compliance and refusal. They sit awaiting their destruction, willingly meeting the same fate as ordinary men and women who hang themselves in ditches, and cannot be compared with those who die in the discharge of their duties. Such people are also offenders against the example of Zi Ai. Thus, in judging Zhao Dun, one cannot let a single deed stand for the whole man; in judging Zi Ai, even to call him a teacher for a hundred …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
世之師也亦宜
禮記
凡官民材必先論之論辨然後使之任事
然後爵之位定然後禄之爵人於朝與
士共之
吳日乙
同考試官教諭王批此作深得先王官人之意百代
之下易簡可行子可語政矣
考試官訓導郭批詞氣古雅
===
考試官學正王批明淨
先王官人惟慎序而布公也蓋序則舉用審公
則好惡明先王之世無昵官矣王制之㫖謂夫
惟爵與賞天所命也非人得而專者則於鄉士
之旣造而入官之伊始也可無慎乎何則進弗
以序則不才者或得以倖進先王于是以辨論
爲先權衡懸而考覈當必其行藝之足取而後
器以使之授之以庶務政事脩而績效彰因其
職任之克勝而後爵以詔之加之以一命位旣
punctuated:
世之師也，亦宜。

禮記

凡官民材，必先論之；論辨，然後使之；任事，然後爵之；位定，然後禄之。爵人於朝，與士共之。

吳日乙

同考試官教諭王批：此作深得先王官人之意，百代之下，易簡可行，子可語政矣。

考試官訓導郭批：詞氣古雅。

考試官學正王批：明淨。

先王官人，惟慎序而布公也。蓋序則舉用審，公則好惡明，先王之世無昵官矣。《王制》之㫖，謂夫惟爵與賞，天所命也，非人得而專者。則於鄉士之旣造，而入官之伊始也，可無慎乎？何則？進弗以序，則不才者或得以倖進。先王于是以辨論爲先，權衡懸而考覈當，必其行藝之足取，而後器以使之，授之以庶務；政事脩而績效彰，因其職任之克勝，而後爵以詔之，加之以一命。位旣
translation_en:
…it is also fitting to call him a teacher for a hundred generations.

Record of Rites

“Whenever appointing talented people to office, one must first assess them. Only after assessment has distinguished their abilities should they be employed; only after they have undertaken duties should they receive rank; only after their positions are settled should they receive stipends. Confer rank upon men at court, sharing the decision with the officers.”

Wu Riyi

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “This composition deeply grasps the former kings’ intention in appointing officials. Even a hundred generations later, its principles are simple and readily practicable. You are someone with whom government can be discussed.”

Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: “The diction and tone are antique and elegant.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, School Instructor: “Clear and clean.”

In appointing officials, the former kings took particular care to follow the proper sequence and act impartially. Following the proper sequence ensured careful selection and employment; impartiality made clear the grounds for approval and disapproval. In the age of the former kings, no one held office through favoritism. The purport of “Royal Regulations” is that ranks and rewards are ordained by Heaven and are not things that any person may monopolize. Thus, when scholars from the local communities had completed their training and were first entering official service, could one fail to exercise care? Why is this so? If advancement does not follow the proper sequence, men without ability may sometimes gain promotion through luck. The former kings therefore made discrimination and assessment their first concern. With the scales of judgment suspended and scrutiny properly conducted, they first required that a man’s conduct and accomplishments merit acceptance, and only then employed him according to his capacity, entrusting him with the various duties of government. Once administrative affairs were well managed and achievements became evident, they conferred rank upon him in recognition of his proven ability to fulfill his duties, granting him the first grade of appointment. title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
定矣祿斯視之錫之公廩恤其私也食以常秩
昭其廉也夫論述詳於官使之先祿爵施於明
試之後其序進有如此者爵不於公則惡德者
或至於濫及先王於是協衆志以布命以朝著
者士之所萃也登崇俊乂必僉諧於疇咨之餘
爵祿者天下之公器也顯庸車服必晝錫於大
廷之上舉賢而置之爵雖自我而彙征之願實
與在位者同之吾何私焉因能而官之命雖自
我而錫類之典實與在職者共之吾何與焉夫
===
其進之也閔然若不得已而其用之也退然不
敢自是其布公有如此者夫官人之序既彰而
公以至此先王之世所以朝無倖位野無遺賢
也嗟夫知人則哲能官人人固不易知也以帝
堯之世而靜言庸違者尚或姦於其間况其餘
者乎是故稽於有衆言不自用也秉心宣猶言
考慎也以此為防後世猶有狎昵私親謀及近
褻以忝王章者其亦弗審於先王之制也夫
立太傅少傅以養之欲其知父子君臣之
punctuated:
定矣，祿斯視之。錫之公廩，恤其私也；食以常秩，昭其廉也。夫論述詳於官使之先，祿爵施於明試之後，其序進有如此者。爵不於公，則惡德者或至於濫及。先王於是協衆志以布命，以朝著者，士之所萃也，登崇俊乂，必僉諧於疇咨之餘；爵祿者，天下之公器也，顯庸車服，必晝錫於大廷之上。舉賢而置之，爵雖自我，而彙征之願，實與在位者同之，吾何私焉？因能而官之，命雖自我，而錫類之典，實與在職者共之，吾何與焉？夫其進之也，閔然若不得已；而其用之也，退然不敢自是，其布公有如此者。夫官人之序既彰，而公以至此，先王之世所以朝無倖位，野無遺賢也。嗟夫！知人則哲，能官人。人固不易知也，以帝堯之世，而靜言庸違者尚或姦於其間，况其餘者乎？是故稽於有衆，言不自用也；秉心宣猶，言考慎也。以此為防，後世猶有狎昵私親，謀及近褻，以忝王章者，其亦弗審於先王之制也夫！

立太傅、少傅以養之，欲其知父子君臣之
translation_en:
…once his rank has been fixed, his stipend is set accordingly. Granting him grain from the public granary provides for his private needs; supporting him with a regular stipend makes manifest his integrity. Assessment is thorough before a man is appointed to office and employed, while stipends and ranks are bestowed only after his abilities have been clearly tested. Such is their orderly advancement. If ranks are not conferred impartially, men of bad character may receive them indiscriminately. Thus the former kings brought the wishes of the multitude into accord before issuing appointments. Since the court is where men of service gather, the promotion of outstanding talent must follow consultation that produces unanimous agreement. Since ranks and stipends are public instruments of all under Heaven, the conspicuous bestowal of carriages and robes must take place in daylight before the great court. When I raise a worthy man and place him in office, although his rank comes from me, I share with those already in high position the wish that worthy men should advance together. What private interest have I in this? When I appoint a man according to his abilities, although the commission comes from me, I share with those already serving the practice of extending favor to others of like worth. What personal part have I in this? In advancing men, the ruler is apprehensive, as though acting only because he must; in employing them, he is modest and does not dare presume himself right. Such is the impartiality of his appointments. With the proper order of appointments thus manifest and impartiality carried so far, it follows that under the former kings no one held a position at court through mere good fortune, and no worthy man outside the court was overlooked.

Alas! To know men is wisdom, enabling one to appoint them to office. Yet men are certainly difficult to know. Even in Emperor Yao's age, those whose quiet words concealed contrary conduct could still work their deceit among the others; how much more so in other times! Thus, to consult the multitude means not relying solely on one's own judgment; to hold fast to one's purpose and seek counsel broadly means examining with care. Even with these safeguards, later ages still saw rulers who favored intimates and relatives and sought counsel from familiar attendants, thereby disgracing royal institutions. Surely they had failed to scrutinize the institutions of the former kings!

Grand Preceptors and Junior Preceptors were appointed to nurture him, with the intention that he should understand the … between father and son, ruler and minister …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
道也
蘇志仁
同考試官教諭王批教世子以正人正道立說反覆
之法無出於此且思致縝密宜錄以式
考試官訓導郭批理精詞裕
考試官學正王批雅正
先王設官以教世子欲其察倫而已夫人倫萬
化之原也察乎此則治天下特舉措之無難矣
記者論教世子之灋若曰世子君之儲也故其
===
學以正蒙爲先而以養心爲要三王之教不獨
禮樂也而又立之太傅立之少傅以養之是故
表之以式定其趨也軌之以儀廸其性也是之
謂身教而薰陶化育之者有所屬矣達之以理
開其明也諭之以事通其蔽也是之謂言教而
啓廸輔導之者有所寄矣夫備官以責任而豈
徒哉蓋以父子者恩之合也統承於宗祧之相
禪而繼志述事之託重矣君臣者義之合也分
原於乾坤之定位而創業守成之責大矣世子
punctuated:
道也。
蘇志仁
同考試官教諭王批：教世子以正人正道立說，反覆之法無出於此，且思致縝密，宜錄以式。
考試官訓導郭批：理精詞裕。
考試官學正王批：雅正。
先王設官以教世子，欲其察倫而已。夫人倫，萬化之原也。察乎此，則治天下特舉措之無難矣。記者論教世子之灋，若曰：世子，君之儲也，故其學以正蒙爲先，而以養心爲要。三王之教，不獨禮樂也，而又立之太傅，立之少傅以養之。是故表之以式，定其趨也；軌之以儀，廸其性也。是之謂身教，而薰陶化育之者有所屬矣。達之以理，開其明也；諭之以事，通其蔽也。是之謂言教，而啓廸輔導之者有所寄矣。夫備官以責任，而豈徒哉？蓋以父子者，恩之合也，統承於宗祧之相禪，而繼志述事之託重矣；君臣者，義之合也，分原於乾坤之定位，而創業守成之責大矣。世子
translation_en:
…the Way.

Su Zhiren

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: In discussing the education of the heir apparent, the argument takes upright men and the correct Way as its basis. No method surpasses this for developing the argument from different sides. Moreover, the reasoning is meticulous; it should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: The principles are finely elucidated, and the expression is ample.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: Elegant and correct.

The former kings established offices to educate the heir apparent, wishing only that he should understand human relationships. Human relationships are the source of all transformation. Once these are understood, governing the realm becomes simply a matter of taking action without difficulty. In discussing the method of educating the heir apparent, the author of the Record seems to say: The heir apparent is the ruler’s successor. Thus, his learning gives priority to correcting youthful ignorance and takes the cultivation of the heart as its essential concern. The teaching of the kings of the Three Dynasties consisted not only of rites and music: they also appointed a Grand Preceptor and a Junior Preceptor to nurture him. Accordingly, they set examples before him to establish the direction of his conduct, and regulated him through proper forms to guide his nature. This is called teaching by personal example; responsibility for molding and transforming him was thus assigned. They made principles clear to him to develop his understanding, and instructed him through concrete affairs to remove his obstructions. This is called verbal instruction; responsibility for enlightening and guiding him was thus entrusted to designated persons. Surely filling these offices and assigning their responsibilities was no empty exercise!

For father and son are joined by affection. The line of succession is continued through the transmission of the ancestral sacrifices, and the charge to carry on one’s predecessor’s aspirations and undertakings is weighty. Ruler and minister are joined by righteousness. Their respective stations originate in the fixed positions of Heaven and Earth, and the responsibility for founding an enterprise and preserving its achievements is great. The heir apparent…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
居子與臣之節知爲人子而後可以爲人父知
爲人臣而後可以爲人君是故篤親親於父子
之間以全吾仁推而極之仁民也愛物也仁不
可勝用矣嚴尊尊於君臣之際以大吾義擴而
弘之而敬長而尊賢義不可勝用矣夫太傅少
傅之官立則羣職舉而無往非正人君臣父子
之倫明則群善萃而無往非正道先王敎世子
之灋不亦詳至矣乎嗚呼有敬承之啓而後有
夏有遷義之太甲而後有商有守成之成王而
===
後可以延有周之祚也三王敎世子之效其盛
如此後世監軍之債巫蠱之禍悖已甚矣何治
之足云是故治天下者當以三王爲準
第貳塲
論
先天下而後天下之謂君
馬拯
同考試官敎諭陳批士子類掇陳言以眩觀覽此作
構思宏深措詞簡古足可與古作者更僕矣惊服惊服
punctuated:
居子與臣之節，知爲人子而後可以爲人父，知爲人臣而後可以爲人君。是故篤親親於父子之間，以全吾仁，推而極之，仁民也，愛物也，仁不可勝用矣；嚴尊尊於君臣之際，以大吾義，擴而弘之，而敬長，而尊賢，義不可勝用矣。夫太傅少傅之官立，則羣職舉而無往非正人；君臣父子之倫明，則群善萃而無往非正道。先王敎世子之灋，不亦詳至矣乎！嗚呼！有敬承之啓而後有夏，有遷義之太甲而後有商，有守成之成王而後可以延有周之祚也。三王敎世子之效，其盛如此。後世監軍之債、巫蠱之禍，悖已甚矣，何治之足云！是故治天下者當以三王爲準。
第貳塲
論
先天下而後天下之謂君
馬拯
同考試官敎諭陳批：士子類掇陳言以眩觀覽，此作構思宏深，措詞簡古，足可與古作者更僕矣。惊服！惊服！
translation_en:
…occupies the position of both son and subject. Only after knowing how to be a son can one be a father; only after knowing how to be a subject can one be a ruler. Thus, by deepening affection for kin within the relationship between father and son, we perfect our benevolence. Extended to its fullest reach, this becomes benevolence toward the people and love for all things: benevolence has inexhaustible applications. By strictly honoring rank within the relationship between ruler and subject, we enlarge our righteousness. Expanded and developed, this becomes respect for elders and reverence for the worthy: righteousness has inexhaustible applications. Once the offices of Grand Mentor and Junior Mentor are established, all duties are performed, and upright men are everywhere. Once the relationships between ruler and subject and between father and son are clarified, all virtues gather, and the correct Way prevails everywhere. Were not the former kings’ methods of educating the heir most thorough and complete!
Ah! Only with Qi, who reverently carried on his inheritance, was there the Xia; only with Tai Jia, who turned toward righteousness, was there the Shang; and only with King Cheng, who preserved what had been achieved, could the dynastic fortune of Zhou be prolonged. Such were the splendid results of the Three Kings’ education of their heirs. In later ages, the “debt” of supervising the army [?] and the calamity of witchcraft accusations were already extreme violations of proper order. What worthy governance could be spoken of? Thus, those who govern All-under-Heaven should take the Three Kings as their standard.
Second Session
Discourse
“To Place Oneself Before All-under-Heaven and Then After All-under-Heaven Is What It Means to Be a Ruler”
Ma Zheng
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Candidates generally gather stale expressions to dazzle their readers. This composition is broad and profound in conception, concise and antique in diction, and fully worthy of taking its place alongside the writers of antiquity. Astonishing and admirable! Astonishing and admirable!

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎諭林批〔晚得此作以君人之道曰謙曰容〕
〔曰厚立說奇崛高邁獨取胸臆而終以先君後身自見佳士也〕
考試官訓導郭〔氣格高邁〕
考試官學正王〔理深詞正〕
夫君人者貴於以志任天下則可以有乎天下
以心下天下則可以託於天下任天下者天下
歸之下天下者天下崇之崇則爲君而歸則爲
國不崇不歸其何能王故君也者其勢尊矣而
德謙也其分嚴矣而度容也其威神矣而體厚
===
也天下承君以爲天君弗敢以天而自大天下
敬君以爲神君不敢以神而自彰故曰容也者
君之體也任也者君之道也任矣故先天下以
有爲容矣故後天下而無爲有爲者王之始無
爲者帝之終舍是而曰君則名隆而實隱身顯
而國危故九五者君之位也萬乘者君之器也
皇王者君之名也威福者君之權也位可尊矣
而弗之保乎器可乘矣而弗之典乎名可榮矣
而弗之實乎權可運矣而弗之守乎故遜毅者
punctuated:
同考試官敎諭林批〔晚得此作，以君人之道曰謙、曰容〕〔曰厚，立說奇崛高邁，獨取胸臆，而終以先君後身自見，佳士也。〕
考試官訓導郭〔氣格高邁。〕
考試官學正王〔理深詞正。〕
夫君人者，貴於以志任天下，則可以有乎天下；以心下天下，則可以託於天下。任天下者，天下歸之；下天下者，天下崇之。崇則爲君，而歸則爲國。不崇不歸，其何能王？故君也者，其勢尊矣，而德謙也；其分嚴矣，而度容也；其威神矣，而體厚也。天下承君以爲天，君弗敢以天而自大；天下敬君以爲神，君不敢以神而自彰。故曰：容也者，君之體也；任也者，君之道也。任矣，故先天下以有爲；容矣，故後天下而無爲。有爲者，王之始；無爲者，帝之終。舍是而曰君，則名隆而實隱，身顯而國危。故九五者，君之位也；萬乘者，君之器也；皇王者，君之名也；威福者，君之權也。位可尊矣，而弗之保乎？器可乘矣，而弗之典乎？名可榮矣，而弗之實乎？權可運矣，而弗之守乎？故遜毅者，
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔I came upon this composition late. It describes the way of ruling others in terms of humility, tolerance,〕〔and generosity. Its argument is strikingly original and lofty, drawn solely from the writer’s own mind. He concludes by expressing his commitment to placing his duties as ruler before his own person. A worthy scholar indeed!〕
Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: 〔Its spirit and style are lofty.〕
Examiner Wang, Instructor: 〔Its reasoning is profound and its language correct.〕
For one who rules others, what matters is to undertake responsibility for all under Heaven with firm purpose: then he may possess all under Heaven. If in his heart he places himself below all under Heaven, then he may entrust himself to them. To one who assumes responsibility for all under Heaven, all under Heaven turn in allegiance; one who places himself below all under Heaven, all under Heaven exalt. Through their exaltation he becomes ruler; through their allegiance he establishes a state. Without exaltation or allegiance, how could he reign as king? Thus a ruler’s power is exalted, yet his virtue is humble; the distinctions of his rank are strict, yet his disposition is tolerant; his majesty is numinous, yet his essential character is generous. All under Heaven uphold their ruler as Heaven itself, yet he dares not aggrandize himself on that account. All under Heaven revere their ruler as a spirit, yet he dares not glorify himself on that account. Thus we say: tolerance is the ruler’s essential character; assuming responsibility is the ruler’s way. Because he assumes responsibility, he goes before all under Heaven and acts; because he is tolerant, he places himself after all under Heaven and refrains from action. Action is the beginning of kingly rule; nonaction is the culmination of imperial rule. If he abandons these principles yet calls himself ruler, his title is exalted but its substance obscured; his person is prominent but his state imperiled. Thus the nine in the fifth place is the ruler’s position; ten thousand chariots are the ruler’s instruments; sovereign and king are the ruler’s titles; punishments and rewards are the ruler’s powers. His position may be exalted, but should he not preserve it? His instruments may be ridden, but should he not have charge of them? His titles may bring honor, but should he not give them substance? His powers may be exercised, but should he not safeguard them? Thus humility and resolve …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
帝道也不穀曷任不遜曷容否則位孰宅之器
孰藏之名孰主之權孰握之是徒擁虛器於天
下而不知其身之入於敝也故聖王後其身而
身先外其身而身存與道消息以灋自然法自
然者不以逸先先之以勞不以危後後之以樂
勞者憂民與共勤之樂者宜民與共履之順先
後之序知進退之度通屈伸之感悟得喪之幾
萬務順焉而不為功萬物歸焉而不為主人稱
之曰天地大君而聖王自謂孤與不穀人奉之
===
===
以天下而聖王則先天下以其心是天下以豫
大望於王而王乃以身後天下而自怵故谷無
以虛將竭而不應君無以謙將亢而無民人不
得誘其踰於先天不得艱其綏於後是謂深根
固柢長乆之道光而不耀積而彌延政渾渾而
民醇醇俗吁吁而道蕩蕩是之謂大君昔者過
門不入禹先天下而不家成功不伐禹後天下
而不有昃不遑食文先天下而弗寧庶罔攸兼
文後天下而不預兹皆察於先後之微而不敢
punctuated: 帝道也。不穀曷任？不遜曷容？否則，位孰宅之？器孰藏之？名孰主之？權孰握之？是徒擁虛器於天下，而不知其身之入於敝也。故聖王後其身而身先，外其身而身存，與道消息，以灋自然。法自然者，不以逸先，先之以勞；不以危後，後之以樂。勞者，憂民與共勤之；樂者，宜民與共履之。順先後之序，知進退之度，通屈伸之感，悟得喪之幾，萬務順焉而不為功，萬物歸焉而不為主。人稱之曰天地大君，而聖王自謂孤與不穀；人奉之以天下，而聖王則先天下以其心。是天下以豫大望於王，而王乃以身後天下而自怵。故谷無以虛，將竭而不應；君無以謙，將亢而無民。人不得誘其踰於先，天不得艱其綏於後。是謂深根固柢、長乆之道，光而不耀，積而彌延。政渾渾而民醇醇，俗吁吁而道蕩蕩，是之謂大君。昔者，過門不入，禹先天下而不家；成功不伐，禹後天下而不有。昃不遑食，文先天下而弗寧；庶罔攸兼，文後天下而不預。兹皆察於先後之微而不敢
translation_en: …is the Way of the true emperor. Without calling himself “unworthy,” how can he bear responsibility? Without humility, how can he be accommodating? Otherwise, who will occupy his position? Who will hold the instruments of his rule? Who will possess his title? Who will wield his authority? He would merely hold empty instruments of power over the world, unaware that he himself was falling into ruin. Thus the sage king puts himself last, yet comes first; places himself outside his concerns, yet preserves himself. He waxes and wanes with the Way, taking what is naturally so as his model. One who models himself on what is naturally so does not take precedence in ease, but leads through toil; he does not lag behind in danger, but comes last in enjoyment. In toil, he is concerned for the people and shares their exertions; in enjoyment, he benefits the people and shares it with them. He follows the proper order of going first and coming last, knows the measure of advance and withdrawal, comprehends the interplay of contraction and expansion, and perceives the subtle beginnings of gain and loss. The myriad affairs proceed smoothly through him, yet he claims no merit; the myriad things turn to him, yet he does not claim mastery. People call him the great ruler of Heaven and Earth, but the sage king calls himself “the solitary one” and “the unworthy one.” People offer him all under Heaven, but the sage king takes the lead in caring for all under Heaven. Thus the world places expectations of ease and greatness upon the king [?], while the king puts himself after everyone else and remains apprehensive. Hence, unless a valley is empty, it will run dry and cease to respond; unless a ruler is humble, he will become overbearing and lose his people. Others cannot entice him to overstep by going first, nor can Heaven impede the tranquillity he achieves by coming last. This is called the Way of deep roots, a firm foundation, and enduring life: shining without dazzling, accumulating and extending ever further. Government is simple and uncontrived, and the people are sincere; customs are harmonious [?], and the Way is broad and open. Such a person is called a great ruler. In former times, Yu passed his own gate without entering: he went before all under Heaven and did not attend to his household. Having accomplished his work, he did not boast: he placed himself after all under Heaven and claimed no possession of his achievements. Though the sun was declining, King Wen had no leisure to eat: he went before all under Heaven and took no rest. He did not take all the manifold affairs upon himself [?]: he placed himself after all under Heaven and did not intervene. These rulers all discerned the subtleties of going first and coming last, and did not dare…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
忽故天下後世紀之爲聖王世人不知曰崇高
莫大乎富貴而君兼之法象莫大乎天地而君
配之巍巍然也赫赫然也豈知聖王以道蒞天
下不以位臨以心同萬民不以分隔因天下之
勢而乗之耳故可先而後之謂之怠可後而先
之謂之迎怠也者廢天下者也迎也者擾天下
者也不怠不迎與時偕行是以爲天下貴大國
者下流大君者下民故無執斯無失也無矯斯
無敗也無尊斯無屈也王者以一心周天下恒
===
業業然若墜於淵懼爲君之日損也而奚榮其
爲君世人榮君可加於庸主聖王則日懼而胡
爲崇世人逸君可擬於中辟聖王則日危而胡
爲逸江海能爲百川谷以其下也天下皆謂我
大豈聖王之福其殆矣哉我有三道持而守之
以與造化循環曰謙曰容曰厚不敢爲天下先
不敢爲天下後今舍謙而驕舍容而察舍厚而
刻則是昧其先後亂且及矣夫不敢爲天下先
故能成器不敢爲天下後故能長存故聖王欲
punctuated: 忽，故天下後世紀之爲聖王。世人不知，曰：「崇高莫大乎富貴，而君兼之；法象莫大乎天地，而君配之。巍巍然也，赫赫然也！」豈知聖王以道蒞天下，不以位臨；以心同萬民，不以分隔，因天下之勢而乗之耳。故可先而後之，謂之怠；可後而先之，謂之迎。怠也者，廢天下者也；迎也者，擾天下者也。不怠不迎，與時偕行，是以爲天下貴。大國者，下流；大君者，下民。故無執斯無失也，無矯斯無敗也，無尊斯無屈也。王者以一心周天下，恒業業然若墜於淵，懼爲君之日損也，而奚榮其爲君？世人榮君，可加於庸主；聖王則日懼，而胡爲崇？世人逸君，可擬於中辟；聖王則日危，而胡爲逸？江海能爲百川谷，以其下也。天下皆謂我大，豈聖王之福？其殆矣哉！我有三道，持而守之，以與造化循環：曰謙，曰容，曰厚。不敢爲天下先，不敢爲天下後。今舍謙而驕，舍容而察，舍厚而刻，則是昧其先後，亂且及矣。夫不敢爲天下先，故能成器；不敢爲天下後，故能長存。故聖王欲
translation_en:
…neglect it; thus the world and later generations recorded them as sage kings. People do not understand this, saying: “Nothing is loftier than wealth and rank, and the ruler possesses both; nothing provides greater patterns to emulate than Heaven and Earth, and the ruler stands alongside them. How towering! How resplendent!” How could they know that the sage king presides over the world through the Way, rather than ruling by his position; that in his heart he is at one with the myriad people, rather than separated from them by distinctions of status? He simply follows the prevailing circumstances of the world and acts upon them.

Thus, to come after when one should come before is called negligence; to come before when one should come after is called anticipation. Negligence leaves the world neglected; anticipation throws the world into turmoil. Neither negligent nor anticipating, one moves in step with the times: this is why one is esteemed throughout the world. A great state occupies the downstream position; a great ruler places himself below the people. Thus, without grasping, there is no loss; without forcing, there is no failure; without exalting oneself, there is no abasement. The king extends the care of his single heart throughout the world, constantly trembling as though falling into an abyss, fearing that his ability to be a ruler diminishes daily. How, then, could he glory in being a ruler?

The glory that people attribute to rulers may apply to an ordinary sovereign; but the sage king lives in daily fear—how could he exalt himself? The ease that people attribute to rulers may describe a middling sovereign; but the sage king daily feels himself in peril—how could he be at ease? Rivers and seas can serve as the receptacle for the hundred streams because they lie below them. “All the world calls me great”: could this be a blessing for the sage king? Surely it is perilous!

I have three principles, which I hold fast and preserve, thereby moving with the cycles of creation and transformation: humility, forbearance, and generosity. I dare neither to come before the world nor to come after it. Now, to abandon humility for arrogance, forbearance for intrusive scrutiny, and generosity for harshness is to misunderstand when to come before and when to come after; disorder will soon follow. By not daring to come before the world, one can become a vessel fit for use; by not daring to come after the world, one can endure long. Thus the sage king wishes…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
先乎民必以身後之是以天下樂推而不厭故
古者雖以拱璧先駟馬不如坐進識先後之勢
也昔黃郊紫微二君問於碧虚子曰天地造化
空茫唐濛致理之道絪縕無端厥先曷始厥後
曷終碧虚子曰豁乎包乎混乎闢乎天下之後
者子先之天下之先者子後之其庶矣乎夫民
先則已後憂先則樂隨順之吉也已先則民後
樂先則憂生逆之凶也是故先後無常因地以
定序先後者道之紀因先後者人之宜故先民
===
而後已者君也先君而後身者臣也先已而後
人者學也先家而後國者治也子其識之毋混
先後而異施毋反造化以自危黃郊紫微二君
恍然有悟曰天下之道盡之矣乃謝碧虚之言
而退一居無外一居無極相與游乎寥廓之宇
而序天地之後先也天地爲之泰民物爲之康
余嘗謂碧虚子之事則誕而言則理故五峯子
述之曰先天下而後天下之謂君余亦述之曰
先一人而後其身之謂臣
punctuated:
先乎民，必以身後之，是以天下樂推而不厭。故古者雖以拱璧先駟馬，不如坐進，識先後之勢也。
昔黃郊、紫微二君問於碧虚子曰：「天地造化，空茫唐濛；致理之道，絪縕無端。厥先曷始？厥後曷終？」碧虚子曰：「豁乎！包乎！混乎！闢乎！天下之後者，子先之；天下之先者，子後之，其庶矣乎！夫民先則已後，憂先則樂隨，順之吉也；已先則民後，樂先則憂生，逆之凶也。是故先後無常，因地以定。序先後者，道之紀；因先後者，人之宜。故先民而後已者，君也；先君而後身者，臣也；先已而後人者，學也；先家而後國者，治也。子其識之，毋混先後而異施，毋反造化以自危。」黃郊、紫微二君恍然有悟，曰：「天下之道盡之矣！」乃謝碧虚之言而退，一居無外，一居無極，相與游乎寥廓之宇，而序天地之後先也。天地爲之泰，民物爲之康。
余嘗謂碧虚子之事則誕，而言則理。故五峯子述之曰：「先天下而後天下之謂君。」余亦述之曰：「先一人而後其身之謂臣。」
translation_en:
…to stand before the people, he must place himself behind them. Thus all under Heaven gladly advance him and never tire of doing so. Hence the ancients held that even offering a jade disk large enough to fill both hands, preceding a team of four horses, was inferior to presenting the Way while seated [?]: they understood the circumstances governing precedence and following.
Once the two gentlemen Huangjiao and Ziwei asked Bixuzi: “The transformations of Heaven and Earth are vast, obscure, and indistinct; the Way by which order is attained is interwoven, without discernible beginning. Where does its beginning commence? Where does its ending conclude?” Bixuzi replied: “How expansive! How encompassing! How undifferentiated! How open! What all under Heaven put last, put first; what all under Heaven put first, put last. Then you may come close to the Way! When the people come first, oneself comes after; when concern comes first, joy follows. This is the good fortune of following the proper course. When oneself comes first, the people come after; when pleasure comes first, concern arises. This is the misfortune of going against the proper course. Thus precedence and following have no fixed positions: they are determined according to one’s situation. Ordering what comes first and what follows is the guiding principle of the Way; adapting to precedence and following is what befits human beings. Thus putting the people before oneself is the way of a ruler; putting the ruler before oneself is the way of a minister; attending to oneself before others is the way of learning; attending to the family before the state is the way of governing. Understand this. Do not confuse precedence and following and apply them amiss; do not oppose the workings of creation and endanger yourselves.”
Huangjiao and Ziwei suddenly understood and said: “The Way of all under Heaven is fully expressed in this!” They thanked Bixuzi for his words and withdrew. One dwelt in the realm beyond which nothing lies, the other in the realm without limit. Together they roamed the boundless universe, ordering what comes before and after in Heaven and Earth. Through this, Heaven and Earth attained harmony, and the people and all creatures enjoyed well-being.
I have often said that although the story of Bixuzi is fanciful, his words accord with principle. Thus Wufengzi expressed it as follows: “To come before all under Heaven and to come after all under Heaven—this is what it means to be a ruler.” I too express it thus: “To put the One Man first and oneself afterward—this is what it means to be a minister.”

擬
册立
皇太子正位東宮羣臣賀表
陳棐

社稷靈長之慶臣民愛戴之忱爛然可睹而氣格雄渾高出剸選之上余爲之一唱三嘆

translation_en:
Memorial
Model congratulatory memorial from the assembled officials on the formal investiture of the Imperial Heir Apparent and his installation in the Eastern Palace
By Chen Fei 陳棐

Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: This composition vividly portrays the joy at the dynasty’s enduring good fortune and the heartfelt affection and allegiance of officials and people. Its vigor and style are grand and full, far surpassing the selected compositions [?]. It moves me to sing its praises and sigh repeatedly in admiration.

Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: The classics have been thoroughly assimilated, leaving no residue or trace. Solemnity, loyalty, and sincerity also lie beyond the words themselves. Who but you will one day assist and guide him along the correct Way?

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: Exemplary and well regulated.

On a certain day of a certain month in a certain year of the Jiajing reign, your servants, so-and-so and the others, in heartfelt joy and delight, bowing our heads to the ground and knocking our foreheads upon it, submit these words. We humbly consider:

Heaven is serene, its vital forces harmonious; the jade registers of the imperial genealogy record the abundant extension of the heavenly lineage. Divine tokens accord with auspicious portents; the golden branches multiply, strengthening the bonds of the state. Throughout the four outskirts, the primal vital force is preserved in its gathering abundance; within the nine ancestral temples, radiant sunlight shines and spreads its transforming warmth. The qilin moves its feet: this comes from the blessings bestowed by the Lord on High. Auspicious clouds glow brilliantly over the vermilion palace precincts; the sun of transforming rule shines beautifully upon the imperial pivot. This …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
蓋恭遇
皇帝陛下
至仁體天以默運
大化配地以厚凝念
國家之本繫於
東宮順臣庶之心定乎
主器乃
玄思而獨斷豈懿惠之能移十奕之
天孫端拱層霄九夷之君長拜舞
===
彤闕靈門衛乎太乙玉鼎涵乎紫華二儀七曜
煥其精五嶽四瀆端其相渾濛之以羲皇
之氣宇炳朗之以列宿之文章信
一人豫懌於
九重亶庶姓咏依於萬世固
祖宗社稷之休實
天地生靈之福者也伏願
皇帝陛下養蒙作聖端可期日表之麗天慎始
培基毋徒羨
punctuated:
蓋恭遇皇帝陛下，至仁體天以默運，大化配地以厚凝。念國家之本繫於東宮，順臣庶之心定乎主器，乃玄思而獨斷，豈懿惠之能移？十奕之天孫端拱層霄，九夷之君長拜舞彤闕。靈門衛乎太乙，玉鼎涵乎紫華，二儀七曜煥其精，五嶽四瀆端其相。渾濛之以羲皇之氣宇，炳朗之以列宿之文章。信一人豫懌於九重，亶庶姓咏依於萬世。固祖宗社稷之休，實天地生靈之福者也。
伏願皇帝陛下養蒙作聖，端可期日表之麗天；慎始培基，毋徒羨
translation_en:
…for we have reverently encountered Your Majesty the Emperor, whose supreme benevolence embodies Heaven in its silent workings, and whose great transforming influence matches Earth in its profound solidity. Mindful that the foundation of the state rests upon the Eastern Palace—the heir apparent—and following the wishes of officials and commoners by settling who shall preside over the ancestral vessels, you pondered deeply and decided alone: how could kindly favor [?] sway you? The heavenly scion of ten generations sits with hands folded high in the layered heavens; the rulers of the Nine Yi bow and dance before the vermilion palace gates. The spirit gate guards the Supreme One; the jade cauldron contains purple radiance. Heaven and Earth and the seven luminaries illuminate his essence; the Five Sacred Peaks and Four Great Rivers give dignity to his appearance. He is endowed with the primordial breadth of spirit of Fuxi and the shining patterns of the constellations. Truly, the One Man rejoices within the ninefold palace, and the myriad families sing their allegiance for ten thousand generations. This is indeed a blessing upon the ancestors and the altars of soil and grain, and truly good fortune for all living beings between Heaven and Earth.
We humbly wish that Your Majesty the Emperor will nurture the youthful and untutored into sagehood: then we may surely anticipate that his sunlike countenance will shine in the heavens. Be careful at the beginning and cultivate the foundations; do not merely admire…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
龍姿之冠世春坊選學行之名儒温室謹保
携之懿姆豫而有立在賓客之得人懋以
交脩貴直諫之有士庶繼承罔媿於雲裔
亶會紹肇顯於
宗功臣等繇從賡歌日詠和於周德黃離布
象朝遐
祝於
天庭竊脩鳧藻之思慶覩
龍翔之瑞守成有託亶錫羨於仙源殖本彌
===
深永祚昌乎
國運是乃寸衷願效於涓埃而天下恭祈於
無斁者也臣等無任踴躍懽慶之至謹奉
表稱
賀以
聞
第參場
策
第一問
punctuated:
龍姿之冠世。春坊選學行之名儒，温室謹保携之懿姆。豫而有立，在賓客之得人；懋以交脩，貴直諫之有士。庶繼承罔媿於雲裔，亶會紹肇顯於宗功。臣等繇從賡歌，日詠和於周德；黃離布象，朝遐祝於天庭。竊脩鳧藻之思，慶覩龍翔之瑞。守成有託，亶錫羨於仙源；殖本彌深，永祚昌乎國運。是乃寸衷願效於涓埃，而天下恭祈於無斁者也。臣等無任踴躍懽慶之至，謹奉表稱賀以聞。

第參場
策
第一問
translation_en:
…his dragon-like bearing surpassing all the world. For the Spring Offices, select renowned Confucian scholars of learning and virtuous conduct; for the inner chambers, carefully choose worthy governesses to protect and tend him. Preparation that establishes him firmly depends on securing suitable Guests of the Heir Apparent; diligent mutual cultivation requires men who will remonstrate frankly. Thus may his succession bring no shame upon his distant descendants, and may the continuation of the ancestral achievement become manifest [?]. We, your servants, accordingly join in songs of praise, daily singing in harmony of virtue like that of Zhou. As the auspicious sign of yellow radiance appears, we offer far-reaching blessings at the celestial court each morning [?]. We humbly express our joy, like ducks sporting among water plants, and rejoice to behold the auspicious sign of the dragon soaring. With someone entrusted to preserve the inherited achievement, abundant blessings shall indeed be bestowed upon the imperial lineage; as its roots grow ever deeper, enduring good fortune shall bring prosperity to the dynasty. This is what our humble hearts wish to contribute, though only as a drop of water or a speck of dust, and what all under Heaven reverently pray for without weariness. Unable to contain our utmost joy and celebration, we, your servants, respectfully present this memorial of congratulation for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session
Policy Essays
First Question

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
馬拯
同考試官教諭陳批史古專職我
皇上嗣位銳意稽古獨茲未及子能議復馬母𨔵達國體矣乎
同考試官教諭林批以史職擬乾曆深爲有見𦾔
非獨以其雄博古雅爾也
考試官訓導郭批發明史關治道意殆盡
考試官學正王批嚴整
夫紀國之有史猶乾象之有曆也天之運
也四時五氣司其權非曆則日月星辰之
愆伏遲逆無所於稽而人時貿矣人主之
宰天下也百工庶府效其職非史則家國
君臣之治亂美惡無所於鑒而主德荒矣
故奉天道者治曆以明時而善治體者隆
史以匡過大矣哉史之益人國也執事以
建官爲問而史職爲先無亦謂資言之士
有達國體者乎洪惟
聖朝稽古定制大率表裏周官如三公以待增
秩而無專官固官不必備惟其人之遺意
punctuated:
馬拯

同考試官教諭陳批：「史古專職。我皇上嗣位，銳意稽古，獨茲未及。子能議復，馬母𨔵達國體矣乎？」

同考試官教諭林批：「以史職擬乾曆，深爲有見𦾔，非獨以其雄博古雅爾也。」

考試官訓導郭批：「發明史關治道意殆盡。」

考試官學正王批：「嚴整。」

夫紀國之有史，猶乾象之有曆也。天之運也，四時五氣司其權；非曆，則日月星辰之愆伏遲逆無所於稽，而人時貿矣。人主之宰天下也，百工庶府效其職；非史，則家國君臣之治亂美惡無所於鑒，而主德荒矣。故奉天道者治曆以明時，而善治體者隆史以匡過。大矣哉，史之益人國也！執事以建官爲問，而史職爲先，無亦謂資言之士有達國體者乎？洪惟聖朝稽古定制，大率表裏周官。如三公以待增秩而無專官，固官不必備、惟其人之遺意
translation_en:
Ma Zheng 馬拯

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: “In antiquity, historical recordkeeping was a specialized office. Since succeeding to the throne, Our Emperor has devoted himself earnestly to examining antiquity, yet this alone has not received his attention. You are able to argue for its restoration; [the following wording is garbled: 馬母𨔵] does this show an understanding of the essential structure of government?”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “The comparison of the historian’s office to the celestial calendar shows profound insight [𦾔?]. The merit does not lie solely in the writing’s vigor, breadth, and antique elegance.”

Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: “He brings out almost exhaustively the significance of historical recordkeeping for the way of government.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “Rigorous and orderly.”

A state’s possession of historians to record its affairs is like the possession of a calendar to chart celestial phenomena. In Heaven’s movements, the four seasons and the five vital energies exercise their powers. Without a calendar, there would be no means of examining the irregularities, disappearances, slow movements, and retrograde motions of the sun, moon, and stars, and the seasons for human activities would become confused. When the ruler governs all under Heaven, the various officers and administrative offices discharge their duties. Without historical records, there would be no mirror in which to examine order and disorder, good and evil, in the ruling house and state, or among rulers and ministers, and the ruler’s virtue would fall into neglect. Thus, those who uphold Heaven’s Way regulate the calendar to clarify the seasons, while those who understand the essential principles of government exalt historical recordkeeping to correct errors. Great indeed is the benefit that historical recordkeeping brings to a state! You, honored examiners, have asked about establishing offices and have placed the historian’s duties first. Is this perhaps because you believe that among the scholars whose views you seek there are some who understand the essential structure of government?

I respectfully consider how our sagely dynasty examined antiquity in establishing its institutions, which broadly accord with the Offices of Zhou. For example, the Three Dukes are reserved as titles for advancement in rank, without dedicated officeholders. This surely preserves the spirit of the ancient principle that offices need not all be filled, but depend upon finding the right men…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
也罷中書而建六曹大政則裁於吏部固
六卿分職冢宰統均之遺矩也他如設都
察院大理寺通政司以備九卿置六科十
三道以廣言路復嵗遣御史分按諸藩以
糾官邪而達民隱之數者則又雜取唐宋
之制而酌用之是故燮理寅亮則陰陽協
軌矣六府孔脩則五行順布矣彰善癉惡
則風雷交益矣其命官立制上擬天道誠
有以備
===
昭代之弘規而貽萬世之典則者矣顧史官
未復於古豈非
治朝之闕政歟夫史官何爲也天子弗遑自
紀人臣弗敢議君故寄之史臣以默握夫
公是公非之柄雖鬼神罔敢干其紀君相
莫得窺其微何者天帝不能以官私其人
人君亦弗得以官私其身也是故是非定
而褒貶形矣褒貶具而儆戒嚴矣故蘇氏
以爲域中有三權至推史官與天子等將
punctuated:
也。罷中書而建六曹，大政則裁於吏部，固六卿分職、冢宰統均之遺矩也。他如設都察院、大理寺、通政司以備九卿，置六科十三道以廣言路，復嵗遣御史分按諸藩，以糾官邪而達民隱之數者，則又雜取唐宋之制而酌用之。是故燮理寅亮，則陰陽協軌矣；六府孔脩，則五行順布矣；彰善癉惡，則風雷交益矣。其命官立制，上擬天道，誠有以備昭代之弘規，而貽萬世之典則者矣。

顧史官未復於古，豈非治朝之闕政歟？夫史官何爲也？天子弗遑自紀，人臣弗敢議君，故寄之史臣，以默握夫公是公非之柄。雖鬼神罔敢干其紀，君相莫得窺其微。何者？天帝不能以官私其人，人君亦弗得以官私其身也。是故是非定而褒貶形矣，褒貶具而儆戒嚴矣。故蘇氏以爲域中有三權，至推史官與天子等，將
translation_en:
…indeed. Abolishing the Central Secretariat and establishing the Six Ministries, with major affairs decided by the Ministry of Personnel, likewise preserves the ancient pattern whereby the six ministers divided their duties and the Minister of State coordinated them all. Other measures—establishing the Censorate, the Court of Judicial Review, and the Office of Transmission to complete the Nine Chief Ministers; instituting the Six Offices of Scrutiny and the Thirteen Circuits to broaden the channels for remonstrance; and annually dispatching investigating censors to inspect the provinces, expose official wrongdoing, and report the people’s hidden sufferings—selectively draw upon and adapt institutions of the Tang and Song. Thus, when ministers harmonize affairs and reverently assist the ruler, yin and yang follow concordant courses; when the six resources are fully attended to, the Five Phases unfold in proper order; and when goodness is commended and evil punished, wind and thunder mutually augment one another. In appointing officials and establishing institutions, the dynasty models itself upon the Way of Heaven above. These measures truly complete the grand design of our illustrious age and bequeath authoritative standards to all generations.

Yet the office of historian has not been restored to its ancient form. Is this not an omission in the governance of an otherwise well-ordered court? What is the historian’s purpose? The Son of Heaven has no leisure to record his own deeds, and subjects dare not pass judgment upon their ruler. Hence this task is entrusted to the historians, who quietly wield the authority to determine impartially what is right and wrong. Even ghosts and spirits dare not interfere with their records, and neither ruler nor chief minister may peer into their confidential contents. Why is this? The Celestial Emperor cannot use office to favor his appointees, nor may a human ruler use office to favor himself. Thus, once right and wrong are determined, praise and blame take shape; once praise and blame are fully expressed, admonitions and warnings become stringent. Accordingly, Master Su held that there were three powers within the realm, going so far as to rank the historian alongside the Son of Heaven, intending to…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
使諱惡名而怵於非憚心誅而攝其惡豈
獨相天地垂戒道於一時哉蓋自史筆肇
見於放勳重華而其職乃專於佚克蘇黯
周官具設漢制猶存晉魏相承唐典益備
故馬遷得以網羅放失見觀盛衰而述史
記吳競得以丏官筆札發紓志意而撰唐
書良以官不貳事職不易業故耳迨我
高皇之世太史起居注如宋王諸公皆擅一時
厥後沿革匪常盡歸翰苑所謂史官者不
===
過脩撰編脩檢討二三執事而已自是遴
選或未克廣其途儲養或未悉當其才愛
惜或未能久其任蓋有如吕公著之所慮
素養者矣是安能盡責以良史乎國有纂
述講讀官僚悉領其事分館編摩非無史
也然居常侍從無幾
宮闈言動罕聞所謂實錄者不過裒諸題奏
采諸邸報與臣僚家狀而已其後筆削或
制於總裁才華或非其儔匹考訂或局於
punctuated:
使諱惡名而怵於非，憚心誅而攝其惡，豈獨相天地、垂戒道於一時哉？蓋自史筆肇見於放勳、重華，而其職乃專於佚、克、蘇、黯。周官具設，漢制猶存，晉魏相承，唐典益備。故馬遷得以網羅放失，見觀盛衰，而述《史記》；吳競得以丏官筆札，發紓志意，而撰《唐書》。良以官不貳事，職不易業故耳。

迨我高皇之世，太史、起居注如宋、王諸公，皆擅一時。厥後沿革匪常，盡歸翰苑。所謂史官者，不過脩撰、編脩、檢討二三執事而已。自是遴選或未克廣其途，儲養或未悉當其才，愛惜或未能久其任，蓋有如吕公著之所慮素養者矣。是安能盡責以良史乎？

國有纂述，講讀官僚悉領其事，分館編摩，非無史也。然居常侍從無幾，宮闈言動罕聞。所謂實錄者，不過裒諸題奏，采諸邸報與臣僚家狀而已。其後筆削或制於總裁，才華或非其儔匹，考訂或局於
translation_en:
…to make them dread an evil reputation and recoil from wrongdoing, fear condemnation of their intentions, and restrain their wickedness. Could this merely assist Heaven and Earth and transmit admonitions for a single age? The historian’s brush first appeared in the days of Fangxun and Chonghua, and its duties subsequently became the special responsibility of Yi, Ke, Su, and An [?]. The Zhou established a full complement of offices; under the Han, the institutions still survived. The Jin and Wei inherited them, and Tang regulations became still more comprehensive. Thus Ma Qian—that is, Sima Qian—could gather scattered and lost materials, observe rise and decline [?], and compose the Records of the Historian; Wu Jing could request official writing materials, give expression to his aspirations, and compile the History of the Tang. This was precisely because their offices did not combine disparate duties, nor did their posts require them to change their occupation.

In the reign of our Emperor Gao, Grand Historians and Court Diarists, such as the gentlemen Song and Wang, were all preeminent in their day. Thereafter, institutional changes were frequent, and these responsibilities passed entirely to the Hanlin Academy. Those called historians were merely the few officials serving as Senior Compilers, Junior Compilers, and Examining Editors. Since then, the avenues of selection may not have been sufficiently broad; the cultivation of a reserve of personnel may not have fully suited their abilities; and efforts to cherish and retain them may not have secured sufficiently long tenures. There have indeed been problems of sustained preparation such as those that concerned Lü Gongzhu. How, then, can they all be held to the standards of good historians?

When the state undertakes historical compilation, the officials serving as Expositors and Readers take charge of all the work, dividing among compilation offices to prepare the texts. It is not that there are no historians. Yet in ordinary times they seldom attend upon the ruler and rarely hear of words and actions within the palace. The so-called Veritable Records are merely assembled from official memorials and reports, with material gathered from court gazettes and family accounts of officials. In the subsequent process of editing, their pens may be constrained by the Directors-General; their literary abilities may not match those of their peers; and their examination and verification of the material may be limited by…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
疎漏盖鮮有如劉子玄之所謂三長者矣
是又安得盡規以直筆乎雖然我
朝史職頗同宋制請以宋事明之聚三館之
雋選京朝之良參以殿閣學士之重猶以
爲未足也詳定取之法從校勘取之布衣
甚者外召還政之臣使充脩撰其博求史
官有如此者愚故以爲今日太史起居注
雖復設可也亦曰脩
祖宗之舊焉爾凡館局之選也或試諸制科新
===
進之士或改命在廷文行之臣英髦宿彥
務在兼收所貴具才是需無論地望有大
著作仍倣
先朝纂脩大典故事廣徵名儒下至山林隱逸
悉召詣公車試可而進俾與羣賢共事則
淹洽者著精覈之功才藻者盡潤色之美
如是則史官備矣時政有記起居有注日
曆有紀而郎舎人左右史復掌記言動
御殿則侍行幸則從事靡鉅細法得備書甚
punctuated:
疎漏，盖鮮有如劉子玄之所謂三長者矣。是又安得盡規以直筆乎？雖然，我朝史職頗同宋制，請以宋事明之。聚三館之雋，選京朝之良，參以殿閣學士之重，猶以爲未足也。詳定取之法從，校勘取之布衣，甚者外召還政之臣，使充脩撰。其博求史官有如此者。愚故以爲今日太史、起居注，雖復設可也，亦曰脩祖宗之舊焉爾。

凡館局之選也，或試諸制科新進之士，或改命在廷文行之臣，英髦宿彥，務在兼收。所貴具才是需，無論地望。有大著作，仍倣先朝纂脩大典故事，廣徵名儒，下至山林隱逸，悉召詣公車，試可而進，俾與羣賢共事。則淹洽者著精覈之功，才藻者盡潤色之美。如是則史官備矣。

時政有記，起居有注，日曆有紀，而郎舎人、左右史復掌記言動。御殿則侍，行幸則從，事靡鉅細，法得備書。甚
translation_en:
… omissions and oversights. Few, indeed, possess what Liu Zixuan called the three strengths. How, then, can they fully discharge their duty by writing with an impartial brush? Nevertheless, the historical offices of our dynasty are quite similar to those of the Song. Allow me to illustrate this with Song precedents. They assembled the outstanding men of the Three Institutes, selected the best capital officials, and added the weighty presence of academicians of the halls and pavilions; yet they still considered this insufficient.
