Those responsible for detailed review were drawn from the emperor’s attendant officials, and collators from men without official rank. They even summoned retired officials from outside the capital to serve as compilers. Such was the breadth of their search for historiographers. I therefore humbly believe that it would be permissible today to reestablish the offices of Grand Astrologer and Court Diarist: this would simply restore the old institutions of our imperial ancestors.

In selecting personnel for the institutes and bureaus, candidates might be tested from among men newly advanced through the special examinations, or officials at court distinguished for literary accomplishment and conduct might be reassigned. The aim should be to recruit both outstanding young men and eminent veterans. What matters is that they possess the requisite abilities, regardless of their standing or prestige. When a major work is to be undertaken, the precedent of compiling the Great Compendium under a former reign should again be followed: renowned scholars should be recruited widely, extending even to recluses in the mountains and forests. All should be summoned to the capital, tested, and appointed if qualified, so that they may work together with the assembled worthies. Those of extensive learning would then contribute meticulous verification, while those with literary talent would give full expression to the beauty of polished writing. In this way the complement of historiographers would be complete.

There were records of current government affairs, notes on the emperor’s daily activities, and entries in the daily chronicles; gentlemen and secretaries [?], together with Historiographers of the Left and Right, also had charge of recording his words and actions. When he occupied the audience hall, they attended him; when he traveled, they accompanied him. Whether an affair was great or small, the regulations permitted it to be recorded in full. Even …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
者一史成於十九年采輯多至數百家其
盡心史職有如此者愚故以為今日之編
摩無藝論譔或疎非無故也亦曰隆任使
之灋焉爾凡居舘局者必久於其職俾飽
探六籍明習
朝章言動畢記巨微勿遺而又倣近年編類
詔旨故事每月别使數人掌記外朝之事如除
拜刑賞戎祀章奏之類咸繫日而書之畢
則藏於東閣以擬日曆有大譔次則博采
===
遺書稗官野語悉送上官假以歲月毋張
僭賞以摇士心則事多本實不惑於諸司
供報之誤詞兼博雅庶免於淺陋蹇澁之
譏如是則史職盡矣嗚呼國是恒存斧鉞
如在於治不亦幾乎由是以觀則史官之
設其於公卿臺諫蓋有致重之道亦猶四
時五氣之資曆而行也仰惟
皇上述作兼隆禮樂明備崇獎儒臣加意史事
邇作
punctuated:
者，一史成於十九年，采輯多至數百家。其盡心史職有如此者，愚故以為今日之編摩無藝、論譔或疎，非無故也。亦曰隆任使之灋焉爾。凡居舘局者，必久於其職，俾飽探六籍，明習朝章，言動畢記，巨微勿遺。而又倣近年編類詔旨故事，每月别使數人掌記外朝之事，如除拜、刑賞、戎祀、章奏之類，咸繫日而書之。畢，則藏於東閣，以擬日曆。有大譔次，則博采遺書、稗官野語，悉送上官，假以歲月，毋張僭賞以摇士心，則事多本實，不惑於諸司供報之誤；詞兼博雅，庶免於淺陋蹇澁之譏。如是，則史職盡矣。
嗚呼！國是恒存，斧鉞如在，於治不亦幾乎？由是以觀，則史官之設，其於公卿臺諫，蓋有致重之道，亦猶四時五氣之資曆而行也。
仰惟皇上述作兼隆，禮樂明備，崇獎儒臣，加意史事，邇作
translation_en:
…in some cases, a single history took nineteen years to complete, drawing materials from as many as several hundred authors. Such was their devotion to the historian’s duties. I therefore believe that there are reasons why historical compilation today lacks proper bounds [?] and its discussions and accounts are sometimes careless. The remedy is simply to give greater weight to the procedures for appointing and employing historians. All who serve in the historiographical offices must remain long in their posts, so that they may thoroughly explore the Six Classics and become fully conversant with the court’s institutions. They should record every word and action, omitting nothing, great or small. Furthermore, following the recent precedent of compiling imperial edicts by category, several additional men should be assigned each month to record the affairs of the outer court: appointments, punishments and rewards, military affairs and sacrifices, memorials and submissions, and the like. All should be recorded under their respective dates. Once completed, these records should be deposited in the Eastern Pavilion to serve as the basis for the daily chronicle. When a major compilation is undertaken, surviving writings and unofficial histories and anecdotes should be collected widely and submitted in full to the responsible senior officials. Ample time should be allowed, and excessive rewards should not be ostentatiously offered to unsettle scholars’ minds. The accounts would then largely rest on facts, without being misled by errors in reports supplied by the various offices; their language would also be learned and elegant, hopefully escaping criticism for shallowness, crudity, awkwardness, and obscurity. In this way, the historian’s duties would be fully discharged.
Alas! If the proper standards of state affairs were perpetually preserved, and the punitive axe seemed ever present, would this not bring us close to good government? Viewed in this light, the establishment of historians provides a means of lending weight to the high ministers, censors, and remonstrance officials, just as the four seasons and the five vital influences proceed with the aid of the calendar.
I respectfully consider how His Majesty has brought both the transmission of tradition and new creation to flourishing heights, making rites and music clear and complete. He honors and rewards scholarly officials and gives particular attention to historical affairs. Recently he began constructing …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
寶宬以藏
謨訓納矇誦以采芻蕘
舜典堯文炳耀萬世則討論舊章以敷大典
亶惟我
聖天子攸望也抑愚又有說焉亮采宣猷者人
臣之責也包荒覆物者君人之度也故豫
養以成器能虛席以延幽隱風動以廣招
徠而後天下之史才出矣開誠心獎勁節
容直臣而後天下之史職修矣此愚生之
===
所致願者也執事釋其僭而幸進之謹對
第二問
劉漢
同考試官教諭蔣批
帝王之馭夷狄必威懷爲上策子條析南北利害難易之形如指諸掌且以虎狼猨猱爲譬尤
爲明切雖頗牧充國復生無以逾子矣尚薦何忝
考試官訓導郭批明達機變可以論兵矣
考試官學正王批詞古識深
夫兵有氣機以曲直爲强弱也兵有地機
punctuated:
寶宬以藏謨訓，納矇誦以采芻蕘。舜典堯文，炳耀萬世，則討論舊章以敷大典，亶惟我聖天子攸望也。抑愚又有說焉：亮采宣猷者，人臣之責也；包荒覆物者，君人之度也。故豫養以成器能，虛席以延幽隱，風動以廣招徠，而後天下之史才出矣；開誠心，獎勁節，容直臣，而後天下之史職修矣。此愚生之所致願者也。執事釋其僭而幸進之。謹對。
第二問
劉漢
同考試官教諭蔣批：帝王之馭夷狄，必威懷爲上策。子條析南北利害難易之形，如指諸掌，且以虎狼猨猱爲譬，尤爲明切。雖頗牧充國復生，無以逾子矣。尚薦何忝！
考試官訓導郭批：明達機變，可以論兵矣。
考試官學正王批：詞古識深。
夫兵有氣機，以曲直爲强弱也；兵有地機
translation_en:
…a precious archive to preserve imperial counsels and instructions, and accepts the recitations of blind musicians to gather the views of grass cutters and firewood gatherers. The canons of Shun and the writings of Yao shine brilliantly through all ages. To examine the old statutes and thereby set forth the great institutions is truly what our sagely Son of Heaven expects.
Yet I, in my ignorance, have something further to say. Faithfully carrying out duties and promulgating the sovereign’s plans are the responsibilities of a minister; embracing the neglected and sheltering all things display the magnanimity of a ruler. Thus, only after nurturing men beforehand to develop their capacities, leaving seats vacant to welcome those living in obscurity, and inspiring men by example to attract talent widely will the realm’s gifted historians emerge. Only after opening one’s heart in sincerity, rewarding steadfast integrity, and tolerating forthright ministers will the realm’s historians properly discharge their duties. This is the earnest wish of this humble student. May you pardon his presumption and graciously put these views forward. Respectfully submitted in reply.
Second Policy Question
Liu Han
Comment by Associate Examiner Jiang, Instructor: In emperors’ and kings’ management of the foreign peoples, the best policy must combine intimidation with conciliation. You distinguish point by point the advantages and disadvantages, difficulties and ease, of conditions in the south and north, making them as clear as something pointed out in one’s palm. Your comparisons with tigers, wolves, apes, and monkeys are especially lucid and apt. Even if Lian Po, Li Mu, and Zhao Chongguo returned to life, they could not surpass you. What cause for shame could there be in recommending you highly!
Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: You clearly understand changing circumstances and how to respond to them; you are qualified to discuss military affairs.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: The language is antique, the understanding profound.
Now, warfare has a dynamic of morale: being in the wrong or in the right determines weakness or strength. Warfare also has a dynamic of terrain …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以主客爲難易也兵有天機以氣運爲盛
衰也兵有人機以應暴爲勝負也世之論
用兵者莫不曰南易而北難而其論夷狄
亦莫不曰北强而南弱此觀其影弗覩其
形據其勢不究其實之說也何者畏其强
則備多而自寡顧强之縱而聽其侵乎輕
其弱則虚張而弗豫乃弱之凌而竭其内
乎愚生雖不知兵願於主客而分難易於
曲直而决强弱也故人曰北難愚則曰易
===
人曰南易愚則曰難何者遠近之勢殊而
勞逸之形判也夫中國爲宗四夷爲守君
子之所永懷暴在四夷禦在中國君子坐
談長治而弗圖乎吾聞之玩治以忘戰則
危恃强以好戰則憤故謀大事者不拘俗
圖永安者不憚勞今日之事克詰戎兵者
時也相其緩急者機也顧可昧而輕於動
耶夫智者覩於未形謀者圖於其大機者
應於其時今天下大勢遠近利害昭然在
punctuated: 以主客爲難易也。兵有天機，以氣運爲盛衰也。兵有人機，以應暴爲勝負也。世之論用兵者，莫不曰南易而北難；而其論夷狄，亦莫不曰北强而南弱。此觀其影弗覩其形，據其勢不究其實之說也。何者？畏其强，則備多而自寡，顧强之縱而聽其侵乎？輕其弱，則虚張而弗豫，乃弱之凌而竭其内乎？愚生雖不知兵，願於主客而分難易，於曲直而决强弱也。故人曰北難，愚則曰易；人曰南易，愚則曰難。何者？遠近之勢殊，而勞逸之形判也。夫中國爲宗，四夷爲守，君子之所永懷。暴在四夷，禦在中國，君子坐談長治而弗圖乎？吾聞之，玩治以忘戰則危，恃强以好戰則憤。故謀大事者不拘俗，圖永安者不憚勞。今日之事，克詰戎兵者，時也；相其緩急者，機也。顧可昧而輕於動耶？夫智者覩於未形，謀者圖於其大，機者應於其時。今天下大勢、遠近利害，昭然在
translation_en:
…with difficulty and ease determined by whether one fights as host or guest. Warfare has its workings of Heaven: flourishing and decline depend on the course of fortune. Warfare has its human workings: victory and defeat depend on whether one responds to aggression or commits it. Those who discuss the use of troops all say that the south is easy and the north difficult; and those who discuss the foreign peoples likewise all say that those in the north are strong and those in the south weak. Such judgments look at the shadow without seeing the form, and rely on outward circumstances without investigating the reality. Why? If we fear their strength, we spread our defenses widely and thin our own forces. Are we then to let the strong run unchecked and allow their incursions? If we disdain their weakness, we make an empty show of force without preparing. Are we then to suffer encroachment by the weak and exhaust our own resources?

Though I, an unworthy student, know nothing of warfare, I would distinguish difficulty from ease by whether one is host or guest, and determine strength and weakness by whether one's cause is unjust or just. Thus, where others call the north difficult, I call it easy; where others call the south easy, I call it difficult. Why? The circumstances of distance and proximity differ, and the conditions of exertion and rest are distinct. That the Central Kingdom should be the honored center and the foreign peoples on its four sides its guardians is what the gentleman always cherishes. Aggression lies with those foreign peoples, and defense with the Central Kingdom. Can the gentleman sit discussing lasting order without devising plans?

I have heard that complacency in peaceful government, causing one to forget warfare, brings danger; reliance on strength, leading one to delight in warfare, brings resentment. Thus, those who plan great undertakings are not bound by conventional views, and those who seek lasting security do not shrink from toil. In present affairs, the time calls for putting our arms and troops in order; discerning what is less urgent and what more urgent is a matter of grasping the critical opportunity. Can we act rashly in ignorance? The wise perceive things before they take form; planners attend to the larger issues; those alert to opportunity respond at the proper time. Now the overall circumstances of the realm, and the advantages and dangers of what is distant and near, stand clearly…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
前故舎近謀遠者勞而無功獵孤棄虗者
名爲不智愚請畢其難易之說可乎夫不
得已而應者勝無故而加者危先爲不可
勝者勝引兵以深入者危故近而爲主者
兵之先遠而爲客者兵之忌愚請於北言
戰功功亦大於南言戰謀謀亦洪昔竇憲
求自贖乃勒石以成赫赫之烈馬援討叛
賊徒表銅以竊沾沾之名究其實則徵側
亂而刺史守以待匈奴强而孤軍懸以攻
===
守以待者其功猶空名懸以攻者其績乃
實效難易之迹已明徴矣夫北虜之强譬
則虎狼虎狼之猛孰不畏之然陷阱可設
羅網可張因其貪饕鷙猛而進以取之是
我得致人而不致於人之勝何强之不可
折也夫南蠻之弱譬則猨猱猨猱之小孰
不狎之然張機則懸崖而伏弛備則烏集
而來或者久暴坐費而反以取侮是彼恃
形我而彼無形之詐何弱之易以加也故
punctuated: 前。故舎近謀遠者，勞而無功；獵孤棄虗者，名爲不智。愚請畢其難易之說，可乎？夫不得已而應者勝，無故而加者危；先爲不可勝者勝，引兵以深入者危。故近而爲主者，兵之先；遠而爲客者，兵之忌。愚請於北言戰功，功亦大；於南言戰謀，謀亦洪。昔竇憲求自贖，乃勒石以成赫赫之烈；馬援討叛賊，徒表銅以竊沾沾之名。究其實，則徵側亂而刺史守以待，匈奴强而孤軍懸以攻。守以待者，其功猶空名；懸以攻者，其績乃實效。難易之迹，已明徴矣。夫北虜之强，譬則虎狼。虎狼之猛，孰不畏之？然陷阱可設，羅網可張，因其貪饕鷙猛而進以取之，是我得致人而不致於人之勝，何强之不可折也？夫南蠻之弱，譬則猨猱。猨猱之小，孰不狎之？然張機則懸崖而伏，弛備則烏集而來，或者久暴坐費，而反以取侮，是彼恃形我而彼無形之詐，何弱之易以加也？故
translation_en:
…before us. Thus, those who abandon what is near to pursue distant designs labor without achievement; those who hunt down isolated foes and disregard undefended positions [?] are deemed unwise. May I finish explaining the relative difficulty and ease of these undertakings? Those who respond because they have no alternative prevail; those who attack without cause court danger. Those who first make themselves invincible prevail; those who lead their troops deep into enemy territory court danger. Thus, remaining nearby and acting as the host takes precedence in warfare; going far afield and acting as the guest is something military commanders avoid. Let me speak of military achievements in the north: those achievements were indeed great. Let me speak of military planning in the south: those plans were likewise grand. Formerly, Dou Xian sought to redeem himself and carved an inscription in stone to establish his illustrious achievements; Ma Yuan campaigned against rebels, yet merely erected a bronze marker to claim a reputation in which he complacently delighted. Examining the actual circumstances, when Zheng Ce rebelled, the Regional Inspector held his position and waited; though the Xiongnu were strong, an isolated army ventured far afield to attack them. The achievements of the one who held his position and waited amounted merely to an empty reputation; those of the one who ventured far afield to attack produced tangible results. The evidence for their relative difficulty and ease is already clear.

The strength of the northern barbarians may be compared to that of tigers and wolves. Who does not fear the ferocity of tigers and wolves? Yet pitfalls can be prepared and nets spread. Taking advantage of their ravenous hunger and ferocity, one can advance and capture them. This is the advantage of compelling the enemy to come to us without being compelled to go to him. What strength, then, cannot be broken? The weakness of the southern barbarians may be compared to that of apes and monkeys. Who does not treat such small creatures lightly? Yet when traps are set, they hide among precipitous cliffs; when precautions are relaxed, they flock in like crows. Our troops may remain exposed in the field for a long time, consuming resources to no purpose, and instead bring humiliation upon themselves. This is their reliance on the stratagem of making us reveal our dispositions while they themselves remain without discernible form. What weakness, then, is easy to assail? Therefore…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
自古以來征北者有功征南者無功乃往
鑒也寧弗審乎生愚以為武不可弛兵有
所先莫先吉囊夫吉囊可容而弗誅生靈
寧忍而不救乎夷狄可禦而弗窮中國寧
坐敝而不戰乎故戰則守有餘備則守不
足吾非為攻之戰來則戰以破之張克伐
之威以奪其魄戰以止戰將不有宣王之
薄伐耶胡曰役中國以事夷也又以為權
有所設變有所圖莫貴於處安南夫安南
===
===
可緩而弗征可聽其負固而不庭乎安南
必征而弗宥可忍驅赤子以罹瘴乎故撫
則享來王之福戰則有角勝之形吾不為
棄之弱來則柔以懷之握馭夷之道以制
其柄征以無征將不有大舜之來格耶胡
曰棄明德以爭利也夫順天者昌得人者
勝故王者奉天行伐霸者假義興師是以
有成烈且犁庭於漠北者其勢險養冦於
門庭者其禍危今吉囊猖獗不犁其庭寧
punctuated: 自古以來，征北者有功，征南者無功，乃往鑒也，寧弗審乎？生愚以為武不可弛，兵有所先，莫先吉囊。夫吉囊可容而弗誅，生靈寧忍而不救乎？夷狄可禦而弗窮，中國寧坐敝而不戰乎？故戰則守有餘，備則守不足。吾非為攻之戰，來則戰以破之，張克伐之威以奪其魄，戰以止戰，將不有宣王之薄伐耶？胡曰役中國以事夷也？又以為權有所設，變有所圖，莫貴於處安南。夫安南可緩而弗征，可聽其負固而不庭乎？安南必征而弗宥，可忍驅赤子以罹瘴乎？故撫則享來王之福，戰則有角勝之形。吾不為棄之弱，來則柔以懷之，握馭夷之道以制其柄，征以無征，將不有大舜之來格耶？胡曰棄明德以爭利也？夫順天者昌，得人者勝，故王者奉天行伐，霸者假義興師，是以有成烈。且犁庭於漠北者，其勢險；養冦於門庭者，其禍危。今吉囊猖獗，不犁其庭，寧
translation_en:
…Since ancient times, campaigns against the north have achieved success, while campaigns against the south have achieved none. Such is the lesson of the past: should we not examine it carefully? In my humble opinion as a student, military preparedness must not be relaxed, and military action has its priorities. None takes precedence over Ji Nang. Even if Ji Nang could be tolerated and left unpunished, could we bear to leave the people without rescue? Even if the non-Chinese peoples could be held off without being pursued to exhaustion, could we sit by while the Central Realm is worn down and refuse to fight? Thus, fighting leaves strength to spare for defense, whereas merely standing on guard leaves defense inadequate. I do not advocate war for conquest: when they come, fight and defeat them. Display the might of victorious arms to break their spirit, using war to end war. Would this not be like King Xuan’s limited punitive expedition? How could it be called burdening the Central Realm in service to foreign peoples?

I further believe that expedients must be devised and changing circumstances planned for; nothing is more important than handling Annam. Even if action against Annam could be postponed and no expedition sent, could we allow it to rely on its strong defenses and refuse attendance at court? If Annam must be attacked and cannot be pardoned, could we bear to drive our people into pestilential miasmas? Thus, conciliation brings the blessing of their coming to acknowledge royal authority, whereas war creates a contest for supremacy. I do not advocate the weakness of abandoning them: when they come, treat them gently and win their allegiance. Grasp the proper way to govern foreign peoples and retain the means of controlling them, bringing them to submission without a campaign. Would this not reproduce the coming into allegiance achieved by the great Shun? How could it be called abandoning luminous virtue to contend for profit?

Those who accord with Heaven prosper; those who win the people prevail. Thus, true kings conduct punitive expeditions in obedience to Heaven, while hegemons raise armies under the guise of righteousness: by these means they accomplish great deeds. Moreover, laying waste an enemy’s stronghold north of the desert entails peril, but nurturing an enemy at one’s own gates brings grave disaster. Now Ji Nang runs rampant. If we do not lay waste his stronghold, could we…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
縱其在門乎故曰當戰且容卧室之虎謂
其不傷人者吾弗信捕在澤之虺謂其不
可置者吾弗知今安南阻絶猶守疆圉寧
拒之不容貢乎故曰宜撫當戰者戰宜撫
者撫王道也夫破胡有算得算者四據勢
形便我主彼客得地之利一勝也
明運丕盛胡運方衰得天之道二勝也民怨其
殘軍士思憤得人之機三勝也天下全力
十倍匈奴謀臣虎臣内外協一得兵之權
===
四勝也夫有此四勝乃謂吉囊不可克彼
李牧之破東胡充國之平西羌又何人也
謂其法不可本之以戰而他求技則自疎
矣夫撫蠻有道得利者四不敝中國生靈
以安一利也坐享修貢中國益尊二利也
積財養兵併力西北三利也關市以通化
其居積四利也夫有此四利乃謂安南必
征彼干羽之舞兩階重譯之來百越又何
道也謂其人不可懷之以德而兵以懲則
punctuated:
縱其在門乎？故曰當戰。且容卧室之虎，謂其不傷人者，吾弗信；捕在澤之虺，謂其不可置者，吾弗知。今安南阻絶，猶守疆圉，寧拒之不容貢乎？故曰宜撫。當戰者戰，宜撫者撫，王道也。
夫破胡有算，得算者四：據勢形便，我主彼客，得地之利，一勝也；明運丕盛，胡運方衰，得天之道，二勝也；民怨其殘，軍士思憤，得人之機，三勝也；天下全力，十倍匈奴，謀臣虎臣，内外協一，得兵之權，四勝也。夫有此四勝，乃謂吉囊不可克，彼李牧之破東胡、充國之平西羌，又何人也？謂其法不可本之以戰，而他求技，則自疎矣。
夫撫蠻有道，得利者四：不敝中國，生靈以安，一利也；坐享修貢，中國益尊，二利也；積財養兵，併力西北，三利也；關市以通，化其居積，四利也。夫有此四利，乃謂安南必征，彼干羽之舞兩階、重譯之來百越，又何道也？謂其人不可懷之以德，而兵以懲，則
translation_en:
…allow him to remain at our gates? Thus I say that we should fight. Moreover, if one tolerates a tiger in the bedchamber and says it will not harm anyone, I do not believe it; if one catches a viper in the marsh and says it cannot be left alone, I do not understand this [?]. Now, although Annan has cut off relations, it still keeps within its borders. Should we reject it and refuse to admit its tribute? Thus I say that we should conciliate it. To fight those who should be fought and conciliate those who should be conciliated is the kingly way.
There are calculations for defeating the Hu, and four considerations favor us. We occupy advantageous terrain; we are the hosts and they the intruders. Possessing the advantage of the ground is our first assurance of victory. The fortunes of the Ming flourish greatly, while those of the Hu are declining. Having Heaven’s course in our favor is our second assurance of victory. The people resent their cruelty, and our soldiers are eager to vent their indignation. Having the opportunity afforded by popular sentiment is our third assurance of victory. The combined strength of the realm is ten times that of the Xiongnu; our counselors and valiant commanders, within and without, act in concert. Possessing military superiority is our fourth assurance of victory. With these four assurances, can anyone still say that Ji Nang cannot be defeated? What sort of men, then, were Li Mu, who defeated the Eastern Hu, and Chongguo, who pacified the Western Qiang? To say that their methods cannot serve as the basis for warfare, and to seek other techniques instead, is to put oneself at a disadvantage.
There is a way to conciliate the Man, yielding four benefits. We do not exhaust the Central Kingdom, and its people thereby enjoy peace: this is the first benefit. We receive their regular tribute without exertion, and the Central Kingdom gains further honor: this is the second benefit. We accumulate wealth and maintain our troops, concentrating our strength in the northwest: this is the third benefit. Trade passes through frontier markets, allowing accumulated goods to circulate: this is the fourth benefit. With these four benefits, can anyone still say that Annan must be attacked? What way was followed, then, when dancers bearing shields and feathers performed between the two stairways, and when the peoples of the Hundred Yue came through successive interpreters? To say that these people cannot be won over through virtue, and to punish them with armed force, is to…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
自竭矣故曰善馭夷者明於威德而已矣
善用兵者相其難易而已矣善權變者審
於緩急而已矣故見機而應若轉石於千
仞之山者勢也不見利而守若千鈞之弩
不爲鼷鼠發機者謀也若當國者信其難
易緩急之說愚請獻平胡之策與撫夷之
頌
第三問
吳日乙
===
同考試官敎諭王批天下之弊莫大於勢極不返之病今之處
宗室則亟矣然動以變成法離骨肉爲誡子獨能反覆論難毫析利害動中肯綮鑿鑿可行用世才
也是可薦于矣
考試官訓導郭批是作深籌遠識曲盡事變且意
婉氣昌造詞古雅佳士也
考試官學正王批仁至義盡
帝王之親親也其處之也仁其裁之也義
仁以處之所以惇倫非以殖私也義以裁
之所以永圖非以厚下也本之所在則衆
punctuated:
自竭矣。故曰：善馭夷者，明於威德而已矣；善用兵者，相其難易而已矣；善權變者，審於緩急而已矣。故見機而應，若轉石於千仞之山者，勢也；不見利而守，若千鈞之弩不爲鼷鼠發機者，謀也。若當國者信其難易緩急之說，愚請獻平胡之策與撫夷之頌。
第三問
吳日乙
同考試官敎諭王批：天下之弊，莫大於勢極不返之病。今之處宗室則亟矣，然動以變成法、離骨肉爲誡。子獨能反覆論難，毫析利害，動中肯綮，鑿鑿可行，用世才也。是可薦于矣。
考試官訓導郭批：是作深籌遠識，曲盡事變，且意婉氣昌，造詞古雅，佳士也。
考試官學正王批：仁至義盡。
帝王之親親也，其處之也仁，其裁之也義。仁以處之，所以惇倫，非以殖私也；義以裁之，所以永圖，非以厚下也。本之所在，則衆
translation_en:
…one merely exhausts oneself. Thus I say: those skilled at managing foreign peoples need only understand awe-inspiring power and virtue; those skilled at employing troops need only assess difficulty and ease; those skilled at adapting to circumstances need only judge what can wait and what is urgent. To recognize an opportunity and respond, like rolling a stone down a mountain a thousand ren high, is to exploit momentum. To hold one's position when no advantage is apparent, like a crossbow of a thousand jun that does not release its trigger for a tiny mouse, is strategic judgment. If those who govern the state accept this account of difficulty and ease, urgency and delay, I humbly beg to present a policy for pacifying the Hu and an ode celebrating the conciliation of foreign peoples.
Third Question
Wu Riyi
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: Of the world's ills, none is greater than allowing a situation to reach an extreme from which it cannot return. The handling of the imperial clan has now become urgent. Yet at every turn, people warn against changing established regulations and estranging one's own flesh and blood. You alone can examine the objections from every angle and distinguish benefits and harms with meticulous precision. Every point strikes home, and your proposals are demonstrably practicable. You possess talent for public service. This merits recommendation [?].
Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: This composition shows profound deliberation and far-reaching insight, thoroughly exploring the changing circumstances of affairs. Its meaning is subtly expressed, its spirit vigorous, and its diction antique and elegant. A fine scholar indeed.
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: Benevolence carried to its utmost; righteousness fully realized.
When emperors and kings cherish their kin, they treat them with benevolence and regulate them with righteousness. Treating them with benevolence serves to strengthen familial relationships, not to cultivate private interests. Regulating them with righteousness serves to plan for the long term, not to enrich those below. Where the root lies, then the many…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
建以貽安勢之所極則變通以定志咸所
以親親也蓋事有相須而理有相成故天
下之財不在官則在民天下之勢此重則
彼輕理其極重而使之平甦其方困而使
之可繼是計之善也故曰太上脩德以撫
民其次親親以相及執事發策以宗爲榦
以民爲土其在兹歟夫封建尚矣欽文光
被九族允親濬哲明揚先彼有庳周垂有
道之長卒之踐土會盟者晉魯其同姓也
===
漢延四百之祚卒之興衰噓燼者苗裔之
猶存也是故封建者天下之大本大端以
厚天倫以貽燕翼以大本根以固屛翰以
鞏大業以庇生靈以杜僭逆詩曰宗子維
城無俾城壞無獨斯畏此之謂也我
太祖高皇帝稽古定制大封諸王錫之國而不
屬以疆域班之祿而不煩以人民兵衛有
防出入有禁
親王得以監夫郡國郡國得以統夫宗人自
punctuated:
建以貽安，勢之所極則變通以定志，咸所以親親也。蓋事有相須，而理有相成，故天下之財不在官則在民，天下之勢此重則彼輕。理其極重而使之平，甦其方困而使之可繼，是計之善也。故曰：「太上脩德以撫民，其次親親以相及。」執事發策，以宗爲榦，以民爲土，其在兹歟？夫封建尚矣，欽文光被，九族允親；濬哲明揚，先彼有庳。周垂有道之長，卒之踐土會盟者，晉魯其同姓也；漢延四百之祚，卒之興衰噓燼者，苗裔之猶存也。是故封建者，天下之大本大端，以厚天倫，以貽燕翼，以大本根，以固屛翰，以鞏大業，以庇生靈，以杜僭逆。《詩》曰：「宗子維城，無俾城壞，無獨斯畏。」此之謂也。
我太祖高皇帝稽古定制，大封諸王，錫之國而不屬以疆域，班之祿而不煩以人民，兵衛有防，出入有禁。親王得以監夫郡國，郡國得以統夫宗人。自
translation_en:
…establish them to bequeath security; when circumstances reach their limit, adapt arrangements to settle people’s aspirations. All these are ways of treating one’s kin with affection. Affairs depend upon one another, and principles complement one another. Thus, the wealth of the realm lies either with the government or with the people; in the balance of power throughout the realm, when one side is weighty, the other is light. To regulate what has become excessively weighty and bring it into balance, and to revive those now in distress so that they can sustain themselves—this is sound planning. Hence the saying: “The highest course is to cultivate virtue and thereby care for the people; next is to cherish one’s kin and extend that affection to others.” In setting this policy question, you gentlemen take the imperial lineage as the trunk and the people as the soil. Is this not the principle at issue?
Enfeoffment has a venerable history. Yao’s reverent culture shone far and wide, and the nine degrees of kinship were truly brought into harmony. Shun’s profound wisdom was manifest, and he gave precedence to that fief at Youbi [?]. The Zhou enjoyed enduring rule through possession of the Way; in the end, those who assembled to covenant at Jiantu were Jin and Lu, states sharing its royal surname. The Han prolonged its dynastic fortune for four hundred years; in the end, those who revived it from decline and breathed life into its embers were descendants of its ruling house who still survived. Thus enfeoffment is a great foundation and cardinal institution of the realm: it strengthens the bonds of kinship, bequeaths protection to posterity, enlarges the roots of the ruling house, secures its protective bulwarks, consolidates the great imperial enterprise, shelters the living, and forestalls usurpation and rebellion. The Book of Odes says: “The sons of the lineage are a wall. Do not let the wall collapse; do not stand alone and thus have cause for fear.” This is what it means.
Our Emperor Taizu Gao examined antiquity and established institutions, extensively enfeoffing princes. He bestowed princedoms upon them without assigning them territorial jurisdiction, and allotted stipends without burdening them with governing the people. Their military guards were subject to restrictions, and their movements to prohibitions. Princes could oversee the commandery princedoms, and the commandery princedoms could exercise authority over members of the imperial lineage. From …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
鎮輔奉國將軍以至于中尉因服而等差
自郡主縣主以至于縣君以世而降殺愛
以浹之分以閑之品節之詳貽謀之善無
以加矣百七十餘年
天潢之派其衍無窮
玉牒所登其麗不億然皆食土之力以相滋
浥顧壤地有限而膏腴將竭無惑乎執事
之惓惓也夫國以宗爲榦而以民爲土理
固然矣將植夫榦不容不厚其宗將沃其
===
土不容不恤夫民審於謀國者舍是其曷
以哉顧動關
宗室諱於進言議若創聞難於慮始愚嘗中
夜以思
今日化之當更而治當亟處之當遠而計當
早者莫大於此我
皇上踐祚以來灋
祖尊
親脩明禮樂上兼三代盡善盡美邇者
punctuated: 鎮輔奉國將軍以至于中尉，因服而等差；自郡主、縣主以至于縣君，以世而降殺。愛以浹之，分以閑之，品節之詳，貽謀之善，無以加矣。百七十餘年，天潢之派，其衍無窮；玉牒所登，其麗不億。然皆食土之力，以相滋浥。顧壤地有限，而膏腴將竭，無惑乎執事之惓惓也。夫國以宗爲榦，而以民爲土，理固然矣。將植夫榦，不容不厚其宗；將沃其土，不容不恤夫民。審於謀國者，舍是其曷以哉？顧動關宗室，諱於進言；議若創聞，難於慮始。愚嘗中夜以思，今日化之當更而治當亟、處之當遠而計當早者，莫大於此。我皇上踐祚以來，灋祖尊親，脩明禮樂，上兼三代，盡善盡美。邇者，
translation_en:
…through the generals who guard, assist, and support the state, down to the commandants, ranks are differentiated according to degrees of mourning obligation; from commandery princesses and county princesses down to county ladies, status diminishes with successive generations. Affection suffuses them, while distinctions of rank restrain them. Nothing could surpass the precision of these gradations or the excellence of this planning for posterity. Over more than 170 years, the branches of the imperial lineage have multiplied without end; those entered in the imperial genealogy are beyond counting. Yet all depend upon the produce of the land for their sustenance. Land is finite, however, and its fertility is approaching exhaustion. It is no wonder that you, sir, are so deeply concerned.

The state takes the imperial clan as its trunk and the people as its soil: this is indeed the natural order. To establish that trunk, one must treat the imperial clan generously; to enrich its soil, one must care for the people. How could anyone discerning in planning for the state proceed otherwise? Yet every action touches upon the imperial clan, making people reluctant to speak; proposals that seem unprecedented are difficult to deliberate upon at their inception. In my humble reflections in the middle of the night, I have thought that, among the matters today in which transforming influence requires renewal and administration requires urgency, in which arrangements must look far ahead and planning must begin early, none is greater than this.

Since Our Emperor ascended the throne, he has followed his ancestors as models, honored his parents, and cultivated and clarified rites and music. He has united in himself the achievements of the Three Dynasties of antiquity, attaining complete goodness and complete perfection. Recently, …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
明詔載頒惓惓然
宗室爲念且曰一切宗藩祿米未給者有司
其處補之噫其即放勳睦族之仁重華有
庳之義則將奚以飭猷劑量以善後通變
以濟時謂非執事之責可乎昔者賈誼陳
治安而規諸侯鼂錯賛密謀而計七國或
託空言而速實禍是又不然談治安者空
而無當計七國者褊而靡恩今欲培既茂
之林而思衍其盛息不支之力而欲爲之
===
所將以廣仁而非以寡恩將以圖安而非
以速釁將以集謀而非以發難將以釋糾
而非以多事愚亦何憚盡言之夫今之
宗室山西河南爲極盛而山西河南之民亦
既困矣豈惟兩藩哉聞之關陝宗祿折值
而入曩頗云厚既而則逓减然猶不給既
而則議處補然猶不能補則是凡有
宗藩之地者其民可知豈惟民哉
宗藩亦有食祿之名而往往不受其實故告
punctuated:
明詔載頒，惓惓然宗室爲念，且曰：「一切宗藩祿米未給者，有司其處補之。」噫！其即放勳睦族之仁、重華有庳之義，則將奚以飭猷劑量，以善後；通變，以濟時？謂非執事之責，可乎？昔者賈誼陳治安而規諸侯，鼂錯賛密謀而計七國，或託空言而速實禍。是又不然。談治安者空而無當，計七國者褊而靡恩。今欲培既茂之林而思衍其盛，息不支之力而欲爲之所，將以廣仁而非以寡恩，將以圖安而非以速釁，將以集謀而非以發難，將以釋糾而非以多事，愚亦何憚盡言之？
夫今之宗室，山西、河南爲極盛，而山西、河南之民亦既困矣。豈惟兩藩哉？聞之關陝宗祿折值而入，曩頗云厚，既而則逓减，然猶不給；既而則議處補，然猶不能補。則是凡有宗藩之地者，其民可知。豈惟民哉？宗藩亦有食祿之名，而往往不受其實，故告
translation_en:
…an enlightened edict was promulgated, expressing earnest concern for the imperial clan and further declaring: “Wherever stipendiary grain remains unpaid to members of the imperial princely houses, the responsible officials shall arrange to make up the deficiency.” Ah! This embodies Fangxun’s [Yao’s] benevolence in bringing harmony to his kin and Chonghua’s [Shun’s] righteousness in his treatment of Youbi [the fief of his brother Xiang]. How, then, should plans be put in order and allocations adjusted to secure a sound settlement for the future, and measures adapted to meet the needs of the times? Could anyone say that this is not your responsibility?
Formerly, Jia Yi set forth plans for orderly and stable government and proposed restraints upon the feudal princes; Chao Cuo assisted in confidential deliberations and devised measures against the Seven Kingdoms. Some might say that relying on empty words only hastened actual disaster. Yet this is not quite so. The proposals for orderly government were abstract and ill-suited to circumstances; the measures against the Seven Kingdoms were narrow-minded and devoid of kindness. Now we wish to nurture an already flourishing forest and extend its luxuriance, to relieve strength strained beyond endurance and provide it support. Our purpose is to extend benevolence, not diminish kindness; to secure peace, not hasten conflict; to gather counsel, not provoke trouble; to resolve entanglements, not multiply complications. Why, then, should I hesitate to speak fully?
Among the imperial clan today, its branches in Shanxi and Henan are exceptionally numerous, while the people of Shanxi and Henan are already impoverished. But is this confined to those two provinces? I have heard that in Guanshan the imperial clan’s stipends are received in commuted monetary payments. Formerly these were said to be quite generous; subsequently they were progressively reduced, yet still could not be paid in full. Later, arrangements were discussed for making up the deficiencies, yet even these could not be made good. From this one may infer the condition of the people wherever imperial princely houses are established. And is it only the people who suffer? The princely houses, too, nominally receive stipends but frequently obtain no actual benefit. Thus they report…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乏干祿者迄無虛歲甚至屢空不給其狀
又難言者又聞
宗室中目擊興思固有請立宗學以興教化
者亦有願辭祿入以就科第者茲非誠負
曠達之識者歟愚於是敢以四善六可議
者爲執事繹而陳之惟執事擇焉如其不
詭于理而可比于芻蕘則惟
廟堂擇焉四者何詩曰文王孫子本支百世
凡周之士不顯亦世今學校遍天下且以
===
育士以及庶人矧曰宗戚而可以無教乎
是故宗學之立拔本之論也以明倫理以
興教化以涵俗習以一趨向是通其生而
厚之是之謂善詩曰建爾元子俾侯于魯
大啓爾宇爲周室輔今分封有地惟于西
北而亦有未之藩封者地同則可以平施
是派遷者導流之遺也且以立籍而非以
啓宇且以僑寓而非以析籍是廣其生而
富之是之謂善詩曰日之方中在前上處
punctuated:
乏干祿者，迄無虛歲，甚至屢空不給，其狀又難言者。又聞宗室中目擊興思，固有請立宗學以興教化者，亦有願辭祿入以就科第者，茲非誠負曠達之識者歟？愚於是敢以四善六可議者，爲執事繹而陳之，惟執事擇焉。如其不詭于理，而可比于芻蕘，則惟廟堂擇焉。

四者何？詩曰：「文王孫子，本支百世。凡周之士，不顯亦世。」今學校遍天下，且以育士以及庶人，矧曰宗戚，而可以無教乎？是故宗學之立，拔本之論也。以明倫理，以興教化，以涵俗習，以一趨向，是通其生而厚之，是之謂善。

詩曰：「建爾元子，俾侯于魯。大啓爾宇，爲周室輔。」今分封有地，惟于西北，而亦有未之藩封者。地同則可以平施，是派遷者導流之遺也。且以立籍，而非以啓宇；且以僑寓，而非以析籍。是廣其生而富之，是之謂善。

詩曰：「日之方中，在前上處。」
translation_en:
…those reporting want and petitioning for stipends have appeared every year without exception. Some even suffer repeated destitution and inadequate provision; their circumstances are difficult to describe. I have also heard that among members of the imperial clan, some, moved to reflection by what they have witnessed, have requested the establishment of clan schools to promote moral instruction. Others wish to relinquish their stipend income and pursue examination degrees. Are these not truly people of broad-minded understanding? I therefore venture to explain and present to you four beneficial measures and six points for deliberation, asking you to select among them. If they do not run counter to reason and may be ranked with the counsel of grass-cutters and wood-gatherers, I ask that the court select among them.

What are the four? The Book of Odes says: “The descendants of King Wen, the main line and its branches, shall endure for a hundred generations. All the officers of Zhou—are they not illustrious, generation after generation?” Schools now extend throughout the realm, educating scholars and reaching even the common people. How, then, could imperial kinsmen be left without instruction? Establishing clan schools is thus a proposal that addresses the root of the matter. By clarifying ethical relationships, promoting moral instruction, cultivating customary conduct, and unifying aspirations, it would open avenues of livelihood for them and make their provision more ample. This is what I call beneficial.

The Book of Odes says: “Establish your eldest son; make him lord in Lu. Greatly enlarge your domain, to serve as a bulwark of the house of Zhou.” At present, territorial enfeoffments are located only in the northwest, and some princes have not yet proceeded to their fiefs. Since the land is alike, provision can be distributed equitably. Relocating branches of the clan thus carries on the practice of channeling a flow [?]. The purpose would be to establish registered residence, rather than to open up domains; to reside away from home, rather than to divide household registrations. This would broaden their means of livelihood and enrich them. This is what I call beneficial.

The Book of Odes says: “When the sun is at its zenith, there in front, in the upper place [?]”…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
是不臨民之官也今宗學旣建而以科貢
入者將安用乎内之奉常且任羽士外之
王官悉聽貲補是皆無所臨民而以有司
治之者也獨不可任乎是之謂善詩曰稼
穡維寶代食維好是不食祿而足者也今
派遷而令立籍者豈其無事書契相通業
可置也恒產自力田可耕也是皆無所妨
民而惟正之供獨不可行乎是之謂善而
猶有可議者何夫宗學立矣王爵之及㓜
===
而有尊何以臨之典學者不可議乎夫分
派遷矣財賦之地不可以封于何而遷地
無藩封者不可議乎以科貢出者以宦入
而今王官不内序無故不令踰廓此其故
何也而曰宗仕可以典奉常諸職乎以義
聚者以恩掩而今諸藩皆五服之戚也而
曰王官可以通融爲乎齊民豪强猶恣兼
倂村儂憃朴不習識吏而況以尊且戚者
臨之乎
punctuated:
是不臨民之官也。今宗學旣建，而以科貢入者，將安用乎？内之奉常且任羽士，外之王官悉聽貲補，是皆無所臨民而以有司治之者也，獨不可任乎？是之謂善。《詩》曰：「稼穡維寶，代食維好。」是不食祿而足者也。今派遷而令立籍者，豈其無事？書契相通，業可置也；恒產自力，田可耕也。是皆無所妨民而惟正之供，獨不可行乎？是之謂善。
而猶有可議者何？夫宗學立矣，王爵之及㓜而有尊，何以臨之？典學者不可議乎？夫分派遷矣，財賦之地不可以封，于何而遷？地無藩封者不可議乎？以科貢出者，以宦入，而今王官不内序，無故不令踰廓，此其故何也？而曰宗仕可以典奉常諸職乎？以義聚者，以恩掩，而今諸藩皆五服之戚也，而曰王官可以通融爲乎？齊民豪强猶恣兼倂，村儂憃朴不習識吏，而況以尊且戚者臨之乎？
translation_en:
…These are offices that do not involve governing the common people. Now that schools for the imperial clan have been established, how are those who enter service through the examinations and tribute recommendations to be employed? At court, even Daoist priests are appointed to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; outside the capital, appointments to offices in the princely establishments are all permitted through monetary contributions. These offices do not involve governing the common people, yet they have officials to administer them. Could clan members alone not be appointed? This is what is meant by a good measure. The Book of Odes says: “Sowing and reaping are a treasure; earning sustenance in place of farming is good.” This refers to those who have enough without drawing an official stipend. Now, when clan branches are relocated and ordered to establish household registration, could they have no occupation? Through written contracts and transactions, they can acquire property; supporting themselves with a stable livelihood, they can cultivate fields. None of this interferes with the common people, and only the regular taxes are to be supplied. Could this alone not be put into practice? This is what is meant by a good measure.
Yet what still calls for discussion? Once clan schools have been established, princely rank may descend to children who thereby possess exalted status: how are they to be supervised? Should the choice of those in charge of their education not be discussed? Once clan branches have been separated and relocated, if lands yielding tax revenue cannot be granted as fiefs, where are they to move? Could places without princely fiefs not be considered? Those who emerge through examinations and tribute recommendations enter official service; yet at present the officials of princely establishments are not ranked within the regular service [?], and without cause they are not permitted to pass beyond the outer walls. What is the reason for this? And can one nevertheless say that imperial clansmen entering service may hold the various offices of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices? Where people are brought together by duty, personal affection may overshadow it. Now all the princes are relatives within the five degrees of mourning: can one say that offices in their establishments may be filled interchangeably? Even powerful men among the ordinary populace indulge unchecked in engrossing land. Simple, unsophisticated villagers are unaccustomed to dealing with officials. How much worse would it be if men of exalted status, who are also imperial relatives, were placed over them?

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
宗藩所統如綱如領蓋有國主宗主者存細
之而家事大之而請名請封諸典皆由卑
達尊類為之奏如今派遷則遠近無算何
以自通旦夕有務何以咨正而希恩專制
者且將乘間起矣今
宗藩之有餘者孰不擇置田宅類以家僮典
買而租稅之入則于其主第額稅類存業
戶而包賠貽累民且弗堪如今置田則明
示以植產而便奸惟其意常賦之入誰能
===
===
速之訟牒呼號者且將毅然興矣凡是六
者不可不預議者也無已則有二計仰惟
皇祖封建之灋尊位重祿仁至渥也親盡義存
恩至遠也夫維奉國中尉親云盡矣而猶
食祿得非仁之至極而可裁之以義者乎
何者支庶不大遠于齊民今齊民長子孫
則各有恒產其所以封殖自愛者無不為
子孫計是以無侈費無冗食積之既厚則
均遺其子孫今
punctuated:
宗藩所統，如綱如領，蓋有國主、宗主者存。細之而家事，大之而請名、請封，諸典皆由卑達尊，類為之奏。如今派遷，則遠近無算，何以自通？旦夕有務，何以咨正？而希恩專制者，且將乘間起矣。今宗藩之有餘者，孰不擇置田宅？類以家僮典買，而租稅之入則于其主。第額稅類存業戶，而包賠貽累，民且弗堪。如今置田，則明示以植產而便奸，惟其意，常賦之入誰能速之？訟牒呼號者，且將毅然興矣。凡是六者，不可不預議者也。
無已，則有二計。仰惟皇祖封建之灋，尊位重祿，仁至渥也；親盡義存，恩至遠也。夫維奉國中尉，親云盡矣，而猶食祿，得非仁之至極，而可裁之以義者乎？何者？支庶不大遠于齊民。今齊民長子孫，則各有恒產，其所以封殖自愛者，無不為子孫計。是以無侈費，無冗食，積之既厚，則均遺其子孫。今
translation_en:
The organization of the imperial clans is like the main cord of a net or the collar of a garment: there are heads of princely domains and heads of lineages. Matters small enough to concern household affairs and great enough to concern requests for names and enfeoffment—all these procedures pass from junior to senior, and memorials are generally submitted on their behalf. If branches are now dispersed and relocated, their distances will vary without limit. How will they communicate their affairs? When business arises at any moment, whom will they consult for guidance? Those seeking favors and exercising arbitrary authority will seize the opportunity to emerge. Among members of the imperial clans who now have surplus means, who does not select and acquire fields and houses? They generally have household servants acquire these through mortgage or purchase, while the rents and dues go to their masters. Yet the assessed taxes generally remain registered under the property holders, and the burden of making up payments brings distress that the common people can scarcely endure. If they are now allowed to acquire land, this will openly encourage them to establish landed estates and facilitate abuses at their pleasure. Who could compel them to remit the regular taxes? Those submitting complaints and crying out in protest will surely rise up. These six matters must all be considered beforehand.
If action cannot be avoided, there are two plans. Reverently considering the Imperial Ancestor’s system of enfeoffment, its exalted ranks and substantial stipends show the utmost generosity of benevolence; its preservation of obligations after the recognized degree of kinship has ended extends imperial grace to the utmost distance. For a Commandant Supporting the State (fengguo zhongwei), the recognized degree of kinship is said to have ended, yet he still receives a stipend. Is this not benevolence carried to its furthest limit, which might therefore be moderated according to righteousness? Why? Members of collateral branches are not greatly removed from ordinary commoners. Now, when commoners raise children and grandchildren, each has a settled livelihood. In everything they do to cultivate their property and care for themselves, they plan for their descendants. Thus they avoid extravagant expenditure and supporting idle mouths; once their accumulations are substantial, they bequeath equal shares to their children and grandchildren. Now…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
宗藩食祿千百者不有可分之祿乎夫父子
之恩天性之愛分其祿以貽所生猶之母
哺而子茹之非割恩也紈袴多餓匹夫有
以自謀故瘠土之民莫不向義其所以昕
夕自力者無不爲其身計是以無暇逸無
坐食卒乃大潤其家今親盡食祿者不可
隷之爲庶士乎夫君子之澤五世而斬刊
其虛藉而適其本性猶之名貶而實厚之
非寡情也凡此二者皆濟窮達變補偏救
===
弊之術也要約而論則學以敎之宦以祿
之籍以遷之田以食之皆以爲
宗藩計也而其實不過仕與耕而已矣如以
仕爲不可則直氣懾姦者非立朝之更生
乎如以耕爲不可則脫難光復者非耕野
之劉欽乎彼綿漢祚者豈其計盡出後人
下哉况夫叢委而不散則聚食京師者可
鑒也極重而不反則本實先撥者可慮也
親盡而不處則引領坐食者可念也窮至
punctuated: 宗藩食祿千百者，不有可分之祿乎？夫父子之恩，天性之愛，分其祿以貽所生，猶之母哺而子茹之，非割恩也。紈袴多餓，匹夫有以自謀，故瘠土之民莫不向義。其所以昕夕自力者，無不爲其身計，是以無暇逸，無坐食，卒乃大潤其家。今親盡食祿者，不可隷之爲庶士乎？夫君子之澤，五世而斬，刊其虛藉而適其本性，猶之名貶而實厚之，非寡情也。凡此二者，皆濟窮達變、補偏救弊之術也。要約而論，則學以敎之，宦以祿之，籍以遷之，田以食之，皆以爲宗藩計也。而其實不過仕與耕而已矣。如以仕爲不可，則直氣懾姦者，非立朝之更生乎？如以耕爲不可，則脫難光復者，非耕野之劉欽乎？彼綿漢祚者，豈其計盡出後人下哉？况夫叢委而不散，則聚食京師者可鑒也；極重而不反，則本實先撥者可慮也；親盡而不處，則引領坐食者可念也；窮至
translation_en: …those of the imperial clan who receive stipends numbering in the hundreds or thousands—do they not have stipends they could divide? The affection between father and son is a love rooted in human nature. To divide one’s stipend and pass it on to one’s offspring is like a mother feeding her child and the child eating: it does not sever affection. Many sons dressed in fine silks go hungry, while ordinary men have means of providing for themselves. Thus the people of barren lands all turn toward righteousness. In exerting themselves morning and evening, they invariably plan for their own livelihoods. Consequently, they have no leisure for idleness and do not eat without working; in the end they greatly enrich their households. Now, could those who still receive stipends after their recognized degree of kinship has expired not be enrolled as commoners? The beneficence of a gentleman ends after five generations. To strike out their nominal registration and let them follow their inherent nature is to lower their status in name while enriching them in substance; it is not unfeeling. Both these measures are methods of remedying an impasse through adaptation, correcting imbalances, and redressing abuses. To put it briefly: educate them through schools, provide stipends through official service, relocate them through household registration, and feed them through farmland. All these measures plan for the welfare of the imperial clan. In substance, however, they amount simply to official service and farming. If official service is deemed impermissible, was it not Gengsheng, serving at court, whose upright spirit cowed the wicked? If farming is deemed impermissible, was it not Liu Qin [?], cultivating the fields, who escaped calamity and restored the dynasty? Could the plans of those who prolonged the Han dynasty’s mandate really have been entirely inferior to those of later generations? Moreover, if they accumulate without being dispersed, those who gather in the capital to live on stipends offer a warning. If their weight reaches an extreme without being checked, there is reason to fear that the roots will be dislodged first. If those whose recognized kinship has expired are not provided for, those who stretch their necks in expectation and eat without working deserve concern. When destitution reaches…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而不恤則向隅之泣者可隱也史遷曰非
常之原黎民懼焉及臻厥成天下晏如也
是故慮始者難樂成者易矧此
宗室之議尤非書生所當與乎維是天啟宗
哲見炳識敷是之謂數理已極機會有開
庸展親親之義以平章仁民之政端在于
今擇四善究六議而酌二計詳爲之處漸
爲之圖曲爲之防博爲之訪以成一代不
刊之典以綿
===
國家億萬載無疆之慶則有賢公卿在位
聖天子在上幸無勞慮執事
第四問
何右之
同考試官學正黃批車戰古法有八勝十敗後世以
用奇始廢今日禦虜要法不懼陵突無逾於此可以謀國矣
考試官訓導郭批善談古今車戰之法
考試官學正王批論議明盡
對先王之灋繁而密其制敵也全以周後
punctuated:
而不恤，則向隅之泣者可隱也。史遷曰：「非常之原，黎民懼焉；及臻厥成，天下晏如也。」是故慮始者難，樂成者易。矧此宗室之議，尤非書生所當與乎？維是天啟宗哲，見炳識敷，是之謂數理已極，機會有開。庸展親親之義，以平章仁民之政，端在于今。擇四善，究六議，而酌二計，詳爲之處，漸爲之圖，曲爲之防，博爲之訪，以成一代不刊之典，以綿國家億萬載無疆之慶，則有賢公卿在位，聖天子在上，幸無勞慮，執事。
第四問
何右之
同考試官學正黃批：「車戰古法，有八勝十敗，後世以用奇始廢。今日禦虜要法，不懼陵突，無逾於此，可以謀國矣。」
考試官訓導郭批：「善談古今車戰之法。」
考試官學正王批：「論議明盡。」
對：先王之灋繁而密，其制敵也全以周。後
translation_en:
…and if they are given no relief, those who weep facing the corner deserve compassion. The historian Sima Qian said: “At the inception of extraordinary undertakings, the common people are afraid; once success is achieved, all under Heaven are at ease.” Thus, those who deliberate at the outset face difficulties, while those who enjoy the achievement have an easy task. How much more is this discussion of the imperial clan a matter in which a mere scholar ought not to intervene! Yet Heaven has enlightened the wise men of the imperial clan, making their vision brilliant and their understanding expansive [?]. This is what is meant by circumstances having reached their limit and an opportunity opening. Now is precisely the time to extend the duty of affection toward one’s kin and judiciously arrange policies of benevolence toward the people. Select among the four merits, investigate the six proposals, and weigh the two plans; make detailed arrangements, pursue them gradually, guard against difficulties in every particular, and consult widely. Thereby establish an enduring code for the dynasty and perpetuate the state’s boundless blessings for countless ages. Worthy dukes and ministers hold office, and the sage Son of Heaven reigns above: may you, sir, have no need to trouble yourself with anxiety.
Fourth Question
He Youzhi
Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “The ancient methods of chariot warfare comprise eight conditions for victory and ten for defeat. Only when later generations employed unconventional tactics did these methods fall into disuse. For resisting the northern invaders today, no essential method surpasses this in withstanding their onrushes. With this, one can devise plans for the state.”
Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: “An able discussion of the methods of chariot warfare, ancient and modern.”
Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “The argument is clear and exhaustive.”
Response: The methods of the former kings were elaborate and meticulous; in subduing the enemy, they were comprehensive and thorough. In later …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
世之灋簡而要其取勝也捷以直蓋王者
之兵出於不得已而非以求勝敵也故其
爲灋整而不漏嚴而有制曲折以極其變
奇餘以盡其數鉤聯相麗各有條理要以
不可敗而已後世之兵必於取勝故其爲
灋屢出屢變運其智巧出其機軸凡可以
速勝而得志者一切以簡易行之用奇掩
襲前茅慮無追蓐厚儲陷堅遮北隨其所
向而無不如意此後世之長技也是故帝
===
者之世以謀勝其微以機發王者之世以
全勝其權以變應伯者之世以術勝其灋
以形設故曰伐謀者微也全國者權也破
敵者灋也三者兵之不可闕一者也蓋嘗
觀古者寓兵於農四丘爲甸甸出長轂一
乘甲士三人步卒七十二人載以弓矢圍
以戈戟守以虎落布以渠荅而戰之具無
弗備及其用也險野人爲主易野車爲主
動則鱗次以衝突止則鉤聯以營衛先偏
punctuated: 世之灋簡而要，其取勝也捷以直。蓋王者之兵出於不得已，而非以求勝敵也。故其爲灋，整而不漏，嚴而有制，曲折以極其變，奇餘以盡其數，鉤聯相麗，各有條理，要以不可敗而已。後世之兵必於取勝，故其爲灋，屢出屢變，運其智巧，出其機軸。凡可以速勝而得志者，一切以簡易行之。用奇掩襲，前茅慮無，追蓐厚儲，陷堅遮北，隨其所向而無不如意，此後世之長技也。是故帝者之世以謀勝，其微以機發；王者之世以全勝，其權以變應；伯者之世以術勝，其灋以形設。故曰：伐謀者微也，全國者權也，破敵者灋也。三者，兵之不可闕一者也。蓋嘗觀古者寓兵於農，四丘爲甸，甸出長轂一乘、甲士三人、步卒七十二人，載以弓矢，圍以戈戟，守以虎落，布以渠荅，而戰之具無弗備。及其用也，險野人爲主，易野車爲主，動則鱗次以衝突，止則鉤聯以營衛，先偏
translation_en:
…the methods of later ages are simple and essential, and their victories swift and direct. The armies of true kings were raised only when unavoidable, rather than for the sake of defeating an enemy. Their methods were therefore orderly and without gaps, strict and regulated. Their intricate arrangements exhausted every variation; their irregular and supplementary dispositions exhausted every numerical combination [?]. Interlinked and mutually supporting, each had its proper order. The essential aim was simply to make defeat impossible. The armies of later ages were intent on victory. Their methods therefore continually emerged and changed, deploying ingenuity and devising stratagems. Whatever could secure a swift victory and accomplish their purpose was carried out through simple, expedient means. They used surprise tactics and sudden attacks, sent advance scouts to guard against unforeseen dangers, prepared encampments and ample supplies [?], broke through strong positions, and intercepted fleeing enemies. Wherever they turned, everything went as they wished: these were the particular strengths of later ages.

Thus, in the age of the sage emperors, victory was achieved through planning, its subtle workings set in motion at the opportune moment. In the age of true kings, victory was achieved by preserving things intact, with discretionary judgment responding to changing circumstances. In the age of hegemons, victory was achieved through stratagems, with methods established according to the disposition of forces. Hence it is said: to attack an enemy’s plans requires subtlety; to preserve a state intact requires discretionary judgment; to defeat an enemy requires method. Of these three, military operations cannot dispense with even one.

I have observed that in antiquity military service was incorporated into farming. Four qiu formed a dian, and each dian supplied one long-hubbed chariot, three armored soldiers, and seventy-two infantrymen. The chariots carried bows and arrows, were surrounded by dagger-axes and halberds, were protected by tiger-fence barriers, and had quda defensive devices arrayed around them. Thus every implement of warfare was provided. In deployment, men took the principal role on difficult terrain, and chariots on level terrain. When moving, they advanced in ranks like overlapping scales to charge and break through; when halted, they linked together to defend the camp, placing the pian chariot units in front…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
後伍前拒旁角出入以宅見可而進而戰
之技無弗周故兵車之灋動有節制古之
帝王恒握長技以制勝宣王戎車之飭如
輊如軒是故以之伐獫狁城朔方平淮夷
而四國罔弗正管子內政之寄灋令簡一
是故以之南伐楚北伐孤竹九合諸侯而
威振天下興周霸齊業隆名立車之爲用
大矣自是以後兵車之變愈出愈奇而愈
簡愈約田單以鐵籠全安平衛青以武剛
===
當匈奴馬隆偏箱之制山溪阸隘運如通
逵所謂一則治力一則前拒一則束部伍
誠得古灋矣馬燧狻猊之冒行以載兵止
則爲陣卽哥舒翰所用以收黃河九曲者
也亦甚輕利矣李忠定公銳志破金乃言
步不足以勝騎騎不足以勝車因繪統制
張行中所創車灋兩竿兩輪上載弓弩中
設皮籬下設鐵裙以長禦人以短禦馬布
列方陣圖而進之而收三勝金狄之功矣
punctuated: 後伍，前拒旁角，出入以宅，見可而進，而戰之技無弗周。故兵車之灋，動有節制。古之帝王恒握長技以制勝。宣王戎車之飭，如輊如軒，是故以之伐獫狁，城朔方，平淮夷，而四國罔弗正。管子內政之寄，灋令簡一，是故以之南伐楚，北伐孤竹，九合諸侯，而威振天下。興周霸齊，業隆名立，車之爲用大矣！自是以後，兵車之變愈出愈奇，而愈簡愈約。田單以鐵籠全安平，衛青以武剛當匈奴，馬隆偏箱之制，山溪阸隘，運如通逵。所謂一則治力，一則前拒，一則束部伍，誠得古灋矣。馬燧狻猊之冒，行以載兵，止則爲陣，卽哥舒翰所用以收黃河九曲者也，亦甚輕利矣。李忠定公銳志破金，乃言：「步不足以勝騎，騎不足以勝車。」因繪統制張行中所創車灋，兩竿兩輪，上載弓弩，中設皮籬，下設鐵裙，以長禦人，以短禦馬，布列方陣，圖而進之，而收三勝金狄之功矣。
translation_en:
…with squads behind, blocking formations in front and flanking formations at the sides; they moved out and back to their stations and advanced when an opportunity appeared. Thus their techniques of combat were comprehensive. In the methods of chariot warfare, every movement was regulated and controlled. The emperors and kings of antiquity consistently secured victory by exploiting their superior capabilities. King Xuan put his war chariots in order, their fronts dipping and rising; with them he attacked the Xianyun, fortified Shuofang, and pacified the Huaiyi, so that none of the states in the four quarters failed to submit to proper rule. Master Guan embedded military organization within domestic administration, making laws and commands simple and uniform. With this system he attacked Chu to the south and Guzhu to the north, assembled the feudal lords nine times, and made his might resound throughout the realm. In reviving Zhou and establishing Qi’s hegemony, great achievements were accomplished and lasting reputations established: immense indeed was the usefulness of chariots!

Thereafter, innovations in war chariots became ever more ingenious, yet ever simpler and more economical. Tian Dan preserved Anping with iron cages [?]; Wei Qing confronted the Xiongnu with “military-strength” wagons. Ma Long’s wagons with shielding on one side moved through mountain streams and narrow defiles as though on an open thoroughfare. As the saying goes, one served to conserve strength, another to block an advance, and another to hold the ranks together: these truly captured the ancient methods. Ma Sui’s lion-shaped coverings [?] were fitted to vehicles that carried soldiers on the march and formed an array when halted. These were precisely what Geshu Han had used to recover the Nine Bends of the Yellow River; they too were exceptionally light and serviceable.

Lord Li Zhongding, firmly resolved to defeat the Jin, declared: “Infantry cannot overcome cavalry; cavalry cannot overcome chariots.” He therefore had drawings made of the chariot design devised by Commander Zhang Xingzhong: two shafts and two wheels, bows and crossbows carried above, a leather screen in the middle, and an iron skirt below. Long weapons repelled men, and short weapons repelled horses. He depicted their deployment in a square formation and submitted the drawings to the throne, thereby achieving three victories over the Jin barbarians.

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
此皆車之用也要之帝王禦戎之兵惟以
持重不以掩襲其爲灋周而整嚴而密本
之以仁義而行之以節制者也戰國以後
則要功眩巧追逐萬里志在破敵故變古
司馬灋以簡速勝矻矻乎肄天下而逞其
欲矣邇者戎虜暴橫深入肆掠不得已而
應者時也先爲不可勝者技也爲今之計
不練於用車則恐紀律未詳罔足以陷堅
棄車而不用則恐倉卒無備不足以制勝
===
===
要之造車有灋用車以人荀吳之敗狄舍
車而用徒車以出奇者也李靖西討突厥
因車而節制車以正勝者也裁而變之神
而明之敦義以一心握機以制勝遇坦途
則爲司馬灋之伍兩爲衛青之武剛爲李
忠定之圖陣堂堂正正整暇有灋雖有驕
橫之虜不可得而犯遇險途則爲管子之
連軌爲馬燧之偏箱爲田單之鐵籠出其
不意而以奇取勝雖有掩伏之衆不可得
punctuated:
此皆車之用也。要之，帝王禦戎之兵，惟以持重，不以掩襲。其爲灋，周而整，嚴而密，本之以仁義，而行之以節制者也。戰國以後，則要功眩巧，追逐萬里，志在破敵，故變古司馬灋，以簡速勝，矻矻乎肄天下而逞其欲矣。邇者戎虜暴橫，深入肆掠，不得已而應者，時也；先爲不可勝者，技也。爲今之計，不練於用車，則恐紀律未詳，罔足以陷堅；棄車而不用，則恐倉卒無備，不足以制勝。

要之，造車有灋，用車以人。荀吳之敗狄，舍車而用徒，車以出奇者也；李靖西討突厥，因車而節制，車以正勝者也。裁而變之，神而明之，敦義以一心，握機以制勝。遇坦途，則爲司馬灋之伍兩，爲衛青之武剛，爲李忠定之圖陣，堂堂正正，整暇有灋，雖有驕橫之虜，不可得而犯；遇險途，則爲管子之連軌，爲馬燧之偏箱，爲田單之鐵籠，出其不意而以奇取勝，雖有掩伏之衆，不可得
translation_en:
These are all uses of chariots. In essence, the armies with which emperors and kings resist outside enemies rely on steadiness and caution, not surprise attacks. Their methods are comprehensive and orderly, strict and meticulous, founded upon benevolence and righteousness and implemented through discipline and command. From the Warring States period onward, however, commanders sought achievements and flaunted ingenuity, pursuing enemies for ten thousand li, intent upon defeating them. Thus they altered the ancient Methods of the Sima (Sima fa), seeking victory through simplicity and speed, laboring incessantly to exhaust the realm [?] and indulge their desires. Recently, the enemy has acted with brutal arrogance, penetrating deep into our territory and plundering at will. That we have no alternative but to respond is dictated by circumstances; first making ourselves invincible is a matter of skill. In planning for the present, if we do not train in the use of chariots, we must fear that discipline and organization will remain insufficiently developed to break strong positions. If we discard chariots and leave them unused, we must fear being unprepared in an emergency and unable to secure victory.

In essence, there are established methods for constructing chariots, but their employment depends upon people. When Xun Wu defeated the Di, he abandoned his chariots and used infantry: this exemplifies gaining an unexpected advantage in the employment of chariots. When Li Jing campaigned westward against the Tujue, he used chariots to maintain discipline and control: this exemplifies winning by orthodox methods through chariots. Adapt and transform their use; exercise inspired understanding of it. Strengthen righteousness to unite men's hearts, and grasp the critical opportunity to secure victory. On level roads, employ the squads and platoons of the Methods of the Sima, Wei Qing's armored wagons, or the diagrammed formations of Li Zhongding. With imposing and properly aligned formations, orderly, composed, and methodical, even an arrogant and unruly enemy will be unable to assail them. On difficult roads, employ Guanzi's linked wheel-tracks, Ma Sui's side-panel wagons, or Tian Dan's iron cages. Take the enemy unawares and gain victory through unorthodox methods; even troops lying in ambush will be unable to…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
而當或其地不輕于馬馬不輕于車車不
輕于人人不輕于戰而妄用之則其灋亂
矣此房琯之所以取敗而非古人之善用
者也噫非車之不利也用車者之罪也故
曰不嚴整不可以全圖不簡直不可以决
勝因噎以廢食豈謀國者之深思耶今三
代什伍之數管子治齊之灋雖不得其詳
而盡用之然取其近於嚴而整者以之守
取其近於簡而直者以之攻雖未必如黃
===
帝指南之車之用亦庶乎不可敗而有必
勝矣
第五問
方大猷
同考試官敎諭王批風俗與敎化相表裏不得已而
後用法子論風俗先崇敎化以申例立學二事尤急其識時務
者與如子言奚其難
考試官訓導郭批文意精到
考試官學正王批達變識要
punctuated:
而當。或其地不輕于馬，馬不輕于車，車不輕于人，人不輕于戰，而妄用之，則其灋亂矣。此房琯之所以取敗，而非古人之善用者也。噫！非車之不利也，用車者之罪也。故曰：「不嚴整，不可以全圖；不簡直，不可以决勝。」因噎以廢食，豈謀國者之深思耶？今三代什伍之數、管子治齊之灋，雖不得其詳而盡用之，然取其近於嚴而整者以之守，取其近於簡而直者以之攻，雖未必如黃帝指南之車之用，亦庶乎不可敗而有必勝矣。

第五問
方大猷

同考試官敎諭王批：「風俗與敎化相表裏，不得已而後用法。子論風俗，先崇敎化，以申例、立學二事尤急，其識時務者與！如子言，奚其難？」

考試官訓導郭批：「文意精到。」

考試官學正王批：「達變識要。」
translation_en:
…withstand them. If the terrain affords no ease to horses, horses afford none to chariots, chariots afford none to men, and men have no ease in battle [?], yet chariots are recklessly employed, their tactical order will fall into confusion. This is why Fang Guan suffered defeat; it was not the skillful employment practiced by the ancients. Alas! The fault lies not in chariots being ineffective, but in those who employ them. Thus it is said: “Without strictness and order, one cannot plan comprehensively; without simplicity and directness, one cannot secure victory.” To give up eating because one has choked—is this profound deliberation by those who plan for the state? Although we cannot recover the full details of the Three Dynasties’ organization into tens and fives or of Guanzi’s methods for governing Qi and put them all into practice, we can nevertheless adopt what approaches strictness and order for defense, and what approaches simplicity and directness for attack. Though this may not match the effectiveness of the Yellow Emperor’s south-pointing chariot, we may still come close to being invulnerable to defeat and certain of victory.

Fifth Policy Question
Fang Dayou

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: “Customs and moral instruction are the outward and inward aspects of one another; only when there is no alternative should laws be employed. In discussing customs, you give priority to moral instruction and regard reaffirming regulations and establishing schools as the two most urgent tasks. Surely you understand the needs of the times! If your proposals were followed, what difficulty would there be?”

Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: “The ideas in this composition are precise and penetrating.”

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: “He understands changing circumstances and recognizes what is essential.”

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
教也者風俗之樞機也灋也者風俗之隄
防也蓋樞機弗謹無以為神化之方而若
于訓者莫知自勵隄防弗立無以為齊治
之具而戾于習者莫知自懲是故教化行
而後俗易俗易則民知嚮方教化衰而後
俗偷俗偷則民日趨於弊將波蕩而不可
禦上之人觀於時俗之弊昭軌植則而表
樹先焉則俗易而淳厚之風可還矣嗟乎
風俗之移人可哀也推之天下皆然者矧
===
一方乎甞聞天下有氣化有治化時之所
鍾為盛衰為汚隆氣化之懸於天者也政
之所施足以挽衰于盛起汚于隆治化之
繫於人者也懸於天者不可以常恃而繫
於人者胡可以自諉故廣谷大川異制民
生其間異俗剛柔輕重遲速異齊言天下
之風俗無常也脩其教不易其俗齊其政
不易其宜言君子之推行有道也顧導民
者不可狃於俗而知教之易行耳我
punctuated: 教也者，風俗之樞機也；灋也者，風俗之隄防也。蓋樞機弗謹，無以為神化之方，而若于訓者莫知自勵；隄防弗立，無以為齊治之具，而戾于習者莫知自懲。是故教化行而後俗易，俗易則民知嚮方；教化衰而後俗偷，俗偷則民日趨於弊，將波蕩而不可禦。上之人觀於時俗之弊，昭軌植則，而表樹先焉，則俗易而淳厚之風可還矣。嗟乎！風俗之移人，可哀也！推之天下皆然者，矧一方乎？甞聞天下有氣化，有治化。時之所鍾，為盛衰，為汚隆，氣化之懸於天者也；政之所施，足以挽衰于盛，起汚于隆，治化之繫於人者也。懸於天者不可以常恃，而繫於人者胡可以自諉？故廣谷大川異制，民生其間異俗，剛柔輕重遲速異齊，言天下之風俗無常也；脩其教，不易其俗，齊其政，不易其宜，言君子之推行有道也。顧導民者不可狃於俗，而知教之易行耳。我
translation_en:
Instruction is the pivot of customs; law is their embankment. If the pivot is not carefully attended to, there is no means of bringing about spiritual transformation, and those who follow instruction do not know how to exert themselves. If the embankment is not established, there is no instrument for bringing about orderly government, and those whose habits are perverse do not know how to restrain themselves. Thus, when moral instruction prevails, customs change; when customs change, the people know to turn toward righteousness. When moral instruction declines, customs become lax; when customs become lax, the people daily sink into corruption, until they surge like waves that cannot be checked. If those above observe the failings of contemporary customs, make proper courses clear, establish standards, and take the lead in setting an example, customs will change and an ethos of sincerity and generosity can be restored. Alas! How lamentable is the power of customs to change people! This holds true throughout the realm; how much more so in a single region?

I have heard that throughout the realm there is transformation through vital forces and transformation through government. What the times bring forth—flourishing or decline, degradation or elevation—is transformation through vital forces, which depends on Heaven. What government puts into practice can turn decline into flourishing and raise degradation to elevation: this is transformation through government, which depends on human beings. What depends on Heaven cannot always be relied upon; how, then, can we shirk responsibility for what depends on human beings? Thus, broad valleys and great rivers differ in configuration, and the people living among them differ in customs; firmness and softness, lightness and gravity, slowness and swiftness vary in degree. This means that customs throughout the realm have no fixed form. Cultivating instruction without changing local customs, and regulating government without changing what suits local circumstances: this means that the gentleman has a proper way of putting his principles into practice. Those who guide the people must simply avoid becoming habituated to prevailing customs and recognize that instruction can readily be carried out. Our…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
國家文敎誕敷王章丕冒中外沐菁莪之化
民人洽熈皞之休盛美之風天下爲同且
以吾廣十郡之俗其淳龐作於古昔者固
弗可得而詳也乃今則躋於治矣士不回
守以脩于家民不荒業以安于鄉純朴之
風禮義之俗雖習尚靡一俗好弗侔未始
不胥迪于彝也爾乃風會乆而少漓氣化
流而或玩蹈瀆祀之愆而吉禮攸紊廢力
本之務而戸口不蕃豪强得以乗姦而盜
===
賊因以暴横悖理而傷化越軌而敗俗如
執事之所言者不終無也夫古之風俗即
今之風俗古之人心即今之人心古何爲
而淳篤今何爲而澆漓古何爲導之而輒
從今何爲禁之而弗止爲民上者其審圖
之徒重其防弗究其本則灋愈密而犯愈
衆刑益繁而罪益多源之不治而末流潰
是猶無鏑銜策錣而御馺馬難乎其止也
是故政不能以無弊捄之存乎時俗不能
punctuated:
國家文敎誕敷，王章丕冒，中外沐菁莪之化，民人洽熈皞之休，盛美之風，天下爲同。且以吾廣十郡之俗，其淳龐作於古昔者，固弗可得而詳也。乃今則躋於治矣，士不回守以脩于家，民不荒業以安于鄉。純朴之風，禮義之俗，雖習尚靡一，俗好弗侔，未始不胥迪于彝也。爾乃風會乆而少漓，氣化流而或玩，蹈瀆祀之愆而吉禮攸紊，廢力本之務而戸口不蕃，豪强得以乗姦而盜賊因以暴横。悖理而傷化，越軌而敗俗，如執事之所言者，不終無也。
夫古之風俗，即今之風俗；古之人心，即今之人心。古何爲而淳篤，今何爲而澆漓？古何爲導之而輒從，今何爲禁之而弗止？爲民上者，其審圖之。徒重其防，弗究其本，則灋愈密而犯愈衆，刑益繁而罪益多。源之不治而末流潰，是猶無鏑銜策錣而御馺馬，難乎其止也。是故政不能以無弊，捄之存乎時；俗不能
translation_en:
…our dynasty has spread its civilizing instruction far and wide, and royal institutions extend their shelter everywhere. Within and beyond the realm, all enjoy the nurturing transformation celebrated in the “Luxuriant Southernwood” ode; the people share the blessings of radiant harmony. These flourishing and admirable ways prevail throughout the world. As for the customs of the ten prefectures of our Guangdong, we cannot ascertain in detail the simple, substantial ways that arose in antiquity. Today, however, they have attained good order. Scholars do not waver in their principles and cultivate themselves within their families; common people do not neglect their occupations and live peacefully in their villages. Their ways are simple and their customs accord with ritual and righteousness. Although their habitual practices differ and their preferences vary, they have always guided one another along the constant moral norms. Yet as prevailing ways endure, they become somewhat diluted, and as transforming influences run their course, people sometimes grow heedless. They commit the fault of profaning sacrifices, thereby disrupting auspicious rites; they neglect the work of agriculture, the fundamental occupation, so that households and population fail to increase. The powerful exploit opportunities for wrongdoing, and robbers consequently become violent and unrestrained. Conduct that violates principle and harms moral transformation, that transgresses proper bounds and corrupts customs—as you, honored examiners, have described—is not altogether absent.
Now, the customs of antiquity are the customs of today, and the human heart of antiquity is the human heart of today. Why were people formerly sincere and steadfast, but are now shallow and insincere? Why did they formerly follow whenever guided, but now refuse to desist even when forbidden? Those who govern the people should consider this carefully. If they merely strengthen restraints without investigating the root, then the more closely drawn the laws, the more numerous the offenders; the more elaborate the punishments, the more numerous the crimes. If the source is left unregulated, the waters downstream burst their bounds. This is like driving a galloping horse without bit, reins, or whip [?]: how difficult it is to stop it! Thus government cannot be free of defects; remedying them depends on the times. Customs cannot…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
以常隆易之存乎變捄其弊而不因其時
弊不可得而捄矣易其俗而不通其變俗
不可得而易矣蓋政與時異道隨變施如
所謂行保甲之灋舉鄉學之規輕折抽之
利申漢條之例嚴酗酒之禁重賭博之律
誠俗易之大機救時之重務也要而言之
申例也立學也其尤急者也夫灋久則民
玩玩則無忌誠使有司嚴其隄防明律飭
灋如漢之察州郡者則豪暴者斂手頑黠
===
者革心倍公向私者不敢侵漁刻剝割損
政令如是則灋立而民有戾于習者乎敎
弛則民賊賊則易肆誠使有司謹其樞機
類族辨物如古之敎鄉學者脩六禮以節
民性明七敎以興民德齊八政以防淫一
道德以同俗如是則敎行而民有弗若于
訓者乎故曰上之所爲民之所歸也雖然
政政移風敎又其本也古之善言治者必
先於崇敎化使比閭族黨之間耳目所濡
punctuated:
以常隆，易之存乎變。捄其弊而不因其時，弊不可得而捄矣；易其俗而不通其變，俗不可得而易矣。蓋政與時異，道隨變施。如所謂行保甲之灋，舉鄉學之規，輕折抽之利，申漢條之例，嚴酗酒之禁，重賭博之律，誠俗易之大機、救時之重務也。要而言之，申例也，立學也，其尤急者也。
夫灋久則民玩，玩則無忌。誠使有司嚴其隄防，明律飭灋，如漢之察州郡者，則豪暴者斂手，頑黠者革心，倍公向私者不敢侵漁刻剝、割損政令。如是則灋立，而民有戾于習者乎？敎弛則民賊，賊則易肆。誠使有司謹其樞機，類族辨物，如古之敎鄉學者，脩六禮以節民性，明七敎以興民德，齊八政以防淫，一道德以同俗。如是則敎行，而民有弗若于訓者乎？故曰：「上之所爲，民之所歸也。」
雖然，政政移風，敎又其本也。古之善言治者，必先於崇敎化，使比閭族黨之間，耳目所濡
translation_en:
…remain flourishing forever; changing customs depends on adapting to change. If one remedies abuses without taking account of the times, those abuses cannot be remedied; if one reforms customs without understanding changing circumstances, those customs cannot be reformed. Government varies with the times, and its methods are applied as circumstances change. Such measures as implementing the baojia system of mutual household responsibility, instituting regulations for community schools, reducing the proceeds from commutation and levies [?], reaffirming precedents from Han statutes, strictly enforcing prohibitions on drunkenness, and strengthening the laws against gambling are indeed crucial means of transforming customs and urgent tasks for remedying the troubles of the age. In brief, reaffirming precedents and establishing schools are especially urgent.
When laws have long been in force, the people treat them lightly; treating them lightly, they lose all restraint. If the responsible officials truly strengthened their safeguards, clarified the statutes, and enforced the laws, as those who inspected regions and commanderies under the Han did, then the powerful and violent would stay their hands, and the obstinate and cunning would change their hearts. Those who betray public interests for private gain would not dare to plunder and exploit or undermine government commands. With the laws thus established, would any among the people persist in wayward practices? When instruction grows lax, the people become wicked; becoming wicked, they readily grow unrestrained. If the responsible officials truly attended carefully to the essential mechanisms, grouped people by kinship and distinguished things according to their kinds, as did those who taught in ancient community schools, they would cultivate the six rites to regulate the people's dispositions, elucidate the seven teachings to promote their virtue, order the eight governmental functions to prevent excess, and unify moral principles to make customs uniform. With instruction thus put into practice, would any among the people fail to follow its guidance? Hence the saying: “What those above do is what the people turn toward.”
Nevertheless, in government and the transformation of customs [?], instruction is fundamental. Those of antiquity who spoke well about governance invariably gave priority to honoring moral instruction, so that, among the neighborhood groupings of bi, lü, zu, and dang, what people's ears and eyes absorbed…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
染日用所見聞罔非軌範之示則觀感啓
進脩之益鼓舞寓丕變之機治化彰而氣
化亦還矣故曰化民成俗其必由學乎握
其機而任其責者非執事其孰圖之
punctuated: 染，日用所見聞，罔非軌範之示，則觀感啓進脩之益，鼓舞寓丕變之機。治化彰，而氣化亦還矣。故曰：「化民成俗，其必由學乎！」握其機而任其責者，非執事，其孰圖之？
translation_en: …imbued, and all that they see and hear in daily life presents models of proper conduct, then observation and its influence will foster advancement in self-cultivation, while encouragement will hold the potential for a great transformation. The transforming influence of governance will become manifest, and the transformation of vital energies will likewise return to its proper course. Thus it is said: “To transform the people and establish good customs, must one not proceed through learning?” Who but you, honored officials, who hold the means and bear the responsibility, should undertake this?

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄後序
吾聞之
聖王運天地以爲化賢哲感聖王
以爲期故運黙而感速聖作
而哲生天精凝焉天粹應焉
作者不測生者不違罔知其
故曷究其端故聖王者典天
===
地以樞機造化者也我
聖天子先崇聖文天下士以禮樂
文章應之爲昭今弘神武天
下士以韜畧謀勇應之爲烈
志一而氣應神一而景從惟
兹元象用以赫觀望之者巋
崑崙探之者浩淵海炳炳烺
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄後序

吾聞之：聖王運天地以爲化，賢哲感聖王以爲期。故運黙而感速，聖作而哲生，天精凝焉，天粹應焉。作者不測，生者不違，罔知其故，曷究其端？故聖王者，典天地以樞機造化者也。我聖天子先崇聖文，天下士以禮樂文章應之爲昭；今弘神武，天下士以韜畧謀勇應之爲烈。志一而氣應，神一而景從。惟兹元象，用以赫觀，望之者巋崑崙，探之者浩淵海，炳炳烺
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination

I have heard it said: the sage king sets Heaven and Earth in motion to bring about transformation; worthy and wise men are moved by the sage king and take him as their goal. Thus his workings are silent, yet their response is swift; when a sage arises, wise men come forth. Heaven’s essence gathers therein, and Heaven’s purest qualities respond. The workings of the one who arises are unfathomable; those who come forth do not depart from his way. If we do not know the cause, how can we fathom its beginnings? Thus the sage king presides over Heaven and Earth and serves as the pivot of creation and transformation. Our sagely Son of Heaven first exalted sagely civil culture, and the scholars of the realm responded through rites, music, and literary accomplishment, making its brilliance manifest. Now he extends his divine martial prowess, and the scholars of the realm respond through military strategy, planning, and courage, making its might manifest. When purpose is united, vital energies respond; when spirit is united, they follow like shadows. This primal manifestation presents a magnificent spectacle: to those who behold it, it towers like Kunlun; to those who explore it, it is vast as the deep ocean, gleaming and radiant…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
爛巍巍峩峩世人僉曰人文
宣朗光昭萬世竝曜隆古曷
知元涵貞育洪權荒輿咸我
聖天子大造縕融玄德廣運日月
星辰天末光也山川喬嶽地
余章也於微見著因流遡源
緊其闡之益以渾淪矣夫文
===
人武士竝禎王國文眀武赫
混於一初故文武一道文爲
運機將相一體相爲握竒
聖天子則權衡將相而無爲張弛
文武而不諄者也今請與諸
士子論文武一道昔者周吕
鷹揚制禮作樂反亂致治伊
punctuated:
爛，巍巍峩峩。世人僉曰：「人文宣朗，光昭萬世，竝曜隆古。」曷知元涵貞育，洪權荒輿，咸我聖天子大造縕融，玄德廣運。日月星辰，天末光也；山川喬嶽，地余章也。於微見著，因流遡源，緊其闡之，益以渾淪矣。夫文人武士，竝禎王國；文眀武赫，混於一初。故文武一道，文爲運機；將相一體，相爲握竒。聖天子則權衡將相而無爲，張弛文武而不諄者也。

今請與諸士子論文武一道。昔者周吕鷹揚，制禮作樂，反亂致治；伊
translation_en:
…resplendent, lofty and towering. People all say: “Civil culture shines forth brightly, illuminating ten thousand generations and matching the splendor of high antiquity.” How could they know that the all-embracing nurture of primordial and steadfast powers, and the mighty authority extending over the vast realm [?], all derive from our sagely Son of Heaven’s great creative work, its accumulated harmony, and the far-reaching operation of his profound virtue? The sun, moon, and stars are but Heaven’s incidental radiance; mountains, rivers, and lofty peaks are but Earth’s remaining adornment. Through the minute we perceive the manifest; following the stream, we trace its source. Pressing its elucidation further [?], we find it ever more an undivided whole. Men of letters and warriors alike bring blessings to the royal realm; civil brilliance and martial splendor merge in a single origin. Thus civil and military affairs constitute one Way, with the civil serving as the mechanism that sets it in motion. Generals and chief ministers form one body, with the chief minister holding the key to extraordinary strategy. The sagely Son of Heaven balances generals and chief ministers while acting without contrivance, tightening and relaxing civil and military measures without repeated exhortation.

Now let me discuss with you candidates how civil and military affairs constitute one Way. In former times, Zhou and Lü soared like eagles, established rites and made music, and turned disorder into good government; Yi…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
虺放伐封禮覆暴歸作一德
厥後蕭何奮沛守關發蹤指
示定章立灋孰將孰相原始
未分它如項王關羽武力無
倫項王悲歌拔山蓋世其辭
丕雄關羽表心如日在天其
論不正張巡岳飛英勇冠絕
===
文思飛騰若吾夫子拓關却
萊開闔文武何暇列其大成
揆茲以揚於前合一以論於
後二之則裂矣得其一則弱
矣姑且言藝出入墳典者正
也搜玄發幽者奇也旁獵曲
暢者揚也含英蘊腴者備也
punctuated: 虺放伐，封禮覆暴，歸作一德。厥後蕭何奮沛守關，發蹤指示，定章立灋，孰將孰相？原始未分。它如項王、關羽，武力無倫。項王悲歌拔山蓋世，其辭丕雄；關羽表心如日在天，其論不正？張巡、岳飛，英勇冠絕，文思飛騰。若吾夫子拓關却萊，開闔文武，何暇列其大成？揆茲以揚於前，合一以論於後，二之則裂矣，得其一則弱矣。姑且言藝：出入墳典者正也，搜玄發幽者奇也，旁獵曲暢者揚也，含英蘊腴者備也。
translation_en: …Hui, through banishment and punitive conquest, establishing ritual [?] and overthrowing tyranny, ultimately acted with a single virtue. Later, Xiao He rose in Pei and guarded the passes, tracing the quarry and directing the pursuit, establishing regulations and instituting laws. Which was the general, and which the chief minister? At their origin, these roles were not divided. Others, such as King Xiang and Guan Yu, possessed martial strength without equal. King Xiang sang mournfully of uprooting mountains and overshadowing the age: how mighty his words! Guan Yu declared his heart to be like the sun in heaven: was his reasoning not upright? Zhang Xun and Yue Fei were unsurpassed in courage, and their literary imagination soared. As for our Master, who lifted a gateway bar and repelled the men of Lai, freely deploying civil and martial capacities, how could there be time to enumerate his consummate achievements? Considering these examples set forth above and discussing them together below, to divide the civil and martial into two is to rend them apart; to possess only one is to be weak. Let us speak for the moment of literary accomplishment: moving freely through the ancient canonical writings constitutes the orthodox; searching out mysteries and bringing hidden meanings to light constitutes the extraordinary; ranging widely and fully developing every subtlety constitutes expansiveness; holding blossoms within and storing richness constitutes completeness.

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
演遺起弱者伏也昔云觀劔
而契於書古人以射而正其
學桑弧蓬矢以志四方道胡
有二學豈可偏以今
聖天子神烈遠揚武不以兵兵不
以戰日南醜酋聞且褫魄方
圖納款修貢我以緩兵爲權
===
彼以轉危爲福天下永享雍
熈矣諸士子相與優游翰墨
曷其弗可惟崇武生變弛武
啓侮况吉囊猖獗不忘備禦
諸士子今日以文進者以武
顯方將獻策
天朝志滅胡虜守其正則紛紜不
punctuated: 演遺起弱者，伏也。昔云觀劔而契於書，古人以射而正其學。桑弧蓬矢，以志四方。道胡有二？學豈可偏？以今聖天子神烈遠揚，武不以兵，兵不以戰。日南醜酋聞且褫魄，方圖納款修貢。我以緩兵爲權，彼以轉危爲福，天下永享雍熈矣。諸士子相與優游翰墨，曷其弗可？惟崇武生變，弛武啓侮。况吉囊猖獗，不忘備禦。諸士子今日以文進者，以武顯，方將獻策天朝，志滅胡虜。守其正，則紛紜不
translation_en: …To develop what has been overlooked and invigorate what is weak [?] is to deploy an ambush. It was said of old that watching swordplay brought insight into calligraphy; the ancients used archery to rectify their learning. A mulberry bow and arrows of fleabane expressed aspirations toward the four quarters. How could the Way be twofold? How could learning be one-sided? Now the awe-inspiring achievements of our sage Son of Heaven spread far abroad: martial power requires no resort to arms, and arms require no resort to battle. The vile chieftain of Rinan hears of them and loses his nerve; he is now planning to pledge allegiance and present tribute. We employ postponement of military action as an expedient; he regards deliverance from peril as a blessing. All under Heaven will forever enjoy harmony and prosperity. Why should the examination candidates not together take their ease among brush and ink? Yet exalting martial pursuits breeds upheaval, while neglecting military preparedness invites affronts. Moreover, with Ji Nang running rampant, defensive preparations must not be forgotten. You candidates who advance today through literary accomplishments will distinguish yourselves through martial achievements. You will offer policy proposals to the imperial court, aspiring to destroy the northern foes. If you adhere to orthodox methods, then amid turmoil you will not …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
亂出其奇則跳盪橫衝張其
揚則鴈行以翼設其備則魚
麗以待發其伏則節短而應
疾取勝於無窮或乃神機默
筭本畧運韜凌軋孫吳邁紹
周呂豈其無人疇昔將入簾
之夕夜夢巨蛇化為龍余持
===
矛刺之未能旦且與諸君子
言之其祥非幻夫蛇陰類也
主武龍陽類也主文蛇化為
龍兵滅而庶蕃文昭而武泯
之象諸士子中能無兼文武
如方叔召虎者出而張文翕
武哉夫文武不一謂之偏張
punctuated: 亂；出其奇，則跳盪橫衝；張其揚，則鴈行以翼；設其備，則魚麗以待；發其伏，則節短而應疾，取勝於無窮。或乃神機默筭，本畧運韜，凌軋孫吳，邁紹周呂，豈其無人？疇昔將入簾之夕，夜夢巨蛇化為龍，余持矛刺之，未能。旦且與諸君子言之，其祥非幻。夫蛇，陰類也，主武；龍，陽類也，主文。蛇化為龍，兵滅而庶蕃，文昭而武泯之象。諸士子中，能無兼文武如方叔、召虎者，出而張文翕武哉？夫文武不一，謂之偏。張
translation_en:
…disordered; when employing surprise tactics, they charge and strike across the field. When deploying their forces [?], they extend their wings in a wild-goose formation; when preparing their defenses, they await the enemy in a fish-scale formation. When springing an ambush, their timing is tight and their response swift, securing victory through inexhaustible variations. There may indeed be men whose inspired calculations are made in silence, who ground themselves in strategy and employ the arts of war, surpassing Sun Wu and Wu Qi and carrying forward—even exceeding—the achievements of the Duke of Zhou and Lü Shang. Could there be no such men?
On the evening before I was to enter the examiners’ enclosure, I dreamed that a giant snake transformed into a dragon. I took a spear and tried to stab it, but could not. At dawn I spoke of this to the gentlemen present: its portent was no illusion. The snake belongs to yin and presides over martial affairs; the dragon belongs to yang and presides over civil affairs. A snake transforming into a dragon signifies the cessation of warfare and the flourishing of the populace, the splendor of civil culture and the disappearance of armed conflict. Among these examination candidates, surely there will emerge men who combine civil and martial accomplishments, like Fang Shu and Shao Hu, to promote civil culture and bring arms to rest! For when civil and martial accomplishments are not united, this is called being one-sided. As for tightening…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
弛不宜謂之塞偏與塞豈以
望於諸子余恐薪者之鹿爲
夢而匪眞余之龍爲眞而匪
夢而誰復能分之者其以獻
之
天朝而瑞世噫龍哉士哉將迎
聖天子之運承天行以光大配地
===
道而含貞者也
直隸松江府華亭縣儒學訓
導郭愷謹序
punctuated:
弛不宜，謂之塞。偏與塞，豈以望於諸子？余恐薪者之鹿爲夢而匪眞，余之龍爲眞而匪夢，而誰復能分之者？其以獻之天朝而瑞世。噫，龍哉！士哉！將迎聖天子之運，承天行以光大，配地道而含貞者也。
直隸松江府華亭縣儒學訓導郭愷謹序。
translation_en:
…and relaxation are ill-timed, this is called obstruction. Could imbalance and obstruction be what I expect of you gentlemen? I fear that the woodcutter’s deer was a dream rather than reality, while my dragon is reality rather than a dream. Yet who can distinguish between them anymore? May you offer this auspicious sign to the imperial court and bring good omens to the age. Ah, dragons! Ah, scholars! You shall welcome the auspicious course of the sage Son of Heaven’s reign, follow Heaven’s movement in its radiance and greatness, and accord with Earth’s Way in embracing steadfastness.
Respectfully prefaced by Guo Kai, Instructor in the Confucian School of Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region.

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
廣東鄉試錄序
聖皇帝文涵武蕩海徼內外戎夷
咸知向學矧嶺以南乃寰宇
中州歲丁酉廣東如期舉試
維時巡按監察御史余光恭
先厥事曁提調官左布政使
陸杰左參議余鋔監試官按
===
察使蔣淦副使鄒守愚與先
巡按監察御史陳大用以禮
聘考試官學正王本才訓導
郭愷同考試官學正黃仲陽
敎諭蔣孟倫林人紀陳玉郝
光潤王蘭矢心入院恪供乃
務維時右布政使柴經左參
punctuated:
廣東鄉試錄序

聖皇帝文涵武蕩，海徼內外戎夷咸知向學，矧嶺以南，乃寰宇中州。歲丁酉，廣東如期舉試。維時，巡按監察御史余光恭先厥事，曁提調官左布政使陸杰、左參議余鋔、監試官按察使蔣淦、副使鄒守愚，與先巡按監察御史陳大用，以禮聘考試官學正王本才、訓導郭愷，同考試官學正黃仲陽、敎諭蔣孟倫、林人紀、陳玉、郝光潤、王蘭，矢心入院，恪供乃務。維時，右布政使柴經、左參
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guangdong Provincial Examination
