Our sage emperor nurtures through civil virtue and pacifies through martial power. The Rong and Yi peoples within and beyond the maritime frontiers all know to turn toward learning; how much more so the lands south of the Ling mountains, a central region of the realm. In the dingyou year [1537], Guangdong held its examination as scheduled. At that time, the Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Yu Guang, respectfully took the preliminary arrangements in hand. Together with the Proctors, Left Administration Commissioner Lu Jie and Assistant Administration Commissioner of the Left Yu Wan; the Examination Monitors, Surveillance Commissioner Jiang Gan and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zou Shouyu; and the former Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Chen Dayong, he ceremoniously invited Instructor Wang Bencai and Assistant Instructor Guo Kai to serve as Examiners, and Instructor Huang Zhongyang and Instructors Jiang Menglun, Lin Renji, Chen Yu, Hao Guangrun, and Wang Lan to serve as Associate Examiners. They entered the examination compound with firm resolve and conscientiously discharged their duties. At that time, Right Administration Commissioner Chai Jing and the Left Vice …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
政詹瀚右參政朱珮右參議
盧蕙副使顧可久葉照僉事
吳玭江匯朱道瀾周相李默
相與畫謨作範殫思獻藝維
時提督兩廣軍務兼理巡撫
兵部左侍郎兼右副都御史
潘旦提督南贛汀漳等處軍
===
務右副都御史王浚昭謀備
典總兵安遠侯柳珣協寅觀
成禮科右給事中沈伯咸湖
廣道監察御史毛復恤刑郎
中鄭朝輔咸諮度定規都指
揮潘璵張輗李讓咸賛翼防
範合提學僉事吳鵬所選士
punctuated: 政詹瀚、右參政朱珮、右參議盧蕙、副使顧可久、葉照、僉事吳玭、江匯、朱道瀾、周相、李默，相與畫謨作範，殫思獻藝。維時，提督兩廣軍務兼理巡撫、兵部左侍郎兼右副都御史潘旦，提督南贛汀漳等處軍務、右副都御史王浚，昭謀備典；總兵安遠侯柳珣，協寅觀成；禮科右給事中沈伯咸、湖廣道監察御史毛復、恤刑郎中鄭朝輔，咸諮度定規；都指揮潘璵、張輗、李讓，咸賛翼防範。合提學僉事吳鵬所選士
translation_en:
…Left Administration Vice Commissioner Zhan Han, Right Administration Vice Commissioner Zhu Pei, Right Administration Assistant Commissioner Lu Hui, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Gu Kejiu and Ye Zhao, and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Wu Pin, Jiang Hui, Zhu Daolan, Zhou Xiang, and Li Mo together devised plans and established procedures, devoting their utmost thought and contributing their expertise.

At this time, Pan Dan, superintendent of military affairs in Guangdong and Guangxi concurrently administering the duties of grand coordinator, Left Vice Minister of War and concurrently Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, and Wang Jun, superintendent of military affairs in Nan’an, Ganzhou, Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and other places and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, clarified the plans and made the prescribed arrangements complete. Liu Xun, regional commander and Marquis of Anyuan, cooperated respectfully and witnessed the successful accomplishment of the undertaking. Shen Boxian, Right Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Rites; Mao Fu, Investigating Censor for the Huguang Circuit; and Zheng Chaofu, bureau director assigned to review criminal sentences, all consulted and deliberated to establish regulations. Chief Military Commissioners Pan Yu, Zhang Ni, and Li Rang all assisted with security and precautions. Bringing together the candidates selected by Wu Peng, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner for Education…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
之九卿分理中之邦伯司牧
外之將帥分閫文武幷效纖
洪畢陳洋洋乎聖謨帝懿彬
彬乎鳳翥麟遊猗歟盛哉或
曰雄論無稽彌文不實言寓
莊周談空鄒衍以科取人無
乃摭華棄腴予應之曰官先
===
事士先志志以論士言以發
志典曰敷奏以言非乎世非
洪龐人非淳古是故求賢良
則深情進矣求隱逸則偽遜
至矣求多途則私門啓矣是
廣虛名而蔽實德乃覬進者
之要津也况非豪傑所樂趨
punctuated: 之九卿分理中之邦，伯司牧外之將帥分閫，文武幷效，纖洪畢陳。洋洋乎聖謨帝懿，彬彬乎鳳翥麟遊，猗歟盛哉！或曰：「雄論無稽，彌文不實，言寓莊周，談空鄒衍，以科取人，無乃摭華棄腴？」予應之曰：「官先事，士先志，志以論士，言以發志。《典》曰：『敷奏以言。』非乎？世非洪龐，人非淳古，是故求賢良，則深情進矣；求隱逸，則偽遜至矣；求多途，則私門啓矣。是廣虛名而蔽實德，乃覬進者之要津也，况非豪傑所樂趨
translation_en:
…the Nine Ministers divide responsibility for governing the realm at the center; regional chiefs oversee those beyond it, and military commanders exercise authority in their assigned territories [?]. Civil and military officials alike render service, and their contributions, small and great, are all displayed. How vast the sage’s counsels and the emperor’s noble achievements! How splendid, like phoenixes soaring and qilin roaming! Ah, what flourishing greatness!

Someone may say: “Grand arguments lack substantiation; elaborate writing lacks substance. Their words are allegories like Zhuang Zhou’s, their discussions empty speculation like Zou Yan’s. In selecting men through examinations, are we not gathering blossoms and discarding the rich substance?”

I reply: “For officials, duties come first; for scholars, aspirations come first. Aspirations are the basis for judging scholars, and words express aspirations. Does not the Canon say, ‘Let them fully present their statements in words’? Our age lacks primordial simplicity, and people lack the purity of antiquity. Thus, seek the worthy and good, and men with concealed motives advance; seek recluses, and those feigning modest withdrawal arrive; seek men through many channels, and doors to private patronage open. This magnifies empty reputations and obscures genuine virtue: it becomes a crucial avenue for those coveting advancement. Moreover, it is hardly what outstanding men gladly pursue…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
乎故謂藝文不能觀人者妄
也謂科目不能盡士者迂也
惟額於數不竝一時終無留
良矣惟執事者秉公司衡者
深識務窮正學以貢於澤宮
爾乃相與告誡於百執事曰
聖天子在上賢公卿在下三年一
===
比士類淹期庸弗慎乎得人
以應社稷攸倚庸弗精乎分
經校藝者毋眩浮獵毋奪鉤
玄則真才得矣監臨提調者
嚴憲肅令協恭和衷則大典
成矣登明以選錄士以應乃
擇日會讌讌畢進之曰嶺以
punctuated:
乎？故謂藝文不能觀人者，妄也；謂科目不能盡士者，迂也。惟額於數，不竝一時，終無留良矣。惟執事者秉公，司衡者深識，務窮正學，以貢於澤宮。
爾乃相與告誡於百執事曰：「聖天子在上，賢公卿在下，三年一比，士類淹期，庸弗慎乎？得人以應，社稷攸倚，庸弗精乎？分經校藝者，毋眩浮獵，毋奪鉤玄，則真才得矣；監臨提調者，嚴憲肅令，協恭和衷，則大典成矣。」
登明以選，錄士以應。乃擇日會讌，讌畢進之曰：「嶺以
translation_en:
…? Thus, to say that literary compositions cannot reveal a person's character is unfounded; to say that the examination system cannot encompass all worthy scholars is misguided. Only because numbers are limited by a quota can they not all be selected at once; in the end, no worthy man will remain overlooked. Those conducting the examination need only act impartially, and those weighing candidates' merits possess discerning judgment, striving to probe their orthodox learning fully before presenting them at the Palace of Selection (Zegong).
Then we jointly admonished all those charged with duties: “The sage Son of Heaven is above, and worthy dukes and ministers are below. The examination is held once every three years, and scholars must wait a long time for their opportunity: how could we fail to exercise care? Securing men to answer the call is what the altars of soil and grain—the state itself—depend upon: how could we fail to exercise discernment? Those assigned to the several Classics to assess compositions must not be dazzled by superficial gleanings of learning, nor slight the probing of profound meaning; then true talent will be found. The Supervising Official and Proctors must enforce regulations strictly and uphold orders rigorously, working together with respect and a common purpose; then this great ceremony will be accomplished.”
Men of evident worth were advanced for selection, and scholars were enrolled in answer to the call. A day was then chosen for a banquet. When it was over, we brought them forward and said: “South of the Ling mountains …

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
南雖在遐荒入漢卽爲名郡
烈士竒節學士雄文卑俯衡
廬潤吞滄溟無論漢宋且評
本朝如丘文莊之經濟陳白沙
之清脩倫迂岡之純懿皆名
諸天下亶非濶論諸士子鍾
竒而力學際時而奮庸近儷
===
諸公遠匹於古者志也進退
以禮窮達罔變者毅也困而
裕如亨而兼善者弘也若騁
藝徼惠而棄其所學爾士子
其自顛隕以疚乃心若別求
往哲以無負明世廓之以配
于天地厥亦自余爾多士其
punctuated: 南雖在遐荒，入漢卽爲名郡。烈士竒節，學士雄文，卑俯衡廬，潤吞滄溟。無論漢宋，且評本朝，如丘文莊之經濟、陳白沙之清脩、倫迂岡之純懿，皆名諸天下，亶非濶論。諸士子鍾竒而力學，際時而奮庸，近儷諸公，遠匹於古者，志也；進退以禮，窮達罔變者，毅也；困而裕如，亨而兼善者，弘也。若騁藝徼惠而棄其所學，爾士子其自顛隕以疚乃心。若別求往哲以無負明世，廓之以配于天地，厥亦自余。爾多士其
translation_en:
…south of the Ling mountains, though situated in the distant wilderness, became a renowned commandery upon its incorporation into the Han realm. Its men of resolve displayed extraordinary integrity, and its scholars produced magnificent writings, making Mounts Heng and Lu bow low and engulfing the vast ocean in their richness [?]. Leaving aside the Han and Song, consider our own dynasty: the statecraft of Qiu Wenzhuang, the pure cultivation of Chen Baisha, and the unalloyed virtue of Lun Yugang are all renowned throughout the realm. These are certainly no empty generalities.

You scholars, endowed with exceptional gifts, should study diligently, seize the opportunities of your age, and exert yourselves in service. To equal these gentlemen of recent times and match the ancients of the distant past is ambition; to advance and withdraw according to ritual propriety, remaining unchanged in adversity or success, is fortitude; to remain at ease in hardship and extend goodness to others when prospering is magnanimity. If you flaunt your literary skills to solicit favor and abandon what you have learned, you scholars will bring about your own downfall and burden your consciences. If instead you seek the worthies of the past as your models, so as not to fail this enlightened age, and expand your capacities to match Heaven and Earth, that too begins with me [?]. You many scholars, may you…

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
毋以余爲寙言哉
浙江湖州府安吉州儒學學
正王本才謹序
punctuated:
毋以余爲寙言哉！

浙江湖州府安吉州儒學學正王本才謹序。
translation_en:
…do not regard what I have said as idle words [?]!

This preface was respectfully composed by Wang Bencai, Instructor at the Confucian School of Anji Department, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang.

title: 嘉靖十六年廣東鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
固天縱之將聖又多能也
馬拯
同考試官教諭陳批脫化題目以錯綜成文實不越
於矩度用以式士作之範
同考試官教諭林批子貢能言聖人之蘊此作能發
子貢之言
考試官訓導郭批子亦善言聖者
===
考試官學正王批變合雄渾
天裕聖人以大德而麗之以藝者也夫天生聖
人以統道也縱之聖以為統而多藝能盡其大
哉太宰不知聖故以多能與夫子子貢告之曰
退藏於密而不見其有者聖人之分智周萬物
而時見其能者聖人之餘夫天篤聖人上焉賴
以成天地之能下焉賴以定民物之志重其任
而薄其德則弗勝也豊其責而嗇其才則弗舉
也故定其命以為固而莫為之回縱其質以為
punctuated:
第壹場
四書
「固天縱之將聖，又多能也。」
馬拯
同考試官教諭陳批：脫化題目，以錯綜成文，實不越於矩度，用以式士作之範。
同考試官教諭林批：子貢能言聖人之蘊，此作能發子貢之言。
考試官訓導郭批：子亦善言聖者。
考試官學正王批：變合雄渾。
天裕聖人以大德，而麗之以藝者也。夫天生聖人以統道也，縱之聖以為統，而多藝能盡其大哉？太宰不知聖，故以多能與夫子。子貢告之曰：「退藏於密而不見其有者，聖人之分；智周萬物而時見其能者，聖人之餘。夫天篤聖人，上焉賴以成天地之能，下焉賴以定民物之志。重其任而薄其德，則弗勝也；豊其責而嗇其才，則弗舉也。故定其命以為固，而莫為之回；縱其質以為

“Surely Heaven has endowed him to be a great sage; he is also skilled in many things.”
Ma Zheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: He transforms the topic and interweaves its elements into an essay, without ever exceeding the proper bounds. It may serve as a model for candidates’ compositions.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: Zigong could articulate the sage’s inner riches; this composition can elucidate Zigong’s words.

Comment by Examiner Guo, Assistant Instructor: You too are skilled at speaking of the sage.

Comment by Examiner Wang, Instructor: Its variations and integration are powerful and full-bodied.

Heaven enriches the sage with great virtue and adorns him with accomplishments. Heaven brings forth the sage to bring the Way together into a unified whole. It endows him with sageliness so that he may do so; could his many accomplishments encompass his greatness? The Grand Steward did not understand sageliness, and therefore credited the Master with skill in many things. Zigong told him:

“What withdraws into hidden depths without displaying its possessions is the sage’s essential portion; what comprehends the myriad things in its wisdom and at times displays its abilities is the sage’s surplus. Heaven indeed richly endows the sage. Above, it relies on him to fulfill the capacities of Heaven and Earth; below, it relies on him to settle the aspirations of the people and all things. Were it to make his charge weighty but his virtue meager, he could not bear it; were it to make his responsibilities abundant but stint his talents, he could not discharge them. Thus it establishes his mandate firmly, so that nothing can turn it aside, and gives free scope to his innate nature so as to make it …

text:
自古以來征北者有功征南者無功乃往
鑒也寧弗審乎生愚以爲武不可弛兵有
所先莫先吉囊夫吉囊可容而弗誅生靈
寧忍而不救乎夷狄可禦而弗窮中國寧
坐敝而不戰乎故戰則守有餘備則守不
足吾非爲攻之戰來則戰以破之張克伐
之威以奪其魄戰以止戰將不有宣王之
薄伐耶胡曰役中國以事夷也又以爲權
有所設變有所圖莫貴於處安南夫安南
===
可緩而弗征可聽其負固而不庭乎安南
必征而弗宥可忍驅赤子以罹瘴乎故撫
則享來王之福戰則有角勝之形吾不爲
棄之弱來則柔以懷之握制夷之道以制
其柄征以無征將不有大舜之來格耶胡
曰棄明德以爭利也夫順天者昌得人者
勝故王者奉天行伐霸者假義興師是以
有成烈且犁庭於漠北者其勢險養寇於
門庭者其禍危今吉囊猖獗不犁其庭寧
punctuated:
自古以來，征北者有功，征南者無功，乃往鑒也，寧弗審乎？生愚以爲，武不可弛，兵有所先，莫先吉囊。夫吉囊可容而弗誅，生靈寧忍而不救乎？夷狄可禦而弗窮，中國寧坐敝而不戰乎？故戰則守有餘，備則守不足。吾非爲攻之戰，來則戰以破之，張克伐之威以奪其魄，戰以止戰，將不有宣王之薄伐耶？胡曰役中國以事夷也？
又以爲，權有所設，變有所圖，莫貴於處安南。夫安南可緩而弗征，可聽其負固而不庭乎？安南必征而弗宥，可忍驅赤子以罹瘴乎？故撫則享來王之福，戰則有角勝之形。吾不爲棄之弱，來則柔以懷之，握制夷之道以制其柄，征以無征，將不有大舜之來格耶？胡曰棄明德以爭利也？

translation_en:
Since ancient times, campaigns to the north have achieved success, while campaigns to the south have achieved none. This is a lesson from the past: should we not examine it carefully? In my humble judgment as a student, military preparedness must not be relaxed. Military action has its priorities, and none takes precedence over Ji Nang. If Ji Nang may be tolerated and left unpunished, can we bear to leave the people without rescue? If the barbarians may merely be repelled without being pursued to exhaustion, can the Central Kingdom sit by and exhaust itself without fighting? Thus, fighting makes defense more than adequate, whereas merely taking precautions leaves defense inadequate. I do not advocate war for conquest. When they come, fight and defeat them; display the might of punitive conquest to strike terror into them. By fighting to end fighting, might we not achieve something like King Xuan’s limited punitive expedition? How can this be called burdening the Central Kingdom in service to the barbarians?
I further hold that expedients must be devised and responses to changing circumstances planned; nothing is more important than dealing properly with Annan. If action against Annan may be delayed and no campaign launched, can we allow it to rely on its strong defenses and refuse to attend court? If Annan must be attacked and cannot be pardoned, can we bear to drive our innocent people into pestilential miasmas? Thus, pacification brings the blessing of their coming to acknowledge royal authority, whereas warfare creates a contest for victory. I do not advocate the weakness of abandoning them. When they come, treat them gently to win their allegiance; grasp the means of controlling the barbarians so as to hold the reins of power over them. Conduct a campaign so that no campaign is needed: might we not achieve something like their coming in submission to the great Shun? How can this be called abandoning luminous virtue to contend for profit?
Those who accord with Heaven flourish; those who win the people prevail. Hence true kings undertake punitive campaigns in obedience to Heaven, while hegemons invoke righteousness to raise armies. Through this they achieve their accomplishments. Yet to plow up the enemy’s encampments north of the desert entails a perilous strategic position; to nurture bandits at one’s own doorstep entails grave danger. Now Ji Nang runs rampant. text:
染日用所見聞罔非軌範之示則觀感啓
進脩之益鼓舞寓丕變之機治化彰而氣
化亦還矣故曰化民成俗其必由學乎握
其機而任其責者非執事其孰圖之
punctuated: 染，日用所見聞，罔非軌範之示，則觀感啓進脩之益，鼓舞寓丕變之機，治化彰而氣化亦還矣。故曰：「化民成俗，其必由學乎！」握其機而任其責者，非執事，其孰圖之？
translation_en: …imbued with these influences, everything they see and hear in daily life exemplifies proper standards. Learning through observation awakens the benefits of advancement in self-cultivation, while encouragement holds the potential for profound change. The transforming influence of government thus becomes manifest, and the transforming processes of vital force (qi) are likewise restored. Hence the saying: “To transform the people and establish good customs, must one not proceed through learning?” Who but you, sir, can undertake this, grasping the opportunity and bearing the responsibility?
